# Metis front-end, plan B: the application shell and screen 24 (project overview) running in the browser for the product owner to review

> **For the implementing agent:** you MUST use the skill `superpowers:subagent-driven-development`
> (recommended) or `superpowers:executing-plans` to run this plan task by task.
> Each step is a checkbox `- [ ]`.

**Goal:** from the base of plan A, build the application shell (sidebar, top bar, project header,
the generic "not built yet" page) and screen 24 (project overview) running in the browser from 1280 px up,
in English and Vietnamese, with mock data for Meridian CGI Campaign and Northwind Showroom VR,
every state of the screen viewable through mock scenarios on the route, reaching the code level of spec section 9; the app
also opens on the iOS Simulator and the Android Emulator (trial run only). The last step hands the product
owner one `pnpm web` command that opens screen 24 of Meridian directly.

**Architecture:** one Expo app, the code areas keep the boundary rules of spec 3.2. `src/core/` adds the route
table, the zod contract of the shell and its client; `src/screens/24-project-overview/` has a pure TypeScript
`model.ts` that turns API data into what the screen draws (every text translated, every number
formatted, every link built), so the component only draws. Styles are written in `*.styles.ts` next to each
component, only with tokens generated from `brand/tokens.css`; the lint rule catches every number, every color code, every
calculation written directly. The MSW mock server runs in a service worker on the web and through a `fetch` wrapper on
the app, only when `EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS=1`; the release build does not carry it, and a script proves it.

## Global constraints

Every task is bound by the constraints below; the values are copied from the spec and from the gates of plan A.

- One app `apps/metis`; no multi-package workspace, no path aliases (spec 3.1).
- Boundaries (spec 3.2): `src/core/` and every `model.ts` (together with its `model.<name>.ts` parts)
  do not import `react`, `react-native`, `src/design-system/`, `src/platform/`, `src/shell/`,
  `src/screens/`, `src/mocks/`, and do not use `window`, `document`, `localStorage`;
  `src/design-system/` does not import `src/core/i18n`, `src/platform/`, `src/shell/`,
  `src/screens/`, `src/mocks/`; one screen does not import another; `src/mocks/` is imported only by `src/platform/`
  and by tests.
- `brand/tokens.css` is the only source of the shape and color numbers; `src/design-system/tokens.ts` is only
  generated by `pnpm gen:tokens`, never edited by hand (spec 5.1).
- No number, no color code, no calculation written directly in a style for size, spacing, corner radius,
  font size, line height, letter spacing, color; a size that is needed is a token of its own (R-B13). The only exceptions are two
  kinds from spec 7 (the intrinsic size of a drawing, the minimum width of a table column), each place has
  `// token-exception: <reason>` on the line right above. Does not apply to unitless properties (`flex`,
  `flexGrow`, `opacity`, `zIndex`, `aspectRatio`) and a border of 1.
- Styles live only in a `*.styles.ts` file next to the component (`StyleSheet.create`, tokens only); other
  files do not import `StyleSheet` and do not write an object in a `style` or `*Style` property
  (R-B14). Three token groups are used only through their own component: the focus ring, the seven status color groups (through
  `src/design-system/status.ts`), the chart palette (through the chart component) (spec 5.1).
- Every displayed text goes through the typed dictionary of the shell or of the screen; design system components receive
  all text through required props, with no default text (spec 5.5). User content (project names,
  people's names, Category names) is shown as is.
- The screen does not count or add up rows by itself; every number is a snapshot from the server; drill-down filters are taken
  as is from the server (spec 3.3, 4.3).
- Percentages round down to a whole number: 99,5% shows 99% (FE-20). Dates and times are strings printed by `Intl`,
  English `en-GB` prints "Sept" (R-B6).
- Coverage 100% of lines, branches, functions, statements; mutation testing threshold 100%; Knip clean, except the debt
  list, which may only be shortened (spec 9.1, plan A).
- Tests that render React Native are named `*.test.native.tsx` (or `.ts`) and run in the iOS and
  Android projects of Jest; pure modules keep `*.test.ts`, which run in the four projects; `*.test.web.ts` run in the
  Web project (R-B5, R-B16). No source file `*.web.tsx` or `*.native.tsx`; only `*.web.ts`, which the Jest
  Web project can cover.
- Tests do not call code of `src/` at the top of the file (apart from `test`, `beforeEach`): Stryker treats every
  mutant that runs at file load time as a static mutant and reruns the whole test suite for each one (measured in the
  Evidence section).
- Each gate is a command `pnpm gate:<name>`; `pnpm verify` runs every `gate:*` in declaration order
  (spec 9.3).
- Review browsers: Playwright's Chromium and WebKit, width from 1280 px (R-B1); narrower widths
  and phones belong to plan C.
- Comments in code are written in Vietnamese (except `brand/tokens.css`, a brand file, which stays in English
  like the part that already exists); names of functions, variables, files are written in English. The Vietnamese text
  in the dictionary is a draft by the code writer, which the product owner reviews when reviewing the screen (spec 5.5).
- No long dash characters (em dash, en dash) anywhere.
- The implementer does not run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, `git init`; the last step of each task
  lists the files changed and then stops. Committing is the product owner's job (FE-19, FE-21).
- Every command runs from the app folder `apps/metis`, unless a step says otherwise. `REPO` is the repo root.
- Before running the gates at the end of each task, run `pnpm exec prettier --write .` once.
- After each task, every gate that exists up to that task must be green. The full-gate `pnpm verify` command runs at the last step
  of Task 1, 3, 13, 14, 15 and 16; the other tasks run the gates named in the task.
- Package install commands, `expo export`, `msw init` get `< /dev/null` added so that no command waits for a question.
- A bare `diff A B` through the RTK hook can print `[ok] Files are identical` even when the two files differ (plan
  A, section The real run); every exact-match comparison uses `cmp` or `shasum`.

## Places that need close checking

Five kinds of input that the spec implies but that easily slip past the main tests, ordered by how likely they are to make the product
owner stumble during review. Each line has a test that pins it, in the task that owns that code.

1. **Vietnamese text longer than English in fixed-size frames** (sidebar 232 px, metric tile
   112,8 px wide at 1280 px; the Vietnamese labels "Workspace dashboard", "Delayed vs baseline", "Deliverables"):
   no horizontal scrolling, the sidebar keeps 232, tiles do not overlap, text wraps instead of being cut. Pinned in
   Task 14 (layout measurement in both languages at 1280 and 1440) and Task 12 (the metric tile lets text
   wrap, no `numberOfLines` set).
2. **Edge-case figures:** the number 0 (the sub-line is not shown, the bar segment is not drawn), the number 1 (English singular
   form), no baseline yet, everyone has 0 open items, empty list, list with more items, numbers in the
   thousands (`2,000` and `2.000`). Pinned in Task 10 (the test table of `model.ts`) and Task 12 (the
   "Not baselined" tile draws text instead of a number).
3. **The server returns an error or data of the wrong shape:** 401, 403, 404, 500, network loss, timeout, missing
   field. The screen shows exactly one named state, a sentence saying why, a button to go on; never a blank
   page or the text `undefined`. Pinned in Task 10 (`problemOf` for each kind of error), Task 12 (the component
   test of each state) and Task 14 (browser scenarios with axe).
4. **Unusual routes:** a project code that does not exist, a project of another workspace (Digital Products), a mistyped route,
   an unknown `?mock=` scenario, `?scope=MINE`. The screen shows "Project not found" or the "Page not found" page
   inside the real shell, with no error in the browser console. Pinned in Task 4 (the route table,
   the filters accepted), Task 7 (`scenarioOf`), Task 12 (`scope` other than `mine` means the whole project) and Task 14
   (deep routes).
5. **Language choice after a reload, or when the browser blocks localStorage:** the text and the `lang`
   attribute are right from the first render, and when blocked it still runs in English. Pinned in Task 7 (`storage.web.ts`)
   and Task 14 (reloading the page in Vietnamese).


## Decisions made while writing the plan

Each line: what was decided, why, the price to pay if it is wrong. The twenty rulings of the controller
(R-B1 to R-B20) are binding; the product owner has said to follow the recommendations and not stop to ask (FE-21).
The D-B decisions belong to the plan writer, each with a measurement or a source.

### Rulings of the controller and how the plan applies them

- **R-B1 The scope is the review milestone in the browser.** The shell and screen 24 run on the web from 1280 px, with
  Meridian and Showroom VR data, two languages, every state viewable, reaching the code level of spec 9 (unit
  tests, 100% coverage, 100% mutation, token rules, import boundaries, dictionary check, axe on
  the web, layout measurement by token); the app opens on the iOS Simulator and the Android Emulator (Task 15, trial
  run only). Automated Safari on iPhone, Maestro, Storybook, reference images, performance numbers, the nine remaining
  reverse tests, the CI cadence and `--publish-status`, the licenses of the dev tools go to plan C.
  Why: the review may change the design, and those suites pin the design. Price: if the product owner wants
  evidence to sign off at the very first review, plan C adds it.
- **R-B2 The shell has its own contract `src/core/api/shell.ts`.** One call
  `GET {apiBase}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/shell`: the user (name, initials), tenant, workspace
  and the list of workspaces for the picker menu, three groups of sidebar items (item code, count, Planned label),
  the project tree (also the source of names for the breadcrumb), the notification count (Task 4). The label of a code lives
  in the shell dictionary, the route of a code lives in the route table; the server only chooses which items appear,
  in which order, the counts and the release label. Why: spec 3.5 only has the call for the overview screen, and
  the shell must not import `src/mocks`. Price: if the back end wants a different shape, only the shell changes; an
  as-built note for spec 3.5 and a question for the back end in the section "New questions for spec 13".
- **R-B3 Every state of the screen can be viewed through mock scenarios on the route** (`?mock=<name>`, read
  once at page load, Task 7): `loading`, `sessionExpired`, `serverError`, `invalidData`,
  `partial`, `unknown`; plus three mock projects (default, no baseline and stale data, 403) and one
  unknown project code (404). The read-only state has no field in the contract yet (spec 4.5, an open question of spec
  13), so it is not drawn. Why: the three mock projects cannot reach the remaining states. Price: one more
  scenario.
- **R-B4 "My items" writes `scope=mine` to the route,** the client sends it as a query parameter, the mock
  server returns the same data until the back end defines the filter (Task 4, 7, 12). Why: the screen
  must not filter rows by itself (spec 3.3). Price: the review sees the same figures under My items.
- **R-B5 Component tests run where they can render.** The trial run measured that RNTL renders only in the iOS and
  Android projects of Jest (Web and Node throw `Text strings must be rendered within a <Text> component`);
  pure modules run in all four. Why: measured. Price: a rendering bug that exists only on the web escapes Jest; Playwright
  on the web catches it (Task 14).
- **R-B6 Dates and times keep the rule of plan A:** the string printed by `Intl` (`en-GB` prints "Sept"); the layout
  measurement and the figures compare number to number, not month names. Price: one token in the formatter if the product owner wants
  "Sep".
- **R-B7 The "not built yet" page takes its title from the label of the destination clicked** (shell dictionary, group
  `destinations`), with the screen number from the route table, the route and the filters accepted; it does not copy
  `wireframes/manifest.json` into the app. Why: the spec allows only two generators. Price: the page has less detail
  than the manifest (no requirement code, no wireframe file path).
- **R-B8 The color `#C9C9D2` of Not Started has a token** `--neutral-fill` in `brand/tokens.css`
  (Task 1). Price: the brand owner renames the token.
- **R-B9 When the wireframe and the style guide disagree, build to the wireframe,** record each discrepancy and ask in
  spec 13: logo 24 high (68,58 wide) below the style guide's minimum of 96 px; project title 26 against
  `--fs-display` 30; the faded button in the `muted` color in `wireframe.css:128` against the style guide 0.5 changing
  to the main text color; font sizes below the floor (freshness 11,5, label 11,5, count and Planned 11, group label
  10,5); horizontal padding of list rows 14 against 16; weight 700 requested in four places, drawn as
  600. Price: changing the sizes after review.
- **R-B10 The browser tests become one gate `gate:web`** in `pnpm verify` if one
  run takes under about 90 seconds; if not, it is a separate command `pnpm check:web` and the plan says so (Task
  14 measures and then chooses, both branches have steps written in advance). Price: verify gets slower.
- **R-B11 Parallel lanes:** (a) design system; (b) platform, mock server with scenarios, placeholder
  routes; (c) dictionary and model of screen 24; then (d) shell and (e) screen 24 in parallel; then integration,
  browser tests, trial run on the app, handover. The token rule, the toolset and the shared
  contract part run first on the main tree (section "Parallel lanes"). Price: merge conflicts, resolved by hand like
  plan A. A ruling after the pre-flight of 06/10/2026 (F3) changed how it applies: (d) and (e) are not parallel;
  Task 11 and then Task 12 run on the main tree after merging (a), (b), (c), because screen 24 uses `ProjectHeader`,
  `projectHeaderOf`, `useLocale` of the shell.
- **R-B12 A UI task gives the structure, props, tokens, text and the table of tests, not the full code
  of the component;** the implementer writes the code, and the plan copies back the real code after the review. Configuration,
  scripts, test scaffolding, contracts, models, hooks, the platform layer have full code that has been run. Price: the
  implementer drifts from the wireframe; the layout measurement by token and the review catch it.
- **R-B13 The token set has every size and color that the shell and screen 24 use** (Task 1, 58 new tokens, 134 in total);
  the generator's test pins the token count; the `tokens.ts` line of the Knip debt list is dropped in the first task that
  imports it (Task 2). The rule reports calculations on tokens. Price: the brand owner renames or merges a few tokens.
- **R-B14 Styles live in `*.styles.ts` next to the component,** outside mutation testing like mock data,
  still within coverage, the token rule and the layout measurement in the browser. Lint blocks `StyleSheet` in other
  files (Task 1). Price: a style bug that the layout measurement does not measure slips through; widen the measured set.
- **R-B15 Errors that have no state of their own in spec 4.5** (`server`, `network`, `timeout`) share one
  "could not load" state with a retry button; `notFound` has the sentence "Project not found"; 401 is session
  expired, 403 is no permission, `invalid` is a shape error naming the wrong field. `ApiError` is exported
  (Task 4, 10). Price: changing the wording after review.
- **R-B16 Tests that render React Native are named `*.test.native.tsx`;** pure modules keep `*.test.ts`.
  No source files `*.web.tsx`, `*.native.tsx`. The trial run measured: `*.web.ts` has a test path through the
  Web project of Jest. Price: a platform file needs a test path of its own.
- **R-B17 Fonts on the web: six `@font-face` rules in `public/index.html`** (the latin and vietnamese blocks
  are two separate faces with `unicode-range`, files in `public/fonts/`); on iOS and Android expo-font
  loads the full-character file (written and tested, to be run on a device in plan C). Why: expo-font on the web
  writes one face per font name and drops the second block (measured: Vietnamese text falls back to Georgia). Price: adding
  one more font-loading path.
- **R-B18 Stryker runs with `timeoutMS` 30000** because tests with the router are slow (the default reported 9 of 14
  mutants of the shell as Timeout). The measurement taken while writing the plan is in the Evidence section; the machine was under
  heavy load at the time (see there). Price: verify gets slower; plan C may add incremental mutation testing.
- **R-B19 Routes follow spec 4.3** (`/w/{workspaceId}/projects/{projectId}/overview`), the root redirects
  to the overview screen of Meridian, each destination not yet built has its own placeholder route (a catch-all route
  would let a mistyped link still pass the type check), `gate:types` regenerates the route types first (Task 3, 8).
  Measured: deleting a placeholder route turns `tsc` red at the `Link` that uses it.
- **R-B20 The mock server on the web runs only when `EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS === '1'`,** from `src/platform/`;
  `pnpm web` sets that flag, so one command shows the data; the script that checks the release build proves the exported build
  has no MSW code, no strings of the mock data, no worker file (Task 3, 7). Price: one environment variable.

### Decisions of the plan writer

- **D-B1 The shared contract part runs before the lanes (Task 4):** the route table, the contract of the shell and
  its mock data, the client's additions. Why: the model of screen 24 (lane c) and the placeholder routes (lane
  b) both import them; if they live in one lane the other lane must wait. Price: one task on the main tree takes
  a few minutes longer.
- **D-B2 The token rule examines every style key in every object of `src`,** not only the argument of
  `StyleSheet.create`, and examines JSX size and color props; it reports calculations (`token * 2`, `-token`);
  it does not examine `tokens.ts` (where the numbers are set). Closes every hole of the left-over list of plan
  A: `*Style` props, spread styles, styles inside variables, the keys `flexBasis`, `translateX`,
  `translateY`, `shadowRadius`, `outlineWidth`, `outlineOffset`, `textShadowRadius`, colors joined
  by string concatenation, styles wrapped at the `create` level, numbers in comparisons flagged by mistake. Measured: 89 tests of
  the rule, 100% coverage, 66 of 66 hand-made mutants killed. Price: data with a key that has the same name as a style (such as
  `width`) in `src` must rename the key (the model uses `share`, `weight`).
- **D-B3 The names of the 58 new tokens** follow the role in `wireframe.css`: `--space-2` to `--space-18`,
  `--radius-xs`, `--radius-sm`, `--radius-pill`, fixed sizes (`--chip-h`, `--avatar`, `--logo-h`,
  ...), font sizes (`--fs-project-title`, `--fs-nav`, `--fs-crumbs`, ...), line heights in px
  (`--lh-body` 20,3 is 14 x 1,45), letter spacing, `--neutral-fill`, a negative `--badge-offset`. Price: the brand
  owner renames them.
- **D-B4 The logo is drawn with react-native-svg-transformer from a byte-for-byte copy of
  `brand/logo/metis-wordmark.svg`.** The native trial of 05/10/2026 ran this approach on iOS,
  Android and the web (needs `.svgrrc` `{"svgo": false}`: SVGO breaks this file); the trial while writing the
  plan measured on the web: 6 paths, `d` identical character by character to the source file, 68,58 x 24. Under Jest, the `.svg` file
  goes through `scripts/jest-svg.cjs` and becomes a stand-in component that records the file path and the number of paths. Price: one
  transformer for Jest.
- **D-B5 The language selector is `@react-native-picker/picker` on all three platforms:** on the web it renders the
  labelled `select` tag (measured on Chromium and WebKit), on iOS and Android it is the native picker; RNTL renders
  it in the iOS and Android projects of Jest. Price: none.
- **D-B6 The type of a link is a union per destination** (`Route` in `src/core/routes.ts`): the route
  pattern verbatim with all the `[name]` segments of the pattern; `src/core` does not import expo-router and `Link` still checks
  each pattern. Measured: a union of patterns given to `Link` is rejected by `tsc`, a union per destination is accepted,
  and a missing `projectId` is rejected. Price: none.
- **D-B7 Jest: `*.test.web.*` tests run only in the Web project; the top level of
  `jest.config.js` sets `testEnvironment: 'jest-fixed-jsdom'` for Stryker.** Measured: StrykerJS 10
  runs every project in one environment taken from the top level
  (`@stryker-mutator/jest-runner/dist/src/jest-plugins/with-coverage-analysis.js:71`), which defaults to
  node, so tests that use `localStorage`, `document`, `window` go red in the dry run; with a
  `@jest-environment` docblock in each file Stryker reports `Missing coverage results`. Stryker's time
  does not change (16 seconds both ways on `useOverview.ts`). Price: under Stryker all four projects run jsdom.
- **D-B8 The model of screen 24 is split into three files** `model.ts`, `model.lists.ts`, `model.tools.ts` because of the 300
  line cap (the one-file version is 332 lines after Prettier); the pure-TypeScript rule is extended to
  `src/**/model{,.*}.ts` (Task 10 edits `eslint.config.js`). Price: three files instead of one.
- **D-B9 The dictionaries `strings/en.ts`, `strings/vi.ts` are outside mutation testing** like the mock data of
  plan A: a mutated string is killed only by a test that copies exactly that string. They are still within
  coverage; the dictionary test pins the Vietnamese version against the source version, the model's test pins the English text,
  the browser test pins the rendered text. Price: a spelling mistake is caught only by the review.
- **D-B10 The "As of" line of the screen:** the worst freshness among the nine snapshots (order fresh, partial, stale,
  unknown), the earliest time, every definition version ("metrics v1, v2"); the text "Stale · as of ...",
  "Partial · as of ...", "Unknown · metrics v1" needs no number of days or number of missing projects, which the contract
  does not have. Price: changing the wording.
- **D-B11 The health warning strip shows when the declared level is better than the computed level** (green, amber, red); when the computed
  level is `unknown` there is no comparison. The Meridian text matches the wireframe word for word. Price: none.
- **D-B12 Metric tile:** the count sub-line shows only when the number is greater than 0 (Deliverables always has "Type =
  Deliverable"); Blocked, Delayed, High risk stand out when greater than 0 per BRD OVW-01
  (`brd/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.5.md:990`; spec line 193 emphasizes only
  Delayed and High risk; the mock data has Blocked 0 so it does not differ from the wireframe); Delayed prints a plus sign and is colored
  `criticalText` when it increases, and when there is no baseline it draws the text "Not baselined" instead of a number. Price: changing the display rule.
- **D-B13 The workload bar per person is proportional to the person with the most items** (Denny K. 100%, Nadia R.
  75%), instead of the wireframe's 16% per item (64, 48, 16, 16 at
  `wireframes/screens/24-project-overview.html:76-79`), because 16% per item overflows beyond 6 items and spec line
  198 gives no rule. Asked in spec 13. Price: the bar is longer than the wireframe.
- **D-B14 The Category bar does not draw a 0 segment** (`24-project-overview.html:65` draws a done segment
  `width:0%`, `wireframe.css:186-189` rounds the corners only of a bar with one segment, so the remaining segment is 2 px off and the
  left end square, measured on the wireframe while writing the plan). Price: 2 px off from the wireframe picture.
- **D-B15 The states of the screen:** loading (one sentence and a labelled spinner), no permission (following
  wireframe 43: an explanatory sentence, Request access, Back to My focus), not found, could not load
  (Try again), session expired (dialog), shape error (naming the field). Request access and Sign in again
  have no destination yet so they are text with a "Not built yet" label (spec 4.3 rule 3). Asked in spec 13. Price: changing when
  a destination exists.
- **D-B16 Share, Export, Help follow the rule of spec 4.3:** text with a label ("Share" and "Export" with "Not
  built yet", "Help" with "Planned V2"; spec lines 239-240), the same kind as the Planned label of
  `brand/style-guide.md:201`; the wireframe draws them as buttons (`24-project-overview.html:21`,
  `shell.js:116`, `shell.js:132`). Price: differs from the wireframe picture in three places.
- **D-B17 The language selector is at the end of the top bar** (the order of spec 4.1); the wireframe does not draw it. Price:
  moving it.
- **D-B18 On iOS and Android plan B does not store the language yet** (`src/platform/storage.ts` always opens
  in English); plan C adds AsyncStorage together with the on-device run. Why: R-B1 only does a trial run of
  the app. Price: on the app every launch is in English.
- **D-B19 Parts that exist only in the wireframe are not built:** the "WIREFRAME" strip (with the Phase, Requirements, POC line
  of `shell.js`), the tab title `Project overview · Metis wireframe`, the numbered annotation circles, the notes block
  (`24-project-overview.html:108-116`, `wireframe.css:274-281`; spec line 188 does not say to drop them).
  Price: none.
- **D-B20 Icons are text symbols like the wireframe** (component `Glyph`, hidden from screen readers;
  the symbols are at `shell.js:59-78`); choosing the 1,5 px stroke icon set is a job for plan C
  (`brand/style-guide.md:254`). Price: the symbols are drawn with the operating system's font, which differs between machines.
- **D-B21 Choosing a workspace:** the button in the sidebar opens a menu (effect `panel`) listing the workspaces of
  the contract; choosing one opens its screen 15 (`/w/{id}/dashboard`). Two mock workspaces: Creative Studio,
  Digital Products (the tree from `shell.js`). Price: the menu has no design yet.
- **D-B22 The sidebar and the top bar stay fixed, the page area scrolls;** the sidebar scrolls by itself when the screen is shorter than
  it. Why: the wireframe is a static page and says nothing (`wireframe.css:15`), and the sidebar needs about
  1037 px of height once the empty space is removed (measured on the wireframe while writing the plan). Price: none.
- **D-B23 `HOME` in `src/platform/config.ts`** (Creative Studio, Meridian) for the root route and for
  the shell of pages that do not belong to a workspace (`/me/...`, `/search`). Price: none.
- **D-B24 The wireframe's weight 700 is drawn as 600.** Measured on the wireframe while writing the plan: the screenshot
  of the letter `b` of the workspace selector (`shell.js:56`) is identical at 600, 700 and 800, 100,234375 wide;
  `wireframe.css:3` loads only Inter 400, 500, 600. Price: none.
- **D-B25 The web favicon is a byte-for-byte copy of `brand/logo/metis-favicon-48.png`;** the app icons for
  iOS and Android move to plan C: `brand/logo/` does not have the three layers that the `adaptiveIcon` of
  `apps/metis/app.json:17-22` needs (spec line 367 demands "app icon from the right file"). Price: none.
- **D-B26 `scripts/tooling.test.mjs` is fixed before adding a new tool** (the left-over list of
  plan A): a tool is a `.js`, `.cjs`, `.mjs` file that has a test with the same extension; subfolders and files of another kind
  are reported; `gate:tooling` also runs `scripts/*.test.cjs`. Measured: a `.cjs` without a test and a
  subfolder both turn it red.
- **D-B27 Focus ring:** the browser's default focus outline still shows on clickable elements (measured
  when pressing Tab: Chromium `auto 1px`, WebKit `auto 3px`); the brand focus ring
  (`--focus-ring`) moves to plan C. Price: the focus outline differs from the style guide at the review.
- **D-B28 The screen contract `contract.yaml`:** controls generated from data are declared once, with a code ending in
  `*` and `nameFrom: data`; the browser test reads the `href` of each link, clicks the
  `state` controls, and does the reverse check (every control in the content area is in the contract). Price: the
  contract format gains two fields.
- **D-B29 The mock server detector in the release build adds the string `Acme Holdings`** (which exists only in the mock data
  of the shell). Price: none.
- **D-B30 The "more" marker of the upcoming list and of the risk list opens WBS** ("+ 2 more · open
  in WBS"), the overdue list opens Focus like the wireframe. Price: changing the destination.
- **D-B31 An empty upcoming list mentions overdue milestones and gates only when there is one of the two** (does not add
  the two numbers). The Meridian sentence matches the wireframe word for word. Price: none.
- **D-B32 Initials take the first letter of the first two words of the name** ("Art Lead" becomes "AL"), because the contract
  has no such field. Price: Vietnamese names produce initials by family name.
- **D-B33 The iOS and Android package id is `dev.metis.app`** (`ios.bundleIdentifier`, `android.package`,
  Task 15). Why: `expo prebuild` needs it; the trial of 05/10 used `dev.metis.spikec`. Asked in spec 13.
  Price: changing it later makes it a different app on real devices and in the store.
- **D-B34 On iOS and Android, the mock server layer defines an empty class for `Event`, `EventTarget`,
  `MessageEvent`, `BroadcastChannel` when missing, before `require('msw')`** (Task 7). Measured while writing the
  plan on the Android Emulator: without them `require('msw')` throws `ReferenceError: Property
  'MessageEvent' doesn't exist`, then `'BroadcastChannel'`, and the app draws nothing; with them both the Android
  Emulator and the iOS Simulator show the mock data of Meridian. The core of MSW 2 only inherits or creates these
  classes at load time (the WebSocket and SSE part: `node_modules/msw/lib/core/ws.js:32`,
  `node_modules/@mswjs/interceptors/lib/browser/interceptors/WebSocket/index.cjs:35`); the mock server on
  the app only answers HTTP. No polyfill package is added. Price: if a later MSW version really uses one of these classes at load time,
  Task 15 turns red and reports the name.
- **D-B35 The trial run on the app uses one Maestro flow kept outside the repo** (`reports/native/smoke.yaml`,
  Task 15): open the app, wait for the text `Meridian CGI Campaign`, see `overview` and then `project-header` (drawn only when
  the screen's data has arrived), take a screenshot; a red flow is installed in advance, with a control flow that changes the id `project-header`. Why:
  the human eye is not a measurement, and a flow generated from the contract (spec 6) is a job for plan C. Price:
  none.
- **D-B36 The keyboard test on WebKit presses `Alt+Tab`** (Task 14). Measured while writing the plan: `Tab` of
  WebKit skips links and `button` tags and stops only at elements with `role="button"` that have `tabindex="0"`;
  `Alt+Tab` goes through everything like Safari's Option+Tab. Price: none.

## Parallel lanes

| Lane | Task | Starting condition |
|---|---|---|
| Main tree | 1, then 2, then 3, then 4 | Immediately |
| (a) design system | 5, then 6 | After Task 4 |
| (b) platform, scenarios, routes | 7, then 8 | After Task 4 |
| (c) dictionary, model | 9, then 10 | After Task 4 |
| Main tree: shell, then screen 24 | 11, then 12 | After merging (a), (b), (c) |
| Finish | 13, then 14, then 15, then 16 | After Task 12 |

The three lanes (a), (b), (c) touch separate folders: (a) `src/design-system/`; (b) `src/mocks/handlers.ts`,
`src/mocks/handlers.test.ts`, `src/platform/`, `src/app/`, `src/shell/NotBuilt.tsx`,
`src/shell/NotBuilt.test.native.tsx`, `e2e/web/routes.spec.ts`, `e2e/web/mocks.spec.ts`; (c)
`src/shell/strings/`, `src/screens/24-project-overview/`, and `eslint.config.js` (only Task 10 edits this
shared file among the three lanes). Only lane (a) adds a package (Task 5: `@react-native-picker/picker`, touching
`package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `LICENSES.md`), so those three files merge from lane (a) without conflict.
The controller runs each lane on an APFS copy of the repo (`cp -c -R`), merges back file by file with
`cmp` (as in plan A, section Rulings made during the run), then runs `pnpm verify` once on the merged tree before
running Task 11.

Tasks 11 and 12 do not run in parallel (pre-flight of 06/10/2026, F3): screen 24 imports `ProjectHeader`,
`projectHeaderOf`, `useLocale` of Task 11 and the screen's tests need `LocaleProvider`, so a copy
of its own for Task 12 lacks three files of Task 11 (`gate:types` reports `TS2307`). Both run on the main tree,
with no copy and no merge step: Task 11 finishes, its gates are green, and only then comes Task 12. Task 11 touches
`src/shell/` except `strings/`; Task 12 touches `src/screens/24-project-overview/` except `strings/`,
`model*.ts`, `contract.yaml`.

```js
// Test of the no-style-literals rule, run with node --test.
const test = require('node:test')
const { RuleTester } = require('eslint')
const rule = require('./no-style-literals')

RuleTester.describe = test.describe
RuleTester.it = test.it
RuleTester.itOnly = test.it.only

const ruleTester = new RuleTester({
  languageOptions: {
    ecmaVersion: 2022,
    sourceType: 'module',
    parserOptions: { ecmaFeatures: { jsx: true } }
  }
})
const box = (body) => `StyleSheet.create({ box: { ${body} } })`
// TypeScript's own syntax (as, satisfies, !) needs the typescript-eslint parser.
const typescript = { languageOptions: { parser: require('typescript-eslint').parser } }
// The <T>x form can be read only when JSX is off: name the file .ts instead of the default file.js.
const typescriptNoJsx = { ...typescript, filename: 'file.ts' }
const error = (messageId) => ({ messageId })

ruleTester.run('no-style-literals', rule, {
  valid: [
    box('padding: tokens.gap'),
    box('flex: 1, flexGrow: 3, opacity: 0.5, zIndex: 2, aspectRatio: 2.86'),
    box('margin: 0, borderWidth: 1, outlineWidth: 1'),
    box("width: '50%'"),
    box("backgroundColor: 'transparent', color: tokens.text"),
    'StyleSheet.create({ box: {\n  // token-exception: intrinsic size of the logo drawing\n  width: 120\n} })',
    box('padding: size ?? tokens.gap'),
    { code: box('width: tokens.gap as number'), ...typescript },
    box('color: dark ? tokens.ink : tokens.text'),
    box("backgroundColor: on ? 'transparent' : tokens.surface"),
    // A comparison in a condition produces true or false, not a size.
    box('width: w > 600 && tokens.sidebarW'),
    box('width: w > 600 ? tokens.sidebarW : tokens.gap'),
    // A size template string holds only variables: no number, no calculation.
    'const fill = (percent) => ({ width: `${percent}%` })',
    // A key that is not a style: numbers and calculations are free.
    'const model = { share: open / max, total: 12, label: "#1" }',
    // A destructuring pattern is not a style.
    'const { width = 8, color = "#fff" } = props',
    'const a = { [width]: 8, [key]: 8, 1: 8 }',
    // A key that merely starts or ends with the name of a size is not a style key.

    '<View width="24" />',
    '<View {...props} />',
    '<svg xlink:href="#abc" />',
    '<View width />',
    '<Spinner size="large" color="transparent" />'

    { code: box("color: '#111827' satisfies string"), ...typescript, errors: [error('colour')] },
    { code: box('padding: <number>8'), ...typescriptNoJsx, errors: [error('number')] },
    { code: box("color: <string>'#111827'"), ...typescriptNoJsx, errors: [error('colour')] },
    // Styles not passed through StyleSheet.create: a variable, a wrapping function, another name, a spread object.
    { code: 'const box = { padding: 8 }', errors: [error('number')] },
    { code: 'StyleSheet.create(factory({ box: { padding: 8 } }))', errors: [error('number')] },
    { code: 'SS.create({ box: wrap({ padding: 8 }) })', errors: [error('number')] },
    { code: 'other.create({ box: { padding: 8 } })', errors: [error('number')] },
    { code: 'StyleSheet.create({ box: { ...base, padding: 8 } })', errors: [error('number')] },
    // JSX properties.
    { code: '<Logo width={68.58} height={24} />', errors: [error('number'), error('number')] },
    { code: '<View padding={tokens.gap * 2} />', errors: [error('arithmetic')] },
    { code: '<Spinner size={20} color="#6D3BEF" />', errors: [error('number'), error('colour')] },
    { code: '<Icon fill="#111827" />', errors: [error('colour')] },
    { code: '<Spinner color="white" />', errors: [error('colour')] },
    { code: '<View\n  // token-exception:\n  width={24}\n/>', errors: [error('number')] }
  ]
})
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the token rule**

Replace the whole of `eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js` with:

```js
// Token gate (spec 7, R-B13 of plan B): size, spacing, corner radius, font size, line height,
// letter spacing and color come from tokens.ts. The rule examines style keys in every object of src, not only the
// argument of StyleSheet.create, so a style kept in a variable, wrapped in a function or called through another name is still
// examined; and it examines JSX size and color properties (width={24}, color="#fff"). Reports: a hard-coded number (except 0,
// and 1 for the border width), a calculation on a value (token * 2, -token), a hard-coded color code or one built by
// string concatenation. Does not apply to unitless properties (flex, flexGrow, opacity, zIndex, aspectRatio). A
// hard-coded value is allowed when the line right above says `// token-exception: <reason>`.
const SIZED =
  /^(width|height|(min|max)(Width|Height)|margin\w*|padding\w*|gap|rowGap|columnGap|top|right|bottom|left|start|end|inset\w*|border\w*Radius|fontSize|lineHeight|letterSpacing|flexBasis|translateX|translateY|shadowRadius|textShadowRadius|outlineOffset|size)$/
const BORDER_WIDTH = /^(border\w*Width|outlineWidth)$/
const COLOUR_KEY = /color$/i
const COLOUR_CODE = /#[0-9a-f]{3,8}\b|\b(rgba?|hsla?)\(/i
const ARITHMETIC = new Set(['+', '-', '*', '/', '%', '**'])
// A TypeScript type wrapper (as, satisfies, !, <T>) does not change the value: unwrap it and check the value inside.
const TS_WRAPPERS = new Set([
  'TSAsExpression',
  'TSSatisfiesExpression',
  'TSNonNullExpression',
  'TSTypeAssertion'
])

// The nodes that can be the final value of an expression: unwrap the type wrapper, take both branches of ?: and both
// sides of ??, ||, &&. A side that is a comparison (w > 600) produces true or false, not a value.
const valuesIn = (node) => {
  if (TS_WRAPPERS.has(node.type)) return valuesIn(node.expression)
  if (node.type === 'ConditionalExpression') {
    return [...valuesIn(node.consequent), ...valuesIn(node.alternate)]
  }
  if (node.type === 'LogicalExpression') return [...valuesIn(node.left), ...valuesIn(node.right)]
  return [node]
}

const isNumber = (node) => node.type === 'Literal' && typeof node.value === 'number'
const isString = (node) => node.type === 'Literal' && typeof node.value === 'string'
const isArithmetic = (node) =>
  (node.type === 'BinaryExpression' && ARITHMETIC.has(node.operator)) ||
  (node.type === 'UnaryExpression' &&
    ['-', '+'].includes(node.operator) &&
    !isNumber(node.argument))

// A template string or a concatenation: its static text, with the expression parts replaced by 000, so '#' + hex becomes
// "#000" and exposes the color code.
const isBuilt = (node) => node.type === 'TemplateLiteral' || node.type === 'BinaryExpression'
const textOf = (node) => {
  if (isString(node)) return node.value
  if (node.type === 'TemplateLiteral') return node.quasis.map((q) => q.value.raw).join('000')
  if (isBuilt(node)) return textOf(node.left) + textOf(node.right)
  return '000'
}

// Color: a color key accepts a hard-coded or concatenated string; no key may carry a color code.
const colourProblem = (key, node) => {
  const textual = isString(node) || isBuilt(node)
  if (COLOUR_KEY.test(key) && textual && node.value !== 'transparent') return 'colour'
  return COLOUR_CODE.test(textOf(node)) ? 'colour' : null
}

// Size: a calculation, or a hard-coded number other than 0 (border width also allows 1).
const sizeProblem = (key, node) => {
  const border = BORDER_WIDTH.test(key)
  if (!SIZED.test(key) && !border) return null
  if (isArithmetic(node)) return 'arithmetic'
  const literal = node.type === 'UnaryExpression' ? node.argument : node
  if (!isNumber(literal) || literal.value === 0) return null
  return border && literal.value === 1 ? null : 'number'
}

// One value under one key: returns the messageId to report, or null.
const problemOf = (key, node) => colourProblem(key, node) ?? sizeProblem(key, node)

// Every place to report under one key; inside a template string (`${x}px`) each expression is examined too.
const problemsIn = (key, value) =>
  valuesIn(value).flatMap((node) => {
    const problem = problemOf(key, node)
    if (problem) return [{ node, problem }]
    if (node.type !== 'TemplateLiteral') return []
    return node.expressions.flatMap((expression) => problemsIn(key, expression))
  })

module.exports = {
  meta: {
    type: 'problem',
    docs: { description: 'Style values come from tokens.ts' },
    messages: {
      number: '{{key}}: use a token from tokens.ts instead of the number {{value}}',
      arithmetic: '{{key}}: no calculation on a token ({{value}}); a size that is needed is a token of its own',
      colour: '{{key}}: use a color token from tokens.ts instead of {{value}}'
    },
    schema: []
  },
  create(context) {
    const excepted = (owner) =>
      context.sourceCode
        .getCommentsBefore(owner)
        .some(
          (c) =>
            c.type === 'Line' &&
            /^\s*token-exception:\s*\S/.test(c.value) &&
            c.loc.end.line === owner.loc.start.line - 1
        )

    const check = (owner, key, value) => {
      if (excepted(owner)) return
      for (const { node, problem } of problemsIn(key, value)) {
        const text = context.sourceCode.getText(node)
        context.report({ node, messageId: problem, data: { key, value: text } })
      }
    }

    return {
      // A key computed at run time ([key]: 8) has no known name, so it is skipped. A destructuring pattern (const { width = 8 } =
      // props) has an AssignmentPattern as its value, not a number, so it is not reported.
      Property(property) {
        if (property.computed) return
        const key = property.key.type === 'Identifier' ? property.key.name : property.key.value
        if (typeof key === 'string') check(property, key, property.value)
      },
      JSXAttribute(attribute) {
        const value = attribute.value
        if (attribute.name.type !== 'JSXIdentifier' || value === null) return
        check(
          attribute,
          attribute.name.name,
          value.type === 'JSXExpressionContainer' ? value.expression : value
        )
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Fix the rule "every tool has a test" before adding tools**

Replace the whole of `scripts/tooling.test.mjs` with:

```js
// The coverage of node --test only counts files that were loaded: a script with no test slips through
// gate:tooling. This test closes that hole.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { test } from 'node:test'

// A tool is a .js, .cjs or .mjs file; its test has the same name, with .test inserted before the extension.
const SOURCE = /\.[cm]?js$/

test('every file in scripts/ and eslint-rules/ is a .js, .cjs, .mjs tool with a test of the same extension next to it', () => {
  const untested = ['scripts', 'eslint-rules'].flatMap((dir) => {
    const entries = readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })
    const files = new Set(entries.filter((entry) => entry.isFile()).map((entry) => entry.name))
    // Finder on macOS may create .DS_Store in a folder; it is not a tool, so it is skipped.
    return entries
      .filter((entry) => entry.name !== '.DS_Store')
      .filter((entry) => !entry.name.includes('.test.'))
      .filter(
        (entry) =>
          !entry.isFile() ||
          !SOURCE.test(entry.name) ||
          !files.has(entry.name.replace(SOURCE, '.test$&'))
      )
      .map((entry) => `${dir}/${entry.name}`)
  })
  assert.deepEqual(untested, [])
})
```

This version differs from the first draft in two lines (fix round 1 of Task 2): Finder on macOS may create a `.DS_Store` file in `scripts/`, the first version treated it as a tool without a test so the test went red wrongly, which is why the list skips the name `.DS_Store` specifically.

```js
// Test of the .svg file transformer for Jest, run with node --test.
const assert = require('node:assert/strict')
const { join } = require('node:path')
const { test } = require('node:test')

const { process: transform } = require('./jest-svg.cjs')

}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the transformer and wire it into Jest**

`scripts/jest-svg.cjs`:

```js
// Transformer for .svg files for Jest. react-native-svg-transformer runs only in Metro, so under Jest
// each .svg file becomes a stand-in component that records its file path and its number of paths (<path>):
// the component test sees which file the logo is drawn from; Playwright measures the real layout on the web.
const { relative } = require('node:path')

module.exports = {
  process(source, filename) {
    const file = JSON.stringify(relative(process.cwd(), filename))
    const paths = (source.match(/<path\b/g) ?? []).length
    return {
      code: [
        "const { createElement } = require('react')",
        `const Svg = (props) => createElement('svg-file', { ...props, file: ${file}, paths: ${paths} })`,
        'module.exports = { __esModule: true, default: Svg }',
        ''
      ].join('\n')
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the whole of `jest.config.js` with the version below. It differs from the version of plan A in three places: the `.svg` pattern comes
before the preset's asset pattern (Jest uses the first pattern that matches); the Node project drops the `.web.` patterns (web
tests use jsdom); the top level has `testEnvironment: 'jest-fixed-jsdom'` only for Stryker to read
(D-B7).

```js
// The time zone of the test process must lie west of UTC and differ from Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, otherwise
// formatDate and formatTime would still print the expected string with the timeZone parameter dropped: format.test.ts uses UTC and
// Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, and a UTC date at midnight falls back to the previous day only in a time zone west of UTC.
process.env.TZ = 'America/Los_Angeles'

const path = require('node:path')
const { getIOSPreset, getAndroidPreset, getWebPreset, getNodePreset } = require('jest-expo/config')

// The dependency packages of MSW 2 ship only as ES modules: Jest 29 must compile them. A
// nested node_modules inside (hoisted install style) leaves the package inside to decide for itself, like .pnpm.
const esmOnly = ['rettime', 'until-async', '@open-draft/deferred-promise', 'set-cookie-parser']
const allowed = [...esmOnly, '(?:@[^/]+/)?[^/]+/node_modules']

// msw/node points the "react-native" condition to null; the iOS and Android projects of Jest still run on Node.
const mswNode = path.join(path.dirname(require.resolve('msw/package.json')), 'lib/node/index.js')
const native = (preset) => ({
  moduleNameMapper: { ...preset.moduleNameMapper, '^msw/node$': mswNode }
})

// The four projects of jest-expo/universal, built here so each project gets its own configuration.
const project = (preset, extra = {}) => {
  const [allowList, ...otherIgnores] = preset.transformIgnorePatterns
  const config = {
    ...preset,
    // Jest tests live only in src/; eslint-rules/ and scripts/ use node --test (gate:tooling).
    roots: ['<rootDir>/src'],
    // .svg comes before the preset's asset pattern: Jest uses the first pattern that matches.
    transform: {
      '\\.svg$': '<rootDir>/scripts/jest-svg.cjs',
      ...preset.transform,
      '\\.mjs$': preset.transform['\\.[jt]sx?$']
    },
    transformIgnorePatterns: [
      allowList.replace('(?!(', `(?!(${allowed.join('|')}|`),
      ...otherIgnores
    ],
    ...extra
  }
  delete config.watchPlugins // Jest accepts watchPlugins only at the top level
  return config
}

/** @type {import('jest').Config} */
module.exports = {
  // Only Stryker reads this line: it runs every project in one environment taken from the top level
  // (node_modules/@stryker-mutator/jest-runner/dist/src/jest-plugins/with-coverage-analysis.js:71),
  // so pick jsdom with fetch for the *.test.web.* tests. When Jest runs normally each project uses the
  // environment of its own.
  testEnvironment: 'jest-fixed-jsdom',
  projects: [
    project(getIOSPreset(), native(getIOSPreset())),
    project(getAndroidPreset(), native(getAndroidPreset())),
    // jsdom plus fetch, Response, TextEncoder and the streams of Node
    project(getWebPreset(), { testEnvironment: 'jest-fixed-jsdom' }),
    // *.test.web.* use localStorage, document, window of jsdom: only the Web project runs them. A
    // @jest-environment docblock in each file means Stryker cannot measure the coverage of that file.
    project(getNodePreset(), {
      testMatch: getNodePreset().testMatch.filter((glob) => !glob.includes('.web.'))
    })
  ],
  collectCoverageFrom: [
    'src/**/*.{ts,tsx}',
    '!src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}',
    '!src/**/*.test.*.{ts,tsx}',
    '!src/**/*.perf-test.{ts,tsx}',
    // Generated from brand/tokens.css by scripts/gen-tokens.mjs, no logic.
    '!src/design-system/tokens.ts',
    // Route files only connect the shell and the screen (spec 3.1); the e2e tests of the second plan check them.
    '!src/app/**'
  ],
  coverageThreshold: {
    global: { lines: 100, branches: 100, functions: 100, statements: 100 }
  }
}
```

```ts
import { useFonts } from 'expo-font'

// iOS and Android (spec 5.4): the file covering all Latin and Vietnamese characters, loaded with expo-font. The key is the first
// name in the font string of the token, exactly the name src/design-system/fonts.ts uses.
const FONT_FILES = {
  Inter: require('../../assets/fonts/Inter.ttf'),
  Newsreader: require('../../assets/fonts/Newsreader.ttf'),
  Manrope: require('../../assets/fonts/Manrope.ttf')
}

// true when the three fonts have loaded, or when loading fails: the app still renders, with the system font.
export function useAppFonts(): boolean {
  const [loaded, error] = useFonts(FONT_FILES)
  return loaded || error !== null
}
```

```ts
// Web (spec 5.4): @font-face in public/index.html declares the latin and vietnamese blocks by
// unicode-range, and the browser loads them itself. expo-font cannot write unicode-range, so the web does not use it.
export function useAppFonts(): boolean {
  return true
}
```

```js
// The logo and the favicon of the app are byte-for-byte copies of brand/logo (spec 5.2), run with node --test.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { test } from 'node:test'

const app = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../assets/brand')
const brand = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../../../brand/logo')

test('every file in assets/brand is byte-for-byte identical to the file of the same name in brand/logo', () => {
  // readdirSync promises no order (CI runs on Linux): sort before comparing. Finder on macOS
  // may create .DS_Store in a folder: drop that file from the list.
  const files = readdirSync(app)
    .filter((name) => name !== '.DS_Store')
    .sort()
  assert.deepEqual(files, ['metis-favicon-48.png', 'metis-wordmark.svg'])
  for (const file of files) {
    assert.ok(readFileSync(resolve(app, file)).equals(readFileSync(resolve(brand, file))), file)
  }
})
```

```js
// Tests of the static server for the web export, run with node --test.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { after, before, test } from 'node:test'

import { fileFor, handler } from './serve-web.mjs'

const CLI = join(import.meta.dirname, 'serve-web.mjs')
const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'serve-web-'))
const server = createServer(handler(root))
let base

before(async () => {
  mkdirSync(join(root, 'fonts'))
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'index.html'), '<div id="root"></div>')
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'entry.js'), 'run()')
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'fonts', 'inter-latin.woff2'), 'wOF2')
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'data.bin'), 'raw')
  await new Promise((done) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', done))
  base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`
})

after(() => {
  server.close()
  // A hung request keeps its connection open and the test process does not exit: close every connection.
  server.closeAllConnections()
  rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })
})

const get = async (path) => {
  const res = await fetch(base + path)
  return [res.status, res.headers.get('content-type'), await res.text()]
}

test('a deep path returns index.html, including a code with a dot and an extension that is not an asset', async () => {
  const page = [200, 'text/html; charset=utf-8', '<div id="root"></div>']
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/'), page)
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'), page)
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/w/creative-studio/projects/p/wbs/item-1.1.1'), page)
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/data.bin'), page)
})

test('a real asset file returns the right content type', async () => {
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/entry.js'), [200, 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', 'run()'])
  // The query string is not part of the file's path.
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/entry.js?v=1'), [200, 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', 'run()'])
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/fonts/inter-latin.woff2'), [200, 'font/woff2', 'wOF2'])
})

test('a file with an extension that does not exist gives 404, not index.html', async () => {
  assert.deepEqual(await get('/nope.js'), [404, 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', 'Not found'])
})

// A request target that cannot be parsed (a broken % sign makes decodeURIComponent throw) gives 404 and the server
// stays alive. The old code did not answer but died, so the request hung: a timeout is needed.
test(
  'a request target that cannot be parsed gives 404, the server keeps serving',
  { timeout: 5000 },
  async () => {
    const notFound = [404, 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', 'Not found']
    assert.deepEqual(await get('/w/100%/x'), notFound)
    assert.deepEqual(await get('/%E0%A4%A'), notFound)
    assert.deepEqual(await get('/entry.js'), [200, 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', 'run()'])
  }
)

test('a path that escapes the export folder has no file', () => {
  assert.equal(fileFor('/srv/dist', '/a%2F..%2F..%2Fsecret.txt'), null)
  // A sibling folder whose name starts with the export folder's name is also outside: the separator must be compared too.
  assert.equal(fileFor('/srv/dist', '/..%2Fdist-other/x.js'), null)
  assert.equal(fileFor('/srv/dist', '/fonts/a.woff2'), '/srv/dist/fonts/a.woff2')
})

test('command line: an export folder without index.html exits 1, names the folder and opens no port', () => {
  const empty = join(root, 'empty')
  mkdirSync(empty)
  const run = spawnSync(process.execPath, [CLI, empty, '0'], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 })
  assert.equal(run.status, 1)
  assert.ok(run.stderr.includes(empty), run.stderr)
  assert.equal(run.stdout, '')
})
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 3): a request with a broken `%` sign (`/%E0%A4%A`) made `decodeURIComponent` throw and killed the whole server, so there is a test that an unparseable target must receive 404; the same round added tests for the query string `?v=1`, for the sibling folder `dist-other` and for the command line when the export folder has no `index.html`.

```js
// Tests of the mock server detector in the web export, run with node --test.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { after, test } from 'node:test'

import { findMocks } from './check-web-release.mjs'

const CLI = join(import.meta.dirname, 'check-web-release.mjs')
const roots = []
const exportOf = (files) => {
  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'check-web-release-'))
  roots.push(root)
  for (const [name, text] of Object.entries(files)) {
    mkdirSync(join(root, name, '..'), { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(join(root, name), text)
  }
  return root
}
after(() => roots.forEach((root) => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })))

test('a clean release build: nothing', () => {
  const dir = exportOf({ 'index.html': '<div id="root"></div>', '_expo/web/entry.js': 'app()' })
  assert.deepEqual(findMocks(dir), [])
})

test('reports the worker file, the MSW marker and the mock data strings, for each .js and .html file', () => {
  const dir = exportOf({
    'mockServiceWorker.js': 'self.addEventListener("fetch", f)',
    'index.html': '<script>/* Creative Production */</script>',
    '_expo/web/entry.js': 'console.warn("[MSW] x"); register("/mockServiceWorker.js")',
    '_expo/web/handlers.js': '{"client":"Northwind Furniture Co.","pic":"Denny K."}',
    '_expo/web/shell.js': '{"tenant":{"name":"Acme Holdings"}}',
    'metadata.json': '{"note":"Denny K."}'
  })
  assert.deepEqual(findMocks(dir).sort(), [
    '_expo/web/entry.js: [MSW]',
    '_expo/web/entry.js: mockServiceWorker',
    '_expo/web/handlers.js: Denny K.',
    '_expo/web/handlers.js: Northwind Furniture Co.',
    '_expo/web/shell.js: Acme Holdings',
    'index.html: Creative Production',
    'mockServiceWorker.js (file)'
  ])
})

// The minimal export that the detector counts as clean, and the line that identifies MSW's real worker file
// (public/mockServiceWorker.js, line 11: there is no [MSW] marker or file name in the worker file itself).
const CLEAN = { 'index.html': '<div id="root"></div>', '_expo/web/entry.js': 'app()' }
const WORKER = "const INTEGRITY_CHECKSUM = '03cb67ac84128e63d7cd722a6e5b7f1e'"

// Each row is a way around that was measured: an export with the mock server, or with nothing to scan, that the detector
// once let through. .json is still not scanned (metadata.json in the test above).
const walkArounds = [
  [
    'worker in a subfolder',
    { ...CLEAN, '_expo/static/mockServiceWorker.js': WORKER },
    ['_expo/static/mockServiceWorker.js: INTEGRITY_CHECKSUM']
  ],
  [
    'renamed worker',
    { ...CLEAN, '_expo/web/sw.js': WORKER },
    ['_expo/web/sw.js: INTEGRITY_CHECKSUM']
  ],
  [
    '[MSW] marker in a .mjs file',
    { ...CLEAN, '_expo/web/boot.mjs': 'warn("[MSW] x")' },
    ['_expo/web/boot.mjs: [MSW]']
  ],
  [
    '[MSW] marker in a .cjs file',
    { ...CLEAN, '_expo/web/boot.cjs': 'warn("[MSW] x")' },
    ['_expo/web/boot.cjs: [MSW]']
  ],
  [
    '[MSW] marker in a .map source map',
    { ...CLEAN, '_expo/web/entry.js.map': '{"sourcesContent":["warn(\\"[MSW] x\\")"]}' },
    ['_expo/web/entry.js.map: [MSW]']
  ],
  ['empty folder', {}, ['*.js (missing)', 'index.html (missing)']],
  ['has index.html but no .js file', { 'index.html': CLEAN['index.html'] }, ['*.js (missing)']],
  [
    'has a .js file but no index.html',
    { '_expo/web/entry.js': CLEAN['_expo/web/entry.js'] },
    ['index.html (missing)']
  ]
]
for (const [name, files, expected] of walkArounds) {
  test(`does not get through: ${name}`, () => {
    assert.deepEqual(findMocks(exportOf(files)).sort(), expected)
  })
}

// The command line's exit code is what the build:web gate relies on, and it lies outside coverage: run it for real to pin it.
test('command line: an export with the mock server exits 1 and prints FAIL, a clean one exits 0 and prints OK', () => {
  const run = (dir) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [CLI, dir], { encoding: 'utf8' })
  const dirty = run(exportOf({ ...CLEAN, 'mockServiceWorker.js': WORKER }))
  assert.equal(dirty.status, 1)
  assert.ok(dirty.stdout.startsWith('FAIL '), dirty.stdout)
  assert.ok(dirty.stdout.includes('mockServiceWorker.js (file)'), dirty.stdout)
  const clean = run(exportOf(CLEAN))
  assert.equal(clean.status, 0)
  assert.ok(clean.stdout.startsWith('OK '), clean.stdout)
})
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the static server and the detector**

`scripts/serve-web.mjs` (a path with an asset extension is a file, any other path is a page of the app; the version of the
trial returned 404 for `/w/.../wbs/item-1.1.1` because it took `.1` as a file extension, measured while writing the plan):

```js
// Static server for the single-page web export (spec 2, web.output "single"), used for Playwright:
// node scripts/serve-web.mjs <export folder> <port>. A path with an asset extension (.js, .woff2, ...)
// is a file: served if it exists, 404 if not. Any other path, including a code with a dot such as wbs/item-1.1.1, is
// a page of the app: it returns index.html so that a deep path can be opened directly.
import { existsSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs'
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { extname, join, normalize, resolve, sep } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

const TYPES = {
  '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8',
  '.js': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8',
  '.json': 'application/json',
  '.woff2': 'font/woff2',
  '.png': 'image/png',
  '.ico': 'image/x-icon'
}

// The request's path becomes a file inside root; a path that escapes root gives null.
export function fileFor(root, url) {
  const path = decodeURIComponent(new URL(url, 'http://localhost').pathname)
  const file = normalize(join(root, path))
  if (!file.startsWith(root + sep)) return null
  return Object.hasOwn(TYPES, extname(path)) ? file : join(root, 'index.html')
}

export const handler = (root) => async (req, res) => {
  try {
    // fileFor also throws for a request target that cannot be parsed (a broken % sign, "//["): it sits inside try
    // so that those targets get 404 instead of killing the server.
    const file = fileFor(root, req.url)
    const body = await readFile(file)
    res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': TYPES[extname(file)] })
    res.end(body)
  } catch {
    res.writeHead(404, { 'content-type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' })
    res.end('Not found')
  }
}

/* node:coverage disable */
// Runs only when called from the command line.
if (process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const [dir = 'dist', port = '5310'] = process.argv.slice(2)
  const root = resolve(dir)
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) {
    createServer(handler(root)).listen(Number(port), '127.0.0.1', () =>
      console.log(`serve-web: http://127.0.0.1:${port} -> ${dir}`)
    )
  } else {
    // The folder has not been exported: exit at once with the reason, so Playwright reports an error right away instead of waiting 60 seconds for the port to open.
    console.error(`serve-web: ${dir} has no index.html, run pnpm build:web:e2e first`)
    process.exitCode = 1
  }
}
/* node:coverage enable */
```

This version differs from the first draft in two places (fix round 1 of Task 3): `fileFor` runs inside `try`, so that a request target that cannot be parsed gets 404 instead of killing the server; and the command line exits at once with one line in Vietnamese when the export folder has no `index.html`, so that Playwright reports an error after about one second instead of waiting the full 60 seconds for the port to open.

`scripts/check-web-release.mjs`:

```js
// The release web export carries no mock server (spec 3.4): no mockServiceWorker.js, no
// MSW code, no mock data strings. Use: node scripts/check-web-release.mjs dist (exit 1 when found).
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'

// Three MSW markers (two in the startup code; INTEGRITY_CHECKSUM is only in the worker file itself, no matter
// which folder it sits in or whether it was renamed), then four strings found only in src/mocks/fixtures (Acme Holdings:
// the shell's data).
const MARKERS = [
  '[MSW]',
  'mockServiceWorker',
  'INTEGRITY_CHECKSUM',
  'Northwind Furniture Co.',
  'Creative Production',
  'Denny K.',
  'Acme Holdings'
]

// Code files and pages that the browser loads; .map holds the whole source code. .json is not scanned (metadata.json).
const SCANNED = /\.(js|mjs|cjs|html|map)$/

export function findMocks(dir) {
  const files = readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }).map(String)
  const found = existsSync(join(dir, 'mockServiceWorker.js')) ? ['mockServiceWorker.js (file)'] : []
  // An empty or wrongly pointed folder has nothing to scan: it must not count as clean.
  if (!existsSync(join(dir, 'index.html'))) found.push('index.html (missing)')
  if (!files.some((file) => file.endsWith('.js'))) found.push('*.js (missing)')
  for (const file of files.filter((name) => SCANNED.test(name))) {
    const text = readFileSync(join(dir, file), 'utf8')
    found.push(...MARKERS.filter((marker) => text.includes(marker)).map((m) => `${file}: ${m}`))
  }
  return found
}

/* node:coverage disable */
// Runs only when called from the command line.
if (process.argv[1] && realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const dir = process.argv[2] ?? 'dist'
  const found = findMocks(dir)
  console.log(
    found.length ? `FAIL ${dir}:\n  ${found.join('\n  ')}` : `OK ${dir}: no mock server`
  )
  process.exitCode = found.length ? 1 : 0
}
/* node:coverage enable */
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 3): added the marker `INTEGRITY_CHECKSUM`, found only in the worker file itself, so it catches a worker put in the wrong place or renamed; also scans `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.map`; and an export with no `index.html` or no `.js` file is reported as an error instead of being counted as clean.

- [ ] **Step 7: Write the shared part, run it to see it green**

`e2e/web/support.ts`:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'

import { AxeBuilder } from '@axe-core/playwright'
import type { Locator, Page } from '@playwright/test'

// Shared part of the tests in the browser (spec 7). Numbers and colours are read at run time from the single source
// brand/tokens.css, never from tokens.ts: changing a number in tokens.ts without changing the source
// must make the measurement go red.
const tokensCss = readFileSync(resolve(__dirname, '../../../../brand/tokens.css'), 'utf8')

export function token(name: string): string {
  const match = tokensCss.match(new RegExp(`--${name}:\\s*([^;]+);`))
  if (!match?.[1]) throw new Error(`--${name} not found in brand/tokens.css`)
  return match[1].trim()
}

// The px number of a size token.
export function px(name: string): number {
  const value = token(name)
  if (!/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?px$/.test(value)) throw new Error(`--${name} is not a px value: ${value}`)
  return Number.parseFloat(value)
}

// A #RRGGBB colour token written the way getComputedStyle returns it.
export function rgb(name: string): string {
  const hex = token(name)
  const parts = hex.match(/^#([0-9a-f]{2})([0-9a-f]{2})([0-9a-f]{2})$/i)
  if (!parts) throw new Error(`--${name} is not a #RRGGBB colour: ${hex}`)
  return `rgb(${parts
    .slice(1)
    .map((pair) => Number.parseInt(pair, 16))
    .join(', ')})`
}

export async function box(locator: Locator) {
  const rect = await locator.boundingBox()
  if (!rect) throw new Error(`no box for ${locator}`)
  return rect
}

export const style = (locator: Locator, property: string) =>
  locator.evaluate((el, name) => getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(name), property)

// axe-core: errors of level serious or critical, each error with the element reported (spec 7, accessibility).
export async function blockingAxe(page: Page): Promise<string[]> {
  const { violations } = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()
  return violations
    .filter((v) => v.impact === 'serious' || v.impact === 'critical')
    .map((v) => `${v.id} (${v.impact}) ${v.nodes.map((n) => n.target.join(' ')).join(', ')}`)
}

// Errors of the page while a test runs: thrown errors and console.error (spec 7, behaviour).
export function pageErrors(page: Page): string[] {
  const errors: string[] = []
  page.on('pageerror', (error) => errors.push(error.message))
  page.on('console', (message) => {
    if (message.type() === 'error') errors.push(message.text())
  })
  return errors
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the route table**

`src/core/routes.ts`:

```ts
// Route table (spec 3.1, 4.3): destination code to the Expo Router route pattern and the screen number in
// wireframes/manifest.json. An MVP destination not yet built has its final route, which opens the shared "not built yet" page
// (rule 1); a destination of a later release has no route (rule 2). Patterns are written verbatim so that the route type of
// Expo Router catches a mistyped path.
export const ROUTES = {
  overview: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/overview',
  charter: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/charter',
  wbs: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/wbs',
  wbsItem: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/wbs/[itemId]',
  plan: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/plan',
  governance: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/governance',
  focus: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/focus',
  changeRequest: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/changes/new',
  newProject: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/new',
  cockpit: '/w/[workspaceId]/cockpit',
  dashboard: '/w/[workspaceId]/dashboard',
  registry: '/w/[workspaceId]/registry',
  roadmap: '/w/[workspaceId]/roadmap',
  capacity: '/w/[workspaceId]/capacity',
  risk: '/w/[workspaceId]/risk',
  frameworks: '/w/[workspaceId]/frameworks',
  templates: '/w/[workspaceId]/templates',
  settings: '/w/[workspaceId]/settings',
  myFocus: '/me/focus',
  approvals: '/me/approvals',
  notifications: '/me/notifications',
  search: '/search'
} as const

export type Destination = keyof typeof ROUTES

// The names of the [name] segments of a route pattern.
type SegmentsOf<P extends string> = P extends `${string}[${infer Name}]${infer Rest}`
  ? Name | SegmentsOf<Rest>
  : never
// Drill-down filters go into query parameters (spec 4.3); values are taken as they are from the server.
export type Query = Record<string, string | string[]>
// A link to a destination: the route pattern verbatim, every [name] segment of the pattern, plus the filters. A union of
// each destination, so when it is handed to the Link of Expo Router, the route type still checks each pattern.
export type Route = {
  [D in Destination]: {
    pathname: (typeof ROUTES)[D]
    params: Record<SegmentsOf<(typeof ROUTES)[D]>, string> & Query
  }
}[Destination]

// The manifest's screen number for each destination, which the "not built yet" page prints.
export const SCREENS: Record<Destination, number> = {
  overview: 24,
  charter: 25,
  wbs: 26,
  wbsItem: 28,
  plan: 30,
  governance: 12,
  focus: 34,
  changeRequest: 32,
  newProject: 37,
  cockpit: 14,
  dashboard: 15,
  registry: 16,
  roadmap: 17,
  capacity: 18,
  risk: 19,
  frameworks: 11,
  templates: 13,
  settings: 9,
  myFocus: 34,
  approvals: 38,
  notifications: 39,
  search: 40
}

// Whether a sidebar item has a route (Investment, Scenarios, SteerCo, AI copilot do not).
export const isDestination = (code: string): code is Destination => Object.hasOwn(ROUTES, code)

// The route parameters and query parameters that a page receives, as useLocalSearchParams returns them.
export type Params = Readonly<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>>

// The values of a query parameter. expo-router writes a multi-value filter as one value
// joined with commas (risk=high%2Ccritical, build/link/href.js:80-84), while a path with a repeated key
// (risk=high&risk=critical) gives an array. Split each element on commas so that the two forms give the same
// values.
const valuesOf = (value: string | string[]) => [value].flat().flatMap((item) => item.split(','))

// The filters that the "not built yet" page prints (spec 4.3 rule 1): the query parameters, without the [name] segments of
// the route pattern, in alphabetical order, each name with all its values.
export function filtersOf(destination: Destination, params: Params): [string, string[]][] {
  const segments = new Set([...ROUTES[destination].matchAll(/\[(\w+)\]/g)].map((m) => m[1]))
  return Object.entries(params)
    .filter(([name]) => !segments.has(name))
    .flatMap(([name, value]): [string, string[]][] =>
      value === undefined ? [] : [[name, valuesOf(value)]]
    )
    .sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b))
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 12): adds the function `valuesOf`, and `filtersOf` uses it so that
each value, single or inside an array, is split on commas. The first version left the string as it was, so clicking the High
risk cell (writing `risk=high%2Ccritical`) shows `risk: high,critical` on the not-built page, while a path with
a repeated key shows `risk: high, critical`. One fix at the only place that reads, because a filter value is a code
of the server and has no comma. The cost if wrong: a future value with a comma would be split; then
plan C writes a repeated key instead of a comma. The test file now has six tests, so Step 2 expects
`Tests: 24 passed, 24 total` (four projects), not 12.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the contract of the shell**

`src/core/api/shell.ts`:

```ts
import { z } from 'zod'

// Contract of the app shell (R-B2, also recorded in spec 3.5): one call for the user, the tenant,
// the workspace and the list of workspaces of the picker menu, the sidebar items with counts and the labels of
// future features, the project tree (also the source of names for the breadcrumb path), the notification count. The data carries only codes
// and user content: the label of a code lives in the shell's dictionary, the route of a code lives in
// src/core/routes.ts.

const text = z.string().min(1)
const count = z.number().int().nonnegative()

// Codes of the sidebar items (spec 4.1), also the destination codes in the route table.
export const NAV_CODES = [
  'myFocus',
  'approvals',
  'cockpit',
  'dashboard',
  'registry',
  'roadmap',
  'capacity',
  'risk',
  'investment',
  'scenarios',
  'steerco',
  'copilot',
  'frameworks',
  'templates',
  'settings'
] as const

const navItem = z.object({
  code: z.enum(NAV_CODES),
  // The count next to the item; alert is a red background, like the number of My focus on the wireframe.
  badge: z.object({ count, alert: z.boolean() }).nullable(),
  // A destination of a later release (spec 4.3 rule 2): text with a Planned label, not clickable.
  planned: z.enum(['V2', 'V3']).nullable()
})

const project = z.object({ id: text, name: text })
const program = z.object({ name: text, projects: z.array(project) })
const portfolio = z.object({ name: text, programs: z.array(program) })

export const shellSchema = z.object({
  user: z.object({ name: text, initials: text }),
  tenant: z.object({ name: text }),
  workspace: z.object({ id: text, name: text }),
  workspaces: z.array(z.object({ id: text, name: text })).min(1),
  nav: z.object({
    home: z.array(navItem),
    portfolio: z.array(navItem),
    workspace: z.array(navItem)
  }),
  tree: z.array(portfolio),
  notifications: count
})

export type Shell = z.infer<typeof shellSchema>
```
