- [ ] **Step 6: Modify the client**

Replace the whole of `src/core/api/client.ts` with:

```ts
import type { z } from 'zod'

import { type Overview, overviewSchema } from './overview'
import { type Shell, shellSchema } from './shell'

// Named errors that the screen knows how to draw (spec 3.3, 4.5, R-B15). The client never throws an error to the screen.
export type ApiError =
  | { kind: 'unauthenticated' }
  | { kind: 'forbidden' }
  | { kind: 'notFound' }
  | { kind: 'server'; status: number }
  | { kind: 'invalid'; issues: { path: string; message: string }[] }
  | { kind: 'network' }
  | { kind: 'timeout' }

export type ApiResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: ApiError }

export type ApiConfig = { baseUrl: string; timeoutMs: number }

// The scope of the overview screen (spec 4.3, R-B4): the whole project, or only the work of the person viewing.
export type Scope = 'project' | 'mine'

const STATUS_ERRORS: Partial<Record<number, ApiError>> = {
  401: { kind: 'unauthenticated' },
  403: { kind: 'forbidden' },
  404: { kind: 'notFound' }
}

const fail = (error: ApiError): { ok: false; error: ApiError } => ({ ok: false, error })

function parse<T>(schema: z.ZodType<T>, text: string): ApiResult<T> {
  let body: unknown
  try {
    body = JSON.parse(text)
  } catch {
    return fail({ kind: 'invalid', issues: [{ path: '', message: 'body is not JSON' }] })
  }
  const result = schema.safeParse(body)
  if (result.success) return { ok: true, data: result.data }
  const issues = result.error.issues.map((issue) => ({
    path: issue.path.join('.'),
    message: issue.message
  }))
  return fail({ kind: 'invalid', issues })
}

// Never throws: every failure becomes an ApiError.
async function request<T>(
  url: string,
  schema: z.ZodType<T>,
  signal: AbortSignal
): Promise<ApiResult<T>> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(url, { signal })
    if (!response.ok) {
      return fail(STATUS_ERRORS[response.status] ?? { kind: 'server', status: response.status })
    }
    return parse(schema, await response.text())
  } catch {
    return fail(signal.aborted ? { kind: 'timeout' } : { kind: 'network' })
  }
}

// The timer is cleared only after the response body has been read, so the timeout counts the body read too: fetch
// cancels the read when the signal is aborted.
async function getJson<T>(url: string, schema: z.ZodType<T>, timeoutMs: number) {
  const controller = new AbortController()
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs)
  const result = await request(url, schema, controller.signal)
  clearTimeout(timer)
  return result
}

// An empty code, "." or ".." stays unchanged through encodeURIComponent, then the URL merges them into the path
// (".." goes up one level) and the call lands on another page. Such a code does not really exist: return notFound, do not
// call the network.
const isRouteId = (id: string) => id !== '' && id !== '.' && id !== '..'

// GET {baseUrl}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/projects/{projectId}/overview (spec 3.5), with
// ?scope=mine for "My items" (R-B4). The codes come from the user's path so they are encoded: a space,
// a slash, an accented letter do not break the call path.
export const getOverview = (
  config: ApiConfig,
  workspaceId: string,
  projectId: string,
  scope: Scope
): Promise<ApiResult<Overview>> => {
  if (!isRouteId(workspaceId) || !isRouteId(projectId)) {
    return Promise.resolve(fail({ kind: 'notFound' }))
  }
  const query = scope === 'mine' ? '?scope=mine' : ''
  return getJson(
    `${config.baseUrl}/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(workspaceId)}/projects/${encodeURIComponent(projectId)}/overview${query}`,
    overviewSchema,
    config.timeoutMs
  )
}

// GET {baseUrl}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/shell: the data of the shell (R-B2).
export const getShell = (config: ApiConfig, workspaceId: string): Promise<ApiResult<Shell>> => {
  if (!isRouteId(workspaceId)) return Promise.resolve(fail({ kind: 'notFound' }))
  return getJson(
    `${config.baseUrl}/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(workspaceId)}/shell`,
    shellSchema,
    config.timeoutMs
  )
}
```

implementer writes the code, the plan copies the real code back after the review. Every measurement is taken from
`wireframes/assets/wireframe.css` (the line is given in parentheses) at a width of 1440 px.

**Files:** each component `X` has `src/design-system/X.tsx`, `X.styles.ts`, `X.test.native.tsx`.
- Create: `status.ts` and `status.test.ts`; `Text`, `Glyph`, `Logo`, `Tag`, `Chip`, `CountBadge`,
  `Avatar`, `Button`, `Spinner`, `Select` (three files each)
- Modify: `apps/metis/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` (the picker), `apps/metis/LICENSES.md` (one line)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `tokens` (Task 1), `fonts` (Task 2), `Route` (Task 4), file
  `assets/brand/metis-wordmark.svg` (Task 2).
- Produces: the components below with exactly the props listed in the table; `type StatusTone`, `STATUS`,
  `type WorkStatus`, `WORK_FILL` from `status.ts` (Task 6 uses the last two names for the bar and the legend);
  `type TextVariant`, `type TextTone`, `type GlyphName`. All text comes in through a required prop (spec 5.5);
  no component has default text. Status colours (seven groups `good` to `neutral` and
  `neutralFill`) go only through `status.ts` (global constraint, spec 5.1): a component reads `STATUS` or
  `WORK_FILL`, and does not read directly `tokens.critical`, `tokens.criticalText`, `tokens.waitingBg`, ...

Common rules for every component in this task and Task 6: styles only in `X.styles.ts`
(`StyleSheet.create`, only tokens; a style that changes with data is a small function in the same file, for example
`grow(weight) => ({ flexGrow: weight })`); no `testID` in the design system unless the table says so;
a link is the `Link` of `expo-router` with `asChild` wrapping `Pressable role="link"`, `href` takes a `Route`;
a button is `Pressable role="button"`.

#### Real code after the review

The full code of 32 files, copied byte for byte after the review (R-B12): the steps above give the structure, props, tokens
and the test table, while the code that ran is in the blocks below, each block being a whole file.

`src/design-system/status.ts`:

```ts
import { tokens } from './tokens'

// The seven status color groups (spec 5.1) go only through this file: a component reads STATUS or WORK_FILL, and does not
// read the tokens `critical`, `waitingBg`, ... directly. Each group has three colors: the fill color (dot, bar), the text color and
// the background color (chip, strip).
export type StatusTone =
  'good' | 'waiting' | 'serious' | 'critical' | 'running' | 'review' | 'neutral'

export const STATUS: Record<StatusTone, { fill: string; text: string; bg: string }> = {
  good: { fill: tokens.good, text: tokens.goodText, bg: tokens.goodBg },
  waiting: { fill: tokens.waiting, text: tokens.waitingText, bg: tokens.waitingBg },
  serious: { fill: tokens.serious, text: tokens.seriousText, bg: tokens.seriousBg },
  critical: { fill: tokens.critical, text: tokens.criticalText, bg: tokens.criticalBg },
  running: { fill: tokens.running, text: tokens.runningText, bg: tokens.runningBg },
  review: { fill: tokens.review, text: tokens.reviewText, bg: tokens.reviewBg },
  neutral: { fill: tokens.neutral, text: tokens.neutralText, bg: tokens.neutralBg }
}

// The fill colors of the work statuses, written once for the stacked bar, the legend and the bar per row
// (wireframe.css:199): done is green, in progress is blue, waiting is amber, blocked is red,
// not started is the fill gray.
export type WorkStatus = 'done' | 'inProgress' | 'waiting' | 'blocked' | 'notStarted'

export const WORK_FILL: Record<WorkStatus, string> = {
  done: STATUS.good.fill,
  inProgress: STATUS.running.fill,
  waiting: STATUS.waiting.fill,
  blocked: STATUS.critical.fill,
  notStarted: tokens.neutralFill
}
```

`src/design-system/status.test.ts`:

```ts
import { STATUS, type StatusTone, WORK_FILL, type WorkStatus } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

const TONES: StatusTone[] = [
  'good',
  'waiting',
  'serious',
  'critical',
  'running',
  'review',
  'neutral'
]

test('STATUS.critical is the three tokens of the same name', () => {
  expect(STATUS.critical).toEqual({
    fill: tokens.critical,
    text: tokens.criticalText,
    bg: tokens.criticalBg
  })
})

test('STATUS has exactly seven groups, in the order of the spec', () => {
  expect(Object.keys(STATUS)).toEqual(TONES)
})

test.each(TONES)('STATUS.%s takes the three tokens of the same name', (tone) => {
  expect(STATUS[tone]).toEqual({
    fill: tokens[tone],
    text: tokens[`${tone}Text` as const],
    bg: tokens[`${tone}Bg` as const]
  })
})

test('WORK_FILL fills the work statuses with the status colors, only not started is the fill gray', () => {
  expect(WORK_FILL).toEqual({
    done: tokens.good,
    inProgress: tokens.running,
    waiting: tokens.waiting,
    blocked: tokens.critical,
    notStarted: tokens.neutralFill
  })
})

test('WORK_FILL has exactly five keys, in that order', () => {
  const order: WorkStatus[] = ['done', 'inProgress', 'waiting', 'blocked', 'notStarted']
  expect(Object.keys(WORK_FILL)).toEqual(order)
})
```

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Text as NativeText } from 'react-native'

import { type TextTone, textStyle, type TextVariant, type TextWeight } from './Text.styles'

export type { TextTone, TextVariant }

type TextProps = {
  // A string, or a nested Text for a part that changes color within a line.
  children: ReactNode
  variant: TextVariant
  tone?: TextTone
  // Overrides the weight of the variant.
  weight?: TextWeight
  // Heading level 1, 2 or 3 for screen readers.
  heading?: 1 | 2 | 3
  // Cut to one line, with an ellipsis added at the end.
  lines?: 1
  tabular?: boolean
}

export function Text({
  children,
  variant,
  tone = 'text',
  weight,
  heading,
  lines,
  tabular
}: TextProps) {
  return (
    <NativeText
      role={heading ? 'heading' : undefined}
      aria-level={heading}
      numberOfLines={lines}
      ellipsizeMode="tail"
      style={textStyle(variant, tone, weight, tabular)}
    >
      {children}
    </NativeText>
  )
}
```

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { fonts } from './fonts'
import { STATUS } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

// Each variant is a row of the table of plan B (Task 5); measurements come from wireframe.css at a width of 1440 px.
// Single-line text has a line height equal to the font size (line-height 1 of the wireframe), multi-line text uses the lh* tokens.
const variants = StyleSheet.create({
  projectTitle: {
    fontFamily: fonts.display,
    fontSize: tokens.fsProjectTitle,
    fontWeight: '500',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhProjectTitle,
    letterSpacing: tokens.lsProjectTitle
  },

    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhH2
  },

    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhH3
  },
  body: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsBody,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhBody
  },
  small: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsSmall,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhSmall
  },
  caption: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsCaption,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhCaption
  },
  crumb: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsCrumbs,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhCrumbs
  },
  fresh: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsTag,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhFresh
  },
  figure: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsFigure,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhFigure
  },
  percent: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsFigure,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhPercent
  },
  nav: {
    fontFamily: fonts.control,
    fontSize: tokens.fsNav,
    fontWeight: '500',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhNav
  },
  navTree: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsNav,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhNav
  },
  sidebar: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsNav,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhSidebar
  },
  tenant: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsBadge,
    fontWeight: '400',
    lineHeight: tokens.lhTenant
  },
  eyebrow: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsEyebrow,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsEyebrow,
    letterSpacing: tokens.lsEyebrow,
    textTransform: 'uppercase'
  },
  tab: {
    fontFamily: fonts.control,
    fontSize: tokens.fsNav,
    fontWeight: '500',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsNav
  },
  control: {
    fontFamily: fonts.control,
    fontSize: tokens.fsSmall,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsSmall
  },
  segment: {
    fontFamily: fonts.control,
    fontSize: tokens.fsSmall,
    fontWeight: '500',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsSmall
  },
  badge: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsBadge,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsBadge
  },
  tag: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsTag,
    fontWeight: '500',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsTag
  },
  chip: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsCaption,
    fontWeight: '500',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsCaption
  },
  micro: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsMicro,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsMicro
  },
  avatarLg: {
    fontFamily: fonts.ui,
    fontSize: tokens.fsTag,
    fontWeight: '600',
    lineHeight: tokens.fsTag
  }
})

// Text colors. Status-colored text takes the `text` of the color group through status.ts, never reading the token directly (spec
// 5.1). The table of the plan lists only criticalText (the rising number, the alert tile) and waitingText (the freshness of stale
// data); the other five names (good, serious, running, review, neutral) are present because Chip and CountBadge color their text
// with STATUS[tone].text through Text itself, so all seven groups have their full names `<group>Text`.
export const tones = StyleSheet.create({
  text: { color: tokens.text },
  muted: { color: tokens.muted },
  accent: { color: tokens.accent },
  white: { color: tokens.white },
  violet: { color: tokens.violet },
  goodText: { color: STATUS.good.text },
  waitingText: { color: STATUS.waiting.text },
  seriousText: { color: STATUS.serious.text },
  criticalText: { color: STATUS.critical.text },
  runningText: { color: STATUS.running.text },
  reviewText: { color: STATUS.review.text },
  neutralText: { color: STATUS.neutral.text }
})

// A weight that overrides the weight of the variant.
const weights = StyleSheet.create({
  '400': { fontWeight: '400' },
  '500': { fontWeight: '500' },
  '600': { fontWeight: '600' }
})

// Digits of the same width (wireframe.css:65-66).
const numerals = StyleSheet.create({ tabular: { fontVariant: ['tabular-nums'] } })

export type TextVariant = keyof typeof variants
export type TextTone = keyof typeof tones
export type TextWeight = keyof typeof weights

// The style of one piece of text: variant, color, then the overriding weight and same-width digits if any. The part that changes with
// data lives here so that Text.tsx has no style branch.
export const textStyle = (
  variant: TextVariant,
  tone: TextTone,
  weight: TextWeight | undefined,
  tabular: boolean | undefined
) => [
  variants[variant],
  tones[tone],
  weight === undefined ? null : weights[weight],
  tabular ? numerals.tabular : null
]
```

```tsx
import { Text } from 'react-native'

import { glyphStyle, type GlyphSize, type GlyphTone } from './Glyph.styles'

// The symbols of the wireframe, written as Unicode escapes (D-B20): text in the operating system font, not images.
const GLYPHS = {
  // Items of the sidebar and the navigation panel (shell.js:59-78)
  myFocus: '\u25CE',
  approvals: '\u2713',
  cockpit: '\u25D0',
  dashboard: '\u25A6',
  registry: '\u2630',
  roadmap: '\u21E5',
  capacity: '\u25EB',
  risk: '\u25B3',
  investment: '\u0024',
  scenarios: '\u21C4',
  steerco: '\u25A4',
  copilot: '\u2726',
  portfolio: '\u25A4',
  program: '\u25B8',
  project: '\u2261',
  frameworks: '\u25C7',
  templates: '\u29C9',
  settings: '\u2699',
  caret: '\u25BE',
  bell: '\u{1F514}',
  // Save state and the lock cell (wireframe.css:141, 293)
  saved: '\u2713',
  lock: '\u{1F512}',
  // RAG health level (wireframe.css:117)
  ragGreen: '\u25CF',
  ragAmber: '\u25B2',
  ragRed: '\u25A0',
  ragUnknown: '\u003F',
  // Data freshness (wireframe.css:299-302)
  freshFresh: '\u25CF',
  freshStale: '\u25B2',
  freshPartial: '\u25D0',
  freshUnknown: '\u003F',
  // Labels of the WBS item (wireframe.css:119-121)
  milestone: '\u25C6',
  checkpoint: '\u25CB',
  approvalGate: '\u25C7',
  inputRequired: '\u2198',
  riskRelated: '\u0021'
}

export type GlyphName = keyof typeof GLYPHS

type GlyphProps = {
  name: GlyphName
  size: GlyphSize
  tone: GlyphTone
  // With a label the symbol is a named image (WBS label, health level); without one it is decorative and hidden.
  label?: string
}

export function Glyph({ name, size, tone, label }: GlyphProps) {
  const decorative = label === undefined
  return (
    <Text
      role={decorative ? undefined : 'img'}
      aria-label={label}
      aria-hidden={decorative}
      style={glyphStyle(size, tone, name === 'riskRelated')}
    >
      {GLYPHS[name]}
    </Text>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Glyph.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { STATUS } from './status'
import { tones } from './Text.styles'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

// The five sizes of the symbol; the line height equals the font size itself (line-height 1 of the wireframe).
const sizes = StyleSheet.create({
  dot: { fontSize: tokens.fsDot, lineHeight: tokens.fsDot },
  badge: { fontSize: tokens.fsBadge, lineHeight: tokens.fsBadge },
  caption: { fontSize: tokens.fsCaption, lineHeight: tokens.fsCaption },
  tag: { fontSize: tokens.fsTag, lineHeight: tokens.fsTag },
  body: { fontSize: tokens.fsBody, lineHeight: tokens.fsBody }
})

// Colors: the twelve colors of Text, plus four status colors (fill colors, through status.ts) and ink.
const colors = StyleSheet.create({
  ...tones,
  good: { color: STATUS.good.fill },
  waiting: { color: STATUS.waiting.fill },
  running: { color: STATUS.running.fill },
  critical: { color: STATUS.critical.fill },
  ink: { color: tokens.ink }
})

// Weight 600; only the exclamation mark of the risk declares 700 at css:121 (drawn as 600, D-B24).
const weights = StyleSheet.create({
  regular: { fontWeight: '600' },
  heavy: { fontWeight: '700' }
})

export type GlyphSize = keyof typeof sizes
export type GlyphTone = keyof typeof colors

export const glyphStyle = (size: GlyphSize, tone: GlyphTone, heavy: boolean) => [
  sizes[size],
  colors[tone],
  heavy ? weights.heavy : weights.regular
]
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

// The symbols of the wireframe (shell.js:59-78, wireframe.css:117-121 and 299-302). Compared by the Unicode code written
// in the \u form, not by copying the character, so that a character deformed by copying does not slip past the test.
const GLYPHS: [GlyphName, string][] = [
  ['myFocus', '\u25CE'],
  ['approvals', '\u2713'],
  ['cockpit', '\u25D0'],

  ['freshUnknown', '\u003F'],
  ['milestone', '\u25C6'],
  ['checkpoint', '\u25CB'],
  ['approvalGate', '\u25C7'],
  ['inputRequired', '\u2198'],
  ['riskRelated', '\u0021']
]

// Five sizes: the font size is a token, the line height equals that same size.

  ['dot', tokens.fsDot],
  ['badge', tokens.fsBadge],
  ['caption', tokens.fsCaption],
  ['tag', tokens.fsTag],
  ['body', tokens.fsBody]
] as const

// Seventeen colors: the twelve colors of Text, four status colors (fill colors) and ink.
const TONES = [
  ['text', tokens.text],
  ['muted', tokens.muted],
  ['accent', tokens.accent],
  ['criticalText', tokens.criticalText],
  ['waitingText', tokens.waitingText],

  ['good', tokens.good],

  ['ink', tokens.ink]
] as const

// Characters used by the tests of size, color and weight: the down arrow of the select box (U+25BE), the solid
// diamond of the milestone (U+25C6), the exclamation mark of the risk (U+0021), the solid square of the red level (U+25A0).
const CARET = '\u25BE'
const MILESTONE = '\u25C6'
const BANG = '\u0021'
const SQUARE = '\u25A0'

test.each(GLYPHS)('%s draws the right character of the table', async (name, character) => {

  expect(screen.queryByRole('img', { includeHiddenElements: true })).toBeNull()
```

```tsx
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { dot, frame } from './Chip.styles'
import type { StatusTone } from './status'
import { Text } from './Text'

// A Chip always has a dot and text, never color alone (wireframes/README.md:36). The text takes the `text` color of
// the status group: the tone `<group>Text` of Text.
export function Chip({ children, tone }: { children: string; tone: StatusTone }) {
  return (
    <View style={frame(tone)}>
      <View style={dot(tone)} />
      <Text variant="chip" tone={`${tone}Text` as const}>
        {children}
      </Text>
    </View>
  )
}
```

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { STATUS, type StatusTone } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // A pill of height chipH (css:104): the dot then the text on one row.
  chip: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space6,
    height: tokens.chipH,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space9,
    borderRadius: tokens.radiusPill
  },
  dot: { width: tokens.dot, height: tokens.dot, borderRadius: tokens.radiusPill }
})

// The background color and the dot color change with the status group, taken through status.ts (css:105-112).
export const frame = (tone: StatusTone) => [styles.chip, { backgroundColor: STATUS[tone].bg }]
export const dot = (tone: StatusTone) => [styles.dot, { backgroundColor: STATUS[tone].fill }]
```

```tsx
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { frames } from './Avatar.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

// The initials of each size: micro for the small size, avatarLg for the large size.
const INITIALS = { sm: 'micro', lg: 'avatarLg' } as const

// A named image: the screen reader reads `name`, not the initials. `accessible` merges the child elements
// into one object on iOS and Android (on the web this attribute has no effect).
export function Avatar({
  initials,
  name,
  size
}: {
  initials: string
  name: string
  size: 'sm' | 'lg'
}) {
  return (
    <View role="img" aria-label={name} accessible style={frames[size]}>
      <Text variant={INITIALS[size]} tone="violet">
        {initials}
      </Text>
    </View>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Button.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Pressable } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { frames } from './Button.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

// The text color of each variant: the solid button has white text, the outlined button has regular text, the bare button has gray text.
const TONE = { primary: 'white', secondary: 'text', ghost: 'muted' } as const

type ButtonProps = {
  label: string
  variant: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost'
  // With href it is a link, otherwise it is a button that calls onPress.
  href?: Route
  onPress?: () => void
  // Toggle button: aria-pressed follows this value; when left out it is not a toggle button.
  pressed?: boolean
  testID?: string
}

export function Button({ label, variant, href, onPress, pressed, testID }: ButtonProps) {
  const button = (
    <Pressable
      role={href === undefined ? 'button' : 'link'}
      aria-pressed={pressed}
      onPress={onPress}
      testID={testID}
      style={frames[variant]}
    >
      <Text variant="control" tone={TONE[variant]}>
        {label}
      </Text>
    </Pressable>
  )
  return href === undefined ? (
    button
  ) : (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      {button}
    </Link>
  )
}
```

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

// The sm size of css:124-130: every button of the frame and of screen 24 is this size.
const base: ViewStyle = {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  alignItems: 'center',
  gap: tokens.space6,
  paddingVertical: tokens.space6,
  paddingHorizontal: tokens.space10,
  borderRadius: tokens.radius,
  borderWidth: 1
}

// The style of a Pressable inside Link asChild must be an object, not an array (the Slot of expo-router
// merges the style of Link into it), so each variant is a complete object.
export const frames = StyleSheet.create({
  primary: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.ink, borderColor: 'transparent' },
  secondary: { ...base, backgroundColor: tokens.surface, borderColor: tokens.lineStrong },
  ghost: { ...base, backgroundColor: 'transparent', borderColor: 'transparent' }
})
```

`src/design-system/Button.test.native.tsx`:

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import { renderRouter } from 'expo-router/testing-library'
import type { ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { ROUTES, type Route } from '../core/routes'
import { Button } from './Button'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

// Three variants (css:124-130, size sm): background, border and text color. `transparent` means no border and no background.
const VARIANTS: ['primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost', ViewStyle, string][] = [
  ['primary', { backgroundColor: tokens.ink, borderColor: 'transparent' }, tokens.white],
  ['secondary', { backgroundColor: tokens.surface, borderColor: tokens.lineStrong }, tokens.text],
  ['ghost', { backgroundColor: 'transparent', borderColor: 'transparent' }, tokens.muted]
]

// renderRouter turns on the fake timers of Jest and does not turn them off. Under Stryker every project runs the jsdom environment,
// which has no setImmediate, so the automatic cleanup of RNTL (flushMicroTasks) falls back to the current
// setTimeout, that is the one of the fake timers, and hangs until the 5 seconds run out. The afterEach of the nested block runs before the afterEach of the
// outer block, so the real timers are restored before that cleanup.
describe('link', () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    jest.useRealTimers()
  })

  test('a Button with href is a link: pressing it goes to the path of the route', async () => {
    const route: Route = {
      pathname: ROUTES.changeRequest,
      params: { workspaceId: 'creative-studio', projectId: 'meridian-cgi-campaign' }
    }
    const router = renderRouter({
      index: () => <Button label="Raise change request" variant="primary" href={route} />,
      'w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/changes/new': () => null
    })
    await router

    const link = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Raise change request' })
    expect(link).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: tokens.ink, paddingHorizontal: tokens.space10 })
    expect(screen.getByText('Raise change request')).toHaveStyle({
      color: tokens.white,
      fontFamily: 'Manrope',
      fontWeight: '600'
    })
    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe('/')

    await fireEvent.press(link)

    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe(
      '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/changes/new'
    )
  })
})

test.each(VARIANTS)('variant %s: background, border and text color', async (variant, frame, color) => {
  await render(<Button label="Share" variant={variant} onPress={jest.fn()} />)

  const button = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Share' })
  expect(button).toHaveStyle({
    ...frame,
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space6,
    paddingVertical: tokens.space6,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space10,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius,
    borderWidth: 1
  })
  expect(screen.getByText('Share')).toHaveStyle({
    color,
    fontFamily: 'Manrope',
    fontSize: tokens.fsSmall,
    fontWeight: '600'
  })
})

test('a Button without href is a button: pressing it calls onPress once, aria-pressed follows pressed', async () => {
  const onPress = jest.fn()
  const { rerender } = await render(
    <Button label="Table view" variant="ghost" onPress={onPress} pressed={false} />
  )

  const button = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Table view' })
  expect(button).toHaveProp('aria-pressed', false)
  await fireEvent.press(button)
  expect(onPress).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)

  await rerender(<Button label="Table view" variant="ghost" onPress={onPress} pressed />)

  expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Table view' })).toHaveProp('aria-pressed', true)
})

test('a button that is not a toggle button has no aria-pressed, testID follows the prop', async () => {
  await render(<Button label="Share" variant="secondary" onPress={jest.fn()} testID="share" />)

  const button = screen.getByTestId('share')
  expect(button.props['aria-pressed']).toBeUndefined()
  expect(screen.queryByRole('link')).toBeNull()
})
```

`src/design-system/Select.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Picker } from '@react-native-picker/picker'

import { styles } from './Select.styles'

type SelectProps = {
  // Label for screen readers ("Language").
  label: string
  value: string
  options: { value: string; label: string }[]
  onChange: (value: string) => void
  testID?: string
}

// The native picker of the platform: a select element on the web, the picker of the operating system on iOS and Android (D-B5).
export function Select({ label, value, options, onChange, testID }: SelectProps) {
  return (
    <Picker
      accessibilityLabel={label}
      selectedValue={value}
      onValueChange={(next) => onChange(String(next))}
      // The type of the package declares `testID?: string` so it does not accept undefined when
      // exactOptionalPropertyTypes is on; at run time React Native ignores a testID with no value.
      testID={testID as string}
      style={styles.select}
    >
      {options.map((option) => (
        <Picker.Item key={option.value} label={option.label} value={option.value} />
      ))}
    </Picker>
  )
}
```

```ts
  // The select box on the top bar (spec 5.3, D-B17). The frame is used for all three platforms; the text (color, fontFamily,
  // fontSize) has an effect on the select element of the web, while on iOS and Android the native picker draws its own text.
  select: {
    height: tokens.iconBtn,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space6,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: tokens.lineStrong,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius,
    backgroundColor: tokens.surface,
    color: tokens.text,

  }
})
```

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react-native'

import { Select } from './Select'

const OPTIONS = [
  { value: 'en', label: 'English' },
  { value: 'vi', label: 'Tieng Viet' }
]

// RNTL renders the picker as RNCPicker on iOS (selectedIndex) and RNCAndroidDialogPicker on Android
// (selected); both receive an `items` list with labels.
const selectedIndexOf = (props: Record<string, unknown>) => props.selectedIndex ?? props.selected
const labelsOf = (props: Record<string, unknown>) =>
  (props.items as { label: string }[]).map((item) => item.label)

test('Select has a label, each choice is an item, the selected item follows value', async () => {
  const { rerender } = await render(
    <Select label="Language" value="en" options={OPTIONS} onChange={jest.fn()} testID="language" />
  )

  const select = screen.getByLabelText('Language')
  expect(labelsOf(select.props)).toEqual(['English', 'Tieng Viet'])
  expect(selectedIndexOf(select.props)).toBe(0)

  await rerender(
    <Select label="Language" value="vi" options={OPTIONS} onChange={jest.fn()} testID="language" />
  )

  expect(selectedIndexOf(screen.getByLabelText('Language').props)).toBe(1)
})

test('choosing an item calls onChange with the value of that item, once', async () => {
  const onChange = jest.fn()
  await render(
    <Select label="Language" value="en" options={OPTIONS} onChange={onChange} testID="language" />
  )

  await fireEvent(screen.getByTestId('language'), 'valueChange', 'vi', 1)

  expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
  expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith('vi')
})

test('the native value sent up always becomes a string', async () => {
  const onChange = jest.fn()
  await render(
    <Select label="Language" value="en" options={OPTIONS} onChange={onChange} testID="language" />
  )

  await fireEvent(screen.getByTestId('language'), 'valueChange', 2, 1)

  expect(onChange).toHaveBeenCalledWith('2')
})

test('without a testID the picker can still be found by its label', async () => {
  await render(<Select label="Language" value="en" options={OPTIONS} onChange={jest.fn()} />)

  expect(screen.getByLabelText('Language')).toBeOnTheScreen()
})
```

Five places differ from the table in the steps above and the review accepted them. One: `TextTone` has 12 names, not seven
(`Chip` and `CountBadge` need five more text colors). Two: `Spinner.styles.ts` keeps only one color constant
(`spinnerColor`), because `ActivityIndicator` takes its color through the prop `color`, not through style. Three:
`Select.tsx` casts `testID as string`, because the type of the picker declares `testID?: string` while
`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` does not accept `undefined`. Four: `Text` always passes `ellipsizeMode="tail"`,
not only when there is `lines`. Five: `Button.test.native.tsx` nests a `describe` with
`afterEach(jest.useRealTimers)`, which runs before the cleanup of RNTL, because `renderRouter` turns on fake timers
and the Stryker run has no `setImmediate`, so the automatic cleanup hangs for 5 seconds on every
test.

Lane (a), after Task 5. A UI task under R-B12: the plan gives the names, props, structure, tokens and the test

The general rules of Task 5, applied in full to every component of this task: style only in `X.styles.ts`

| Segmented with "This project" selected, "My items" not | `getByLabelText('Scope')` has the prop `role` equal to `'tablist'`; `getByRole('tab', { name: 'This project', selected: true })` background `tokens.ink`, text `tokens.white`; `My items` not selected, text `tokens.muted`, no right border |
| Menu with two workspaces, Creative Studio current | `getByLabelText('Workspaces')` has the prop `role` equal to `'menu'`; two `menuitem`; the current item has background `tokens.accentSoft` and the prop `aria-current` equal to `'true'`; the other item has no background and `props['aria-current']` is `undefined` (read the value, because `toHaveProp(name)` only asks whether the key exists, while `aria-current={undefined}` still leaves the key) |

The three containers (`Segmented` and `Menu` in the table above, `Dialog` in Step 4) are found with `getByLabelText`
and then the `role` prop is asserted, not with `getByRole`. Reason: the `*ByRole` of RNTL matches only accessibility
elements, and a `View` is an element of that kind only when it has the prop `accessible` [Source: RNTL documentation,
section ByRole, oss.callstack.com/react-native-testing-library/docs/api/queries]; measured: a `View` with
`role` but without `accessible` is not found by `getByRole`, but is found by `getByLabelText`. Do not put
`accessible` on the container, because on iOS this prop becomes `isAccessibilityElement` and VoiceOver does not
allow nested accessibility elements, so the tabs, menu items and buttons of the dialog inside would not be
selected separately [Source: reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility, section `accessible`]. The `tab`,
`menuitem` and `link` are still found with `getByRole`, because `Pressable` has `accessible` built in.

#### Real code after the review

The full code of 45 files, copied byte for byte after the review (R-B12): the steps above give the structure, props, tokens
and the table of checks, while the code that was run is in the blocks below, each block being a whole file.

`src/design-system/Card.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { bodyStyle, styles } from './Card.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

type CardProps = {
  title: string
  // Count chip, caption or dimmed button at the end of the card head.
  aside?: ReactNode
  // List card: the body has no padding.
  flush?: boolean
  children: ReactNode
  testID?: string
}

export function Card({ title, aside, flush, children, testID }: CardProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.frame} testID={testID}>
      <View style={styles.head}>
        <View style={styles.title}>
          <Text variant="cardTitle" heading={3}>
            {title}
          </Text>
        </View>
        {aside}
      </View>
      <View style={bodyStyle(flush)}>{children}</View>
    </View>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Card.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Card frame (css:85): raised background, border 1, corners rounded by radius. flex 1 so cards in the same row share the width equally.
  frame: {
    flex: 1,
    backgroundColor: tokens.surface,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: tokens.line,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius
  },
  // Card head (css:86): the title and then the aside part on one row, bottom border.
  head: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space10,
    paddingVertical: tokens.space12,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.gap,
    borderBottomWidth: 1,
    borderBottomColor: tokens.line
  },
  // Text does not accept style, so the remaining space of the title (css:87) is on the frame wrapping it.
  title: { flex: 1 },
  // Card body (css:88).
  body: { padding: tokens.gap }
})

// List card (flush): each row has its own horizontal padding, so the body has no padding (css:168).
export const bodyStyle = (flush: boolean | undefined) => (flush ? null : styles.body)
```

`src/design-system/Tile.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { Text } from './Text'
import { frame, styles } from './Tile.styles'

type TileProps = {
  label: string
  value: string
  // A number is drawn at figure size; text (for example "Not baselined") is drawn at body size, bold, gray.
  figure: boolean
  // The secondary line is made of parts: the `bad` part is painted bold red (css:98), the `muted` part keeps the gray color of the line.
  delta: { text: string; tone: 'muted' | 'bad' }[]
  // Highlighted tile: border and number in the critical color.
  alert: boolean
  href: Route
  testID: string
}

// Do not set numberOfLines: long text (Vietnamese) wraps to the next line instead of being cut off.
export function Tile({ label, value, figure, delta, alert, href, testID }: TileProps) {
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable role="link" testID={testID} style={frame(alert)}>
        <Text variant="small" tone="muted">
          {label}
        </Text>
        <View style={styles.value}>
          {figure ? (
            <Text variant="figure" tone={alert ? 'criticalText' : 'text'}>
              {value}
            </Text>
          ) : (
            <Text variant="body" weight="600" tone="muted">
              {value}
            </Text>
          )}
        </View>
        {delta.length > 0 ? (
          <View style={styles.delta}>
            <Text variant="caption" tone="muted">
              {delta.map((part, index) =>
                part.tone === 'bad' ? (
                  <Text key={index} variant="caption" tone="criticalText" weight="600">
                    {part.text}
                  </Text>
                ) : (
                  part.text
                )
              )}
            </Text>
          </View>
        ) : null}
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Tile.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { STATUS } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

// Metric tile frame (css:94, 85): a card with padding 12 x 14, sharing the row width equally and able to shrink all the way.
const base: ViewStyle = {
  flex: 1,
  minWidth: 0,
  paddingVertical: tokens.space12,
  paddingHorizontal: tokens.gap,
  backgroundColor: tokens.surface,
  borderWidth: 1,
  borderRadius: tokens.radius
}

// A Pressable inside Link asChild must have a style that is an object, not an array (the Slot of expo-router
// merges the style of Link into it), so each variant is a complete object. The highlighted tile has a border in the critical color
// (css:100), taken through status.ts.
const frames = StyleSheet.create({
  normal: { ...base, borderColor: tokens.line },
  alert: { ...base, borderColor: STATUS.critical.fill }
})

export const frame = (alert: boolean) => (alert ? frames.alert : frames.normal)

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // The value sits 4 below the label (css:96); the secondary line sits 2 below the value (css:97).
  value: { marginTop: tokens.space4 },
  delta: { marginTop: tokens.space2 }
})
```

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render, screen, within } from '@testing-library/react-native'

}

// renderRouter turns on the fake timers of Jest and does not turn them off. Under Stryker every project runs the jsdom environment,
// which has no setImmediate, so the automatic cleanup of RNTL (flushMicroTasks) falls back to the setTimeout in
// effect, that is the one of the fake timers, and hangs until the 5 seconds are over. The afterEach of the nested block runs before the afterEach of
// the outer block, so the real timers are given back before that cleanup.
describe('links', () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    jest.useRealTimers()
  })

          alert={false}
          href={FOCUS}
          testID="tile-blocked"
        />

      'w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/focus': () => null
    })
    await router

    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe('/')

    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe('/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/focus')

})
```

`src/design-system/Meter.tsx`:

```tsx
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { done, rest, styles } from './Meter.styles'

// value is the integer percentage that the model already rounded down (FE-20): the component does not multiply and does not
// round. `accessible` makes the bar one object with a name and a value for the screen reader (on web
// this attribute has no effect), and lets RNTL find it by role.
export function Meter({ value, label }: { value: number; label: string }) {
  return (
    <View
      accessible
      role="progressbar"
      aria-label={label}
      aria-valuemin={0}
      aria-valuemax={100}
      aria-valuenow={value}
      style={styles.track}
    >
      <View style={done(value)} />
      <View style={rest(value)} />
    </View>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Meter.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { STATUS } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Track (css:181): a bar rounded at both ends, clipping the done part to the track.
  track: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    height: tokens.meterH,
    backgroundColor: tokens.line,
    borderRadius: tokens.radiusPill,
    overflow: 'hidden'
  },
  // Done part (css:182), green through status.ts.
  done: { backgroundColor: STATUS.good.fill, borderRadius: tokens.radiusPill }
})

// value is the integer percentage from 0 to 100: the done part and the rest share the track by flexGrow.
export const done = (value: number) => [styles.done, { flexGrow: value }]
export const rest = (value: number) => ({ flexGrow: 100 - value })
```

`src/design-system/StackBar.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { segment, styles } from './StackBar.styles'
import type { WorkStatus } from './status'

type StackBarProps = {
  // Each segment is a link that drills down into the filtered WBS list; weight is the relative width.
  segments: { status: WorkStatus; weight: number; href: Route; label: string; testID: string }[]
}

export function StackBar({ segments }: StackBarProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.bar}>
      {segments.map((item, index) => (
        <Link key={item.testID} href={item.href} asChild>
          <Pressable
            role="link"
            aria-label={item.label}
            testID={item.testID}
            style={segment(item.status, item.weight, index, segments.length)}
          />
        </Link>
      ))}
    </View>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/StackBar.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { WORK_FILL, type WorkStatus } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Stacked bar (css:191): the segments sit side by side, 2 apart.
  bar: { flexDirection: 'row', height: tokens.barH, gap: tokens.space2 },
  // Every segment starts from width 0 and then they share the free space by flexGrow (css:192).
  segment: { flexBasis: 0 },
  first: { borderTopLeftRadius: tokens.radiusSm, borderBottomLeftRadius: tokens.radiusSm },
  last: { borderTopRightRadius: tokens.radiusSm, borderBottomRightRadius: tokens.radiusSm }
})

// One segment of the bar (shared by StackBar and BarTrack, css:193 and 187-189): the fill color comes from the table
// WORK_FILL of status.ts; the first segment rounds its two left corners, the last segment rounds its two right corners, the only segment rounds all
// four. A Pressable inside Link asChild must have a style that is an object, not an array (the Slot of
// expo-router merges the style of Link into it), so the result is flattened.
export const segment = (status: WorkStatus, weight: number, index: number, count: number) =>
  StyleSheet.flatten<ViewStyle>([
    styles.segment,
    { flexGrow: weight, backgroundColor: WORK_FILL[status] },
    index === 0 && styles.first,
    index === count - 1 && styles.last
  ])
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'

import { ROUTES, type Route } from '../core/routes'
import { StackBar } from './StackBar'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

// The drill-down filter goes into the query parameters (spec 4.3).
const wbs = (status: string): Route => ({
  pathname: ROUTES.wbs,
  params: { workspaceId: 'creative-studio', projectId: 'meridian-cgi-campaign', status }
})

// The four segments of Meridian: Blocked 0 has no segment (the model already filtered it).
const MERIDIAN: ComponentProps<typeof StackBar>['segments'] = [
  { status: 'done', weight: 3, href: wbs('done'), label: 'Done 3', testID: 'status-done' },
  {
    status: 'inProgress',
    weight: 3,
    href: wbs('inProgress'),
    label: 'In Progress 3',
    testID: 'status-inProgress'
  },
  {
    status: 'waiting',
    weight: 1,
    href: wbs('waiting'),
    label: 'Waiting 1',
    testID: 'status-waiting'
  },
  {
    status: 'notStarted',
    weight: 5,
    href: wbs('notStarted'),
    label: 'Not Started 5',
    testID: 'status-notStarted'
  }
]

// Each segment: name, testID, flexGrow, fill color taken from the WORK_FILL table (done is good, inProgress is
// running, waiting is waiting, notStarted is neutralFill).
const SEGMENTS = [
  ['Done 3', 'status-done', 3, tokens.good],
  ['In Progress 3', 'status-inProgress', 3, tokens.running],
  ['Waiting 1', 'status-waiting', 1, tokens.waiting],
  ['Not Started 5', 'status-notStarted', 5, tokens.neutralFill]
] as const

// Corner rounding of a segment: toHaveStyle with undefined asserts that the corner has no rounding.
const round = tokens.radiusSm
const NONE = {
  borderTopLeftRadius: undefined,
  borderBottomLeftRadius: undefined,
  borderTopRightRadius: undefined,
  borderBottomRightRadius: undefined
}
const LEFT = { ...NONE, borderTopLeftRadius: round, borderBottomLeftRadius: round }
const RIGHT = { ...NONE, borderTopRightRadius: round, borderBottomRightRadius: round }
const ALL = {
  borderTopLeftRadius: round,
  borderBottomLeftRadius: round,
  borderTopRightRadius: round,
  borderBottomRightRadius: round
}

test('StackBar: a one-row bar of height barH, segments spaced space2 apart', async () => {
  await render(<StackBar segments={MERIDIAN} />)

  expect(screen.root).toHaveStyle({
    flexDirection: 'row',
    height: tokens.barH,
    gap: tokens.space2
  })
})

test('StackBar four segments of Meridian: four links in order', async () => {
  await render(<StackBar segments={MERIDIAN} />)

  expect(screen.getAllByRole('link').map((link) => link.props.testID)).toEqual([
    'status-done',
    'status-inProgress',
    'status-waiting',
    'status-notStarted'
  ])
})

test.each(SEGMENTS)(
  'segment %s: testID %s, flexGrow %s, flexBasis 0, fill color %s',
  async (name, testID, grow, fill) => {
    await render(<StackBar segments={MERIDIAN} />)

    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name })).toHaveProp('testID', testID)
    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name })).toHaveStyle({
      flexGrow: grow,
      flexBasis: 0,
      backgroundColor: fill
    })
  }
)

test('each segment opens the exact path of its href, with the filter', async () => {
  await render(<StackBar segments={MERIDIAN} />)

  expect(screen.getByTestId('status-inProgress')).toHaveProp(
    'href',
    '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/wbs?status=inProgress'
  )
})

test('the first segment rounds its two left corners, the middle segments are not rounded, the last segment rounds its two right corners', async () => {
  await render(<StackBar segments={MERIDIAN} />)

  const [first, second, third, last] = screen.getAllByRole('link')
  expect(first).toHaveStyle(LEFT)
  expect(second).toHaveStyle(NONE)
  expect(third).toHaveStyle(NONE)
  expect(last).toHaveStyle(RIGHT)

test('StackBar one segment: the only segment rounds all four corners', async () => {
  await render(
    <StackBar
      segments={[
        { status: 'done', weight: 12, href: wbs('done'), label: 'Done 12', testID: 'status-done' }
      ]}
    />
  )

  expect(screen.getByRole('link')).toHaveStyle(ALL)
})
```

```tsx
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { styles, swatchFill } from './Legend.styles'
import type { WorkStatus } from './status'
import { Text } from './Text'

type LegendProps = {
  // Lists every status, including the 0 item, so the legend is complete even when the bar does not draw that segment.
  items: { status: WorkStatus; text: string }[]
}

export function Legend({ items }: LegendProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.legend}>
      {items.map((entry) => (
        <View key={entry.status} style={styles.item}>
          <View style={swatchFill(entry.status)} />
          <Text variant="caption" tone="muted">
            {entry.text}
          </Text>
        </View>
      ))}
    </View>
  )
}
```

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { WORK_FILL, type WorkStatus } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Legend (css:194): the items sit in one row, wrapping to the next line when space runs out.
  legend: { flexDirection: 'row', flexWrap: 'wrap', columnGap: tokens.gap, rowGap: tokens.gap },
  item: { flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center' },
  // Square color swatch (css:195).
  swatch: {
    width: tokens.swatch,
    height: tokens.swatch,
    borderRadius: tokens.radiusXs,
    marginRight: tokens.space6
  }
})

// The swatch color comes from WORK_FILL of status.ts, the same table as the stacked bar.
export const swatchFill = (status: WorkStatus) => [
  styles.swatch,
  { backgroundColor: WORK_FILL[status] }
]
```

```tsx
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { part, styles } from './BarTrack.styles'

type BarTrackProps = {
  // The model already filtered out the 0 segment (D-B14): the component draws exactly the segments it receives.
  segments: { tone: 'good' | 'neutral'; weight: number }[]
}

export function BarTrack({ segments }: BarTrackProps) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.track}>
      {segments.map((item, index) => (
        <View key={index} style={part(item.tone, item.weight, index, segments.length)} />
      ))}
    </View>
```

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { segment } from './StackBar.styles'
import type { WorkStatus } from './status'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Row bar (css:185): the same layout as the stacked bar.
  track: { flexDirection: 'row', height: tokens.barH, gap: tokens.space2 }
})

// The done part is filled like the done status, the rest like notStarted: the same WORK_FILL table as StackBar.
const STATUS_OF: Record<'good' | 'neutral', WorkStatus> = { good: 'done', neutral: 'notStarted' }

// Corner rounding and space sharing by flexGrow exactly like the segment of StackBar (css:186-189).
export const part = (tone: 'good' | 'neutral', weight: number, index: number, count: number) =>
  segment(STATUS_OF[tone], weight, index, count)
```

```tsx
import { bar, empty, styles } from './ShareBar.styles'

// share is a number from 0 to 1 computed by the model; the component does not compute it again.
export function ShareBar({ share }: { share: number }) {

    <View style={styles.track}>
```

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Workload bar per person (html:76-79): a row of height barH, the left bar and then the empty part.
  track: { flexDirection: 'row', height: tokens.barH },
  // The series1 color of the chart palette: ShareBar is a chart component so it may read it (spec 5.1).
  bar: { backgroundColor: tokens.series1, borderRadius: tokens.radiusSm }
})

// share is the part of the whole bar, from 0 to 1: the bar and the empty part share the row by flexGrow.
export const bar = (share: number) => [styles.bar, { flexGrow: share }]
export const empty = (share: number) => ({ flexGrow: 1 - share })
```

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Pressable, Text as NativeText, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { styles, valueText } from './BarRow.styles'

type BarRowProps = {
  // Label cell with a fixed width: text, or a row with an avatar.
  label: ReactNode
  value: string
  href: Route
  testID: string
  // The bar of the row (BarTrack, ShareBar), taking the remaining space.
  children: ReactNode
}

// The rows are stacked vertically space8 apart: that belongs to the block of the screen that places them.
export function BarRow({ label, value, href, testID, children }: BarRowProps) {
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable role="link" testID={testID} style={styles.row}>
        <View style={styles.label}>{label}</View>
        <View style={styles.bar}>{children}</View>
        <NativeText style={valueText}>{value}</NativeText>
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/BarRow.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { textStyle } from './Text.styles'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // One row of the bar block (css:184): label, bar and value on one row. It is the style of a Pressable
  // inside Link asChild so it must be an object, not an array.
  row: { flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', columnGap: tokens.space10 },
  label: { width: tokens.barLabelW },
  bar: { flex: 1 },
  // The value is right-aligned in a cell of width barValueW (css:190).
  value: { width: tokens.barValueW, textAlign: 'right' }
})

// The Text of the design system does not accept width and textAlign, so the value is the native Text of React Native carrying
// exactly the style of Text (small, gray, tabular digits) plus the two properties above.
export const valueText = [...textStyle('small', 'muted', undefined, true), styles.value]
```

`src/design-system/ListRow.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { Glyph } from './Glyph'
import { frame, styles } from './ListRow.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

// WBS label of an item: named the same as the glyph of the same name in Glyph (css:119-121).
export type WbsLabel = 'milestone' | 'checkpoint' | 'approvalGate' | 'inputRequired' | 'riskRelated'

// Glyph color of each label (css:119-121, style guide section 6 "WBS labels"). Checkpoint has no color of its own
// at css:119, so the glyph keeps the gray color of the label (css:118, `.lbl`).
const TONE: Record<WbsLabel, ComponentProps<typeof Glyph>['tone']> = {
  milestone: 'ink',
  checkpoint: 'muted',
  approvalGate: 'accent',
  inputRequired: 'waiting',
  riskRelated: 'critical'
}

type ListRowProps = {
  code: string
  // The same shape as rows[].labels of the model: text is the name of the label for screen readers.
  labels: { label: WbsLabel; text: string }[]
  name: string
  // The end of the row: number of days, risk level chip.
  trailing: ReactNode
  href: Route
  // The last row of a card has no bottom border.
  last: boolean
  testID: string
}

export function ListRow({ code, labels, name, trailing, href, last, testID }: ListRowProps) {
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable role="link" testID={testID} style={frame(last)}>
        <Text variant="body" tone="muted" tabular>
          {code}
        </Text>
        {labels.length > 0 ? (
          <View style={styles.labels}>
            {labels.map((item) => (
              <Glyph
                key={item.label}
                name={item.label}
                size="tag"
                tone={TONE[item.label]}
                label={item.text}
              />
            ))}
          </View>
        ) : null}
        <View style={styles.name}>
          <Text variant="body">{name}</Text>
        </View>
        {trailing}
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/ListRow.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

// Row of a list card (css:168): minimum height rowList, horizontal padding gap, separated by a bottom border.
const row: ViewStyle = {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  alignItems: 'center',
  gap: tokens.space10,
  minHeight: tokens.rowList,
  paddingHorizontal: tokens.gap,
  borderBottomColor: tokens.line
}

// A Pressable inside Link asChild must have a style that is an object, not an array (the Slot of expo-router
// merges the style of Link into it), so each variant is a complete object. The last row has no bottom border
// (css:169). ListNote shares this frame.
const frames = StyleSheet.create({
  between: { ...row, borderBottomWidth: 1 },
  last: { ...row, borderBottomWidth: 0 }
})

export const frame = (last: boolean) => (last ? frames.last : frames.between)

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // WBS label row (css:118): the glyphs are 4 apart.
  labels: { flexDirection: 'row', gap: tokens.space4 },
  // The name takes the remaining space and can shrink so that long text wraps to the next line (css:170).
  name: { flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }
})
```

```tsx
  ['inputRequired', '\u2198', tokens.waiting],
  ['riskRelated', '\u0021', tokens.critical]
]

// The solid diamond of the milestone, used in the first two checks.
const MILESTONE = '\u25C6'

const overdue = (days: string) => (
  <Text variant="small" tone="criticalText">
    {days}
```

`src/design-system/ListNote.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { frame, styles } from './ListNote.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

type ListNoteProps = {
  text: string
  // With href the sentence is a link ("+ 5 more · open in Focus"); without it, it is plain text (the sentence saying why it is empty).
  href?: Route
  // The last row of a card has no bottom border.
  last: boolean
  testID?: string
}

export function ListNote({ text, href, last, testID }: ListNoteProps) {
  const note = (
    <View style={styles.text}>
      <Text variant="small" tone="muted">
        {text}
      </Text>
    </View>
  )
  if (href === undefined) {
    return (
      <View testID={testID} style={frame(last)}>
        {note}
      </View>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable role="link" testID={testID} style={frame(last)}>
        {note}
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Segmented.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { cell, styles } from './Segmented.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

type SegmentedProps = {
  // The name of the group for screen readers ("Scope").
  label: string
  options: { label: string; href: Route; selected: boolean; testID: string }[]
}

// Each cell is a link: choosing a cell changes the path, not a state inside the component.
export function Segmented({ label, options }: SegmentedProps) {
  return (
    <View role="tablist" aria-label={label} style={styles.group}>
      {options.map((option, index) => (
        <Link key={option.testID} href={option.href} asChild>
          <Pressable
            role="tab"
            aria-selected={option.selected}
            testID={option.testID}
            style={cell(option.selected, index === options.length - 1)}
          >
            <Text variant="segment" tone={option.selected ? 'white' : 'muted'}>
              {option.label}
            </Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      ))}
    </View>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Segmented.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Group of choice buttons (css:148): outer border rounded by radius, clipping the corners of the choice cells, shrinking to its content.
  group: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignSelf: 'flex-start',
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: tokens.lineStrong,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius,
    overflow: 'hidden'
  },
  cell: { paddingVertical: tokens.space6, paddingHorizontal: tokens.space11 },
  // The selected cell has an ink background (css:151); every cell except the last has a divider on its right side (css:149-150).
  selected: { backgroundColor: tokens.ink },
  divider: { borderRightWidth: 1, borderRightColor: tokens.lineStrong }
})

// A Pressable inside Link asChild must have a style that is an object, not an array (the Slot of expo-router
// merges the style of Link into it), so the parts are flattened into one object.
export const cell = (selected: boolean, last: boolean) =>
  StyleSheet.flatten<ViewStyle>([styles.cell, selected && styles.selected, !last && styles.divider])
```

`src/design-system/Menu.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import type { Route } from '../core/routes'
import { entry, styles } from './Menu.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

type MenuProps = {
  // The name of the menu for screen readers ("Workspaces").
  label: string
  items: { label: string; href: Route; current: boolean; testID: string }[]
}

// Floating menu of the workspace picker: each item is a link to the screen of that workspace. The current item
// is marked with aria-current like the open items of the frame, not only by color (react-native-web
// prints this attribute into the DOM).
export function Menu({ label, items }: MenuProps) {
  return (
    <View role="menu" aria-label={label} style={styles.menu}>
      {items.map((item) => (
        <Link key={item.testID} href={item.href} asChild>
          <Pressable
            role="menuitem"
            aria-current={item.current ? 'true' : undefined}
            testID={item.testID}
            style={entry(item.current)}
          >
            <Text variant="sidebar" tone={item.current ? 'accent' : 'text'}>
              {item.label}
            </Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      ))}
    </View>
  )
}
```

`src/design-system/Menu.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Floating menu (D-B21, panel effect): placed absolutely right below the picker, as wide as the picker.
  menu: {
    position: 'absolute',
    top: '100%',
    left: 0,
    right: 0,
    zIndex: 1,
    backgroundColor: tokens.surface,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: tokens.line,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius,
    padding: tokens.space6,
    gap: tokens.space2
  },
  entry: {
    paddingVertical: tokens.space6,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space8,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius
  },
  current: { backgroundColor: tokens.accentSoft }
})

// A Pressable inside Link asChild must have a style that is an object, not an array (the Slot of expo-router
// merges the style of Link into it), so the parts are flattened into one object.
export const entry = (current: boolean) =>
  StyleSheet.flatten<ViewStyle>([styles.entry, current && styles.current])
```

`src/design-system/StatePanel.tsx`:

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Text as NativeText, View } from 'react-native'

import { Glyph, type GlyphName } from './Glyph'
import { sentenceText, styles } from './StatePanel.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

type StatePanelProps = {
  // Decorative glyph above the title (hidden from screen readers).
  glyph?: GlyphName
  title: string
  // The sentence saying why and what to do next.
  body: string
  // A button or text with the label "Not built yet"; null when there is no action.
  actions: ReactNode
  testID: string
}

// The state panel is the main content of an error page (an error page has no project page header), so its
// title is the level 1 heading of the page: screen reader users browse by heading and need an h1.
export function StatePanel({ glyph, title, body, actions, testID }: StatePanelProps) {
  return (
    <View testID={testID} style={styles.panel}>
      {glyph === undefined ? null : <Glyph name={glyph} size="body" tone="muted" />}
      <Text variant="pageTitle" heading={1}>
        {title}
      </Text>
      <NativeText style={sentenceText}>{body}</NativeText>
      <View style={styles.actions}>{actions}</View>
    </View>
  )
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 14): the title is `heading={1}`, not
`heading={2}`, with a comment. Error pages (403, 404, failed to load, wrong data) have no project page
header, so the state panel is the main content of the page and its title is the level 1 heading: people
who use screen readers browse by heading and need an `h1`, and the row "every link of the frame opens a page with a
heading" of Task 14 demands exactly one per destination. Level 2 of the original plan was written for a panel inside a
page. `StatePanel` is used only by the `StateView` of screen 24, so nothing else changes.

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { textStyle } from './Text.styles'
import { tokens } from './tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // State of the screen (wireframes/screens/43-access-states.html:40-47): a centered column.
  panel: {
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space8,
    paddingVertical: tokens.pagePad,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.pagePad
  },
  // Action row: the buttons wrap to the next line when space runs out, centered.
  actions: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    flexWrap: 'wrap',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space8
  },
  // A multi-line explanatory sentence is centered line by line.
  sentence: { textAlign: 'center' }
})

// The design system's Text does not accept textAlign, so the sentence is React Native's own Text carrying exactly the style
// of Text (small, gray) plus textAlign.
export const sentenceText = [...textStyle('small', 'muted', undefined, undefined), styles.sentence]
```

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { styles } from './Dialog.styles'
import { Text } from './Text'

type DialogProps = {
  title: string
  children: ReactNode
  testID: string
}

// The dialog covers the frame that contains it (the frame must be the positioning anchor of the overlay). The box does not set
// `accessible`: it holds buttons and text, and a screen reader must be able to reach every part.
export function Dialog({ title, children, testID }: DialogProps) {
  return (
    <View testID={testID} style={styles.overlay}>
      <View style={styles.scrim} />
      <View role="dialog" aria-modal aria-label={title} style={styles.box}>
        <Text variant="pageTitle" heading={2}>
          {title}
        </Text>
        {children}
      </View>
    </View>
  )
}
```

Six places that differ from the table in the steps above, which the review accepted. One: the container frame of `Segmented`, `Menu` and
`Dialog` is found with `getByLabelText` and then the `role` prop is asserted, not with `getByRole` (the reason is in the note
after the table of tests of Step 3). Two: `Meter` sets `accessible`, because `getByRole('progressbar')` needs
it and because assistive technology needs a single object that carries the name and the value of the bar; unlike the three
containers above, inside the bar there is no interactive element to be hidden. On the web this prop has
no effect (measured: the DOM has no `accessible` attribute). Three: the value of `BarRow` and the sentence of
`StatePanel` use react-native's `Text` with `textStyle(...)` plus `width` or `textAlign`, because
the design system's `Text` has no `style` prop. Four: a few wrapping `View`s carry `flex` or `margin` where
the table puts them on `Text` (the title of `Card`, the value and sub-line of `Tile`, the name of `ListRow`,
the sentence of `ListNote`), with the same layout. Five: `ListRow` drops the label row when `labels` is empty, because an
empty row still takes up an extra `gap: space10` in the row. Six: every child of `Link asChild` receives exactly
one style object, never an array, because expo-router's `Slot` throws an error when the child's style is an
array, and that check runs in dev mode [Source: expo-router, ui/Slot, the check of `NODE_ENV` other than
`production`, in the installed copy it is `node_modules/expo-router/build/ui/Slot.js:62-63`]; where the style changes with
data, the function in the style file returns `StyleSheet.flatten<ViewStyle>([...])` or picks one of two
prebuilt objects.

The fix round after the review changed three places of the first submission, and the tables above follow the fixed version. One: the
`checkpoint` label of `ListRow` changes from `waiting` to `muted`, because css:119 sets no color for
`.lbl.cp::before`, so the symbol keeps the gray of `.lbl` at css:118 (the five-label `test.each` test changes
along with it: `tokens.muted`). Two: the current item of `Menu` carries `aria-current="true"` and the other items do not
have this prop; the test reads `props['aria-current']` of the other item, because `toHaveProp(name)` only asks whether the key
exists, whereas `aria-current={undefined}` still leaves the key behind. These two tests are red on the old code (ListRow 2
out of 20 runs, Menu 2 out of 6) and green after the fix. Three: the note in `StatePanel.styles.ts` cites
`wireframes/screens/43-access-states.html:40-47` (the centered frame), not `:28-37`.

Android, the service worker on the web).

- Create: `apps/metis/src/platform/config.ts`, `config.test.ts`

- Create: `apps/metis/src/platform/mocks.ts`, `mocks.web.ts`, `mocks.test.native.ts`, `mocks.test.web.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `getOverview`, `getShell`, `ApiConfig` (Task 4); `creativeStudio`, `digitalProducts`,

- Produces, from `src/mocks/handlers.ts`: `SCENARIOS` (`'default' | 'loading' | 'sessionExpired' |
  'serverError' | 'invalidData' | 'partial' | 'unknown'`), `type Scenario`,
  `scenarioOf(value: string | null): Scenario`, `handlersFor(scenario: Scenario)` (the handlers of

  (web: `localStorage` key `metis.locale` and the `lang` attribute of the page; iOS and Android: always
  English, nothing saved).
- Produces, from `src/platform/mocks`: `startMocks(): Promise<void>` (only when `EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS ===
  '1'`; the web picks the scenario by the `?mock=` of the page at load time); `src/platform/mocks.ts` alone (iOS,
  Android) exports in addition `defineMissingEventClasses(scope: Record<string, unknown>): string[]`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the red tests of the scripted mock server**

Replace the whole of `src/mocks/handlers.test.ts` with:

```ts
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node'

import { getOverview, getShell } from '../core/api/client'
import { meridian } from './fixtures/meridian'
import { creativeStudio, digitalProducts } from './fixtures/shell'
import { showroom } from './fixtures/showroom'
import { handlersFor, type Scenario, SCENARIOS, scenarioOf } from './handlers'

const config = { baseUrl: 'https://api.metis.test', timeoutMs: 2000 }
const server = setupServer()

beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }))
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers())
afterAll(() => server.close())

const serve = (scenario: Scenario) => server.use(...handlersFor(scenario))
const meridianOf = (scenario: Scenario, timeoutMs = 2000) => {
  serve(scenario)
  return getOverview(
    { ...config, timeoutMs },
    'creative-studio',
    'meridian-cgi-campaign',
    'project'
  )
}

test('the shell of two workspaces, matching the contract; an unknown workspace returns 404', async () => {
  serve('default')
  expect(await getShell(config, 'creative-studio')).toEqual({ ok: true, data: creativeStudio })
  expect(await getShell(config, 'digital-products')).toEqual({ ok: true, data: digitalProducts })
  expect(await getShell(config, 'other-studio')).toEqual({
    ok: false,
    error: { kind: 'notFound' }
  })
})

test('Meridian and Showroom VR return mock data, matching the contract; My items returns the same data', async () => {
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the scripted mock server**

Replace the whole of `src/mocks/handlers.ts` with:

```ts
import { delay, http, HttpResponse } from 'msw'

import type { Overview } from '../core/api/overview'
import type { Shell } from '../core/api/shell'
import { meridian } from './fixtures/meridian'
import { creativeStudio, digitalProducts } from './fixtures/shell'
import { showroom } from './fixtures/showroom'

// The mock server of the shell and the overview screen (spec 3.4), shared by Jest, the web and the app. An address ending in
// .test never resolves, so only the mock server can answer.
const BASE = 'https://api.metis.test/workspaces/:workspaceId'
const WORKSPACE = 'creative-studio'
const shells = new Map<string, Shell>([
  ['creative-studio', creativeStudio],
  ['digital-products', digitalProducts]
])
// Three projects in the shell's tree: two projects with data, one project the mock user has no access to.
const overviews = new Map<string, Overview>([
  ['meridian-cgi-campaign', meridian],
  ['northwind-showroom-vr', showroom]
])
const FORBIDDEN = 'spring-catalogue-renders'

// Scenarios exist only in development (R-B3), chosen with ?mock=<name> in the page's path: they put the
// overview screen into states that the three mock projects do not have.
export const SCENARIOS = [
  'default',
  'loading',
  'sessionExpired',
  'serverError',
  'invalidData',
  'partial',
  'unknown'
] as const
export type Scenario = (typeof SCENARIOS)[number]

export const scenarioOf = (value: string | null): Scenario =>
  SCENARIOS.find((scenario) => scenario === value) ?? 'default'

const withFreshness = (body: Overview, freshness: 'partial' | 'unknown') => {
  const copy: Overview = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(body))
  for (const metric of Object.values(copy.metrics)) metric.freshness = freshness
  return copy
}

// The answer of the scenario for a project that has data.
async function answer(scenario: Scenario, body: Overview) {
  if (scenario === 'loading') await delay('infinite')
  if (scenario === 'sessionExpired') return new HttpResponse(null, { status: 401 })
  if (scenario === 'serverError') return new HttpResponse(null, { status: 500 })
  if (scenario === 'invalidData') {
    // One metric snapshot is missing: the zod contract must report the right field metrics.blocked.
    const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(body))
    delete copy.metrics.blocked
    return HttpResponse.json(copy)
  }
  if (scenario === 'partial' || scenario === 'unknown') {
    return HttpResponse.json(withFreshness(body, scenario))
  }
  return HttpResponse.json(body)
}

export const handlersFor = (scenario: Scenario) => [
  http.get<{ workspaceId: string }>(`${BASE}/shell`, ({ params }) => {
    const body = shells.get(params.workspaceId)
    return body ? HttpResponse.json(body) : new HttpResponse(null, { status: 404 })
  }),
  // ?scope=mine (R-B4) returns the same data until the back end defines the filter.
  http.get<{ workspaceId: string; projectId: string }>(
    `${BASE}/projects/:projectId/overview`,
    ({ params }) => {
      if (params.workspaceId !== WORKSPACE) return new HttpResponse(null, { status: 404 })
      if (params.projectId === FORBIDDEN) return new HttpResponse(null, { status: 403 })
      const body = overviews.get(params.projectId)
      return body ? answer(scenario, body) : new HttpResponse(null, { status: 404 })
    }
  )
]
```

```ts
import { DEFAULT_LOCALE, type Locale } from '../core/i18n/locale'

// iOS and Android (spec 5.3): plan B only tries running the app (R-B1), so the language choice is not stored yet;
```
