`src/platform/storage.web.ts`:

```ts
import { type Locale, resolveLocale } from '../core/i18n/locale'

// Web (spec 5.3): the language choice lives in localStorage, and the lang attribute of the page changes with it;
// public/index.html reads the same key to set lang before the first paint. If the browser blocks localStorage (private
// mode, a device policy) the app still runs, in English.
const KEY = 'metis.locale'

export function readLocale(): Locale {
  try {
    return resolveLocale(localStorage.getItem(KEY))
  } catch {
    return resolveLocale(null)
  }
}

export function writeLocale(locale: Locale): void {
  document.documentElement.lang = locale
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(KEY, locale)
  } catch {
    // If it cannot be saved, the choice lasts until the page is reloaded.
  }
}
```

`src/platform/mocks.ts` (iOS and Android: the `require` sits inside an `if` block, so the release build does not carry
`src/mocks`; the trial measured that the iOS export without the flag has 0 strings of the mock data). Before `require('msw')`
it sets an empty class for `Event`, `EventTarget`, `MessageEvent`, `BroadcastChannel` when they are missing: when the
plan was written, the app running on the Android Emulator reported `ReferenceError: Property 'MessageEvent' doesn't exist` and then
`Property 'BroadcastChannel' doesn't exist` at the line `require('msw')` and rendered nothing; with the empty classes
both the Android Emulator and the iOS Simulator show the mock data of Meridian (Task 15):

```ts
// iOS and Android (spec 3.4): there is no service worker, so this layer wraps the global fetch and asks the
// handlers of src/mocks directly with getResponse of MSW 2; a request that no handler takes goes on to the
// network. It runs only when EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS=1; the require sits inside the if block so that the release build does not carry
// src/mocks (same reason as mocks.web.ts). In the app there is only the default scenario.
export async function startMocks(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS === '1') {
    defineMissingEventClasses(globalThis as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)
    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports -- loaded conditionally, see above
    const { getResponse } = require('msw') as typeof import('msw')
    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports -- loaded conditionally, see above
    const mocks = require('../mocks/handlers') as typeof import('../mocks/handlers')
    // In the app there is no path to choose a scenario: the scenario of "nothing chosen", that is default.
    const handlers = mocks.handlersFor(mocks.scenarioOf(null))
    const network = globalThis.fetch
    const mocked: typeof fetch = async (input, init) =>
      (await getResponse(handlers, new Request(input, init))) ?? network(input, init)
    Object.assign(globalThis, { fetch: mocked })
  }
}

// Hermes lacks the classes that the core of MSW 2 uses right at load time, in the WebSocket and SSE part (`extends
// MessageEvent`, `extends Event`, `extends EventTarget`, `new BroadcastChannel(...)`): measured on the Android
// Emulator, `ReferenceError: Property 'MessageEvent' doesn't exist` and then `... 'BroadcastChannel' ...` at
// require('msw'). The mock server in the app only answers HTTP, so no class is really used: an empty class
// is enough to load. Returns the names of the classes it set.
export function defineMissingEventClasses(scope: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
  const missing = ['Event', 'EventTarget', 'MessageEvent', 'BroadcastChannel'].filter(
    (name) => typeof scope[name] !== 'function'
  )
  for (const name of missing) scope[name] = class {}
  return missing
}
```

`src/platform/mocks.web.ts` (only the form `if (flag) { require(...) }` keeps MSW out of the release build; the form
`if (flag !== '1') return` followed by `require` brings along all 1116 modules, measured in the trial section 3):

```ts
// Web (spec 3.4): the mock server is the service worker of MSW, running only in a build with EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS=1
// (pnpm web, the export for e2e). The release build does not set the flag: Metro replaces the flag with its value and drops the whole
// if block, so MSW and src/mocks do not enter the bundle. require must sit inside the if block; as for import(), the project's Jest 29
// cannot run it. The scenario (R-B3) is chosen with ?mock=<name> when the page loads.
export async function startMocks(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS === '1') {
    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports -- loaded conditionally, see above
    const { setupWorker } = require('msw/browser') as typeof import('msw/browser')
    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports -- loaded conditionally, see above
    const mocks = require('../mocks/handlers') as typeof import('../mocks/handlers')
    const scenario = mocks.scenarioOf(new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('mock'))
    await setupWorker(...mocks.handlersFor(scenario)).start({
      onUnhandledRequest: 'bypass',
      quiet: true
    })
  }
}
```

```js
  dashboard: 'w/[workspaceId]/dashboard.tsx',

  roadmap: 'w/[workspaceId]/roadmap.tsx',
  capacity: 'w/[workspaceId]/capacity.tsx',

}

for (const [destination, file] of Object.entries(FILES)) {

  writeFileSync(
    path,
    `import { NotBuilt } from '${shell}'\n\n` +
      `// An MVP destination not built yet (spec 4.3 rule 1): the final path already exists, it opens the shared "not built" page.\n` +
      `export default function ${name}() {\n  return <NotBuilt destination="${destination}" />\n}\n`
  )
}
console.log(`routes: wrote ${Object.keys(FILES).length} files`)
```

```tsx
import { Slot } from 'expo-router'
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

import { useAppFonts } from '../platform/fonts'
import { startMocks } from '../platform/mocks'

}
```

`e2e/web/mocks.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, type Page, test } from '@playwright/test'

import { meridian } from '../../src/mocks/fixtures/meridian'
import { creativeStudio } from '../../src/mocks/fixtures/shell'

const API = 'https://api.metis.test/workspaces/creative-studio'

// Call the API from the page itself: the service worker of MSW answers (api.metis.test never resolves).
const call = (page: Page, url: string) =>
  page.evaluate(async (target) => {
    const response = await fetch(target)
    return { status: response.status, body: response.status === 200 ? await response.json() : null }
  }, url)

test('the service worker of MSW returns the mock data of the shell and of Meridian', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/w/creative-studio/registry')
  await expect(page.getByTestId('not-built-registry')).toBeAttached()
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => navigator.serviceWorker.controller?.scriptURL)).toMatch(
    /\/mockServiceWorker\.js$/
  )
  expect(await call(page, `${API}/shell`)).toEqual({ status: 200, body: creativeStudio })
  expect(await call(page, `${API}/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview?scope=mine`)).toEqual({
    status: 200,
    body: meridian
  })
  expect((await call(page, `${API}/projects/spring-catalogue-renders/overview`)).status).toBe(403)
})

test('?mock=serverError at page load selects the scenario for the whole session', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/w/creative-studio/registry?mock=serverError')
  await expect(page.getByTestId('not-built-registry')).toBeAttached()
  expect((await call(page, `${API}/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview`)).status).toBe(500)
  expect((await call(page, `${API}/shell`)).status).toBe(200)
})

test('the saved language goes into the lang attribute as soon as the page loads', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/w/creative-studio/registry')
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang)).toBe('en')
  await page.evaluate(() => localStorage.setItem('metis.locale', 'vi'))
  await page.reload({ waitUntil: 'commit' })
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.readyState !== 'loading')
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang)).toBe('vi')
})
```

`whole`: "the whole reply". When the whole reply is broken (the body is not JSON, or the root has the wrong type) the path of the
error is empty, so there is no field name to state; the first version showed the machine's English error message (`body is not
JSON`) on the screen, against the rule that all displayed text goes through the dictionary (spec 5.5). Now `problemOf` (Task 10)
states this phrase.

    `freshness: { tone: 'fresh' | 'partial' | 'stale' | 'unknown'; text: string }`; `scopeNote:
    string`; `scope: { label: string; active: Scope; options: { scope: Scope; label: string; route:
    Route }[] }`; `exportLabel: { label: string; note: string }`; `tiles: { id; label: string; value:
    string; figure: boolean; delta: { text: string; tone: 'muted' | 'bad' }[]; alert: boolean; route:
    Route }[]` (eight tiles, `id` is `'workItems' | 'deliverables' | 'workPackages' | 'milestones' |
    'approvalGates' | 'blocked' | 'delayed' | 'highRisk'`; `delta` matches the prop of `Tile` in Task 6);
    `progress: { title; percent; value: number; caption; note }` (`percent` is text like `'25%'`; `value`
    is the whole-number percentage rounded down, the same number as `percent`, FE-20; `Meter` of Task 6 takes
    `value`); `status: { title; tableView; columns: { status; count }; rows: { status; name; count; legend
    }[]; segments: { status; weight: number; route: Route }[] }`; `health: { title; declared: {
    label; level; text }; computed: { label; level; text }; warning: string | null }`; `categories:
    { name; value; segments: { tone: 'good' | 'neutral'; weight: number }[]; route: Route }[]`;
    `workload: { initials; name; value; share: number; route: Route }[]`; `titles: { categories: {
    title; caption; value }; workload: { title; caption } }`; `upcoming`, `overdue`, `risks` (each one
    `{ title; rows: { id; code; labels: { label; text }[]; name; trailing: { text; tone }; route
    }[]; empty: string | null; more: { text; route } | null }`, `upcoming` additionally has `action: { label;
    route }`, `overdue` and `risks` additionally have `count: string`; `labels[].label` is the WBS label code, the same name
    as the field of the prop `ListRow.labels` of Task 6).
  - `problemOf(error: ApiError, strings: OverviewStrings)` returns `{ kind: 'noAccess' | 'notFound' |
    'unavailable' | 'sessionExpired' | 'invalid'; title: string; body: string; actions: ({ kind:
    'link'; label; route } | { kind: 'retry'; label } | { kind: 'notBuilt'; label; note })[] }`; the branch
    `noAccess` additionally has `request: string` and the branch `sessionExpired` additionally has `signIn: string` (spreading
    the whole text group of the dictionary; the test pins both), the other three branches have none.
- Produces, from `model.tools.ts`: `type Context = { locale: Locale; strings: OverviewStrings;
  workspaceId: string; projectId: string; scope: Scope }`, `type Tone = 'muted' | 'bad' | 'critical'
  | 'serious'` (`part` keeps exactly the tone passed in, so the `delta` of a tile only has `'muted' | 'bad'`; `rowsOf`
  also keeps each list's own tone: `trailing` of an upcoming row is `'muted'`, of an overdue row is
  `'critical'`, of a risk row is `'critical' | 'serious'`, all assignable to `Tone`; `'critical'` and
  `'serious'` are values of `StatusTone` (Task 5), so Task 12 passes the tone of a risk row straight into `Chip`
  without a cast). From `model.lists.ts`: `initialsOf(name: string): string`.
- Types used in Task 12: `ReturnType<typeof buildOverview>` and `ReturnType<typeof problemOf>`
  (`import type { buildOverview, problemOf } from './model'`); the model does not export a type name of its own
  (Knip reports an export nobody uses).

```ts
import { meridian } from '../../mocks/fixtures/meridian'
import { buildOverview } from './model'
import { STRINGS } from './strings'

// Screen 24 with the data of Meridian: all text and all numbers exactly as in wireframe 24 (English prints "Sept", R-B6).
const ids = { workspaceId: 'creative-studio', projectId: 'meridian-cgi-campaign' }
// Build inside each test, not at the top of the file: code that runs at file load makes Stryker treat every mutant
// of it as a static mutant and rerun the whole test suite for each mutant.
const build = () =>
  buildOverview(meridian, { locale: 'en', strings: STRINGS.en, ...ids, scope: 'project' })
const wbs = (drill: Record<string, string[]>) => ({
  pathname: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/wbs',
  params: { ...drill, ...ids }
})
const item = (itemId: string) => ({
  pathname: '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/wbs/[itemId]',
  params: { ...ids, itemId }
})
const muted = (text: string) => ({ text, tone: 'muted' })

test('OVW-01 first row: title, freshness, work item count, scope buttons, Export not built yet', () => {
  const model = build()
  expect(model.title).toBe('Overview')
  expect(model.freshness).toEqual({
    tone: 'fresh',
    text: 'As of 22 Sept 2026, 09:40 · metrics v1'
  })
  expect(model.scopeNote).toBe('12 work items · Category rows excluded')
  const overview = '/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/overview'
  expect(model.scope).toEqual({
    label: 'Scope',
    active: 'project',
    options: [
      { scope: 'project', label: 'This project', route: { pathname: overview, params: ids } },
      {
        scope: 'mine',
        label: 'My items',
        route: { pathname: overview, params: { scope: 'mine', ...ids } }
      }
    ]
  })
  expect(model.exportLabel).toEqual({ label: 'Export', note: 'Not built yet' })
})

test('OVW-01 OVW-04 BR-32 eight metric tiles, sub-lines, highlighted tiles, drill-down links of the server', () => {
  const model = build()
  expect(model.tiles).toEqual([
    {
      id: 'workItems',
      label: 'Work items',
      value: '12',
      figure: true,
      delta: [muted('6 category rows not counted')],
      alert: false,
      route: wbs({})
    },
    {
      id: 'deliverables',
      label: 'Deliverables',
      value: '3',
      figure: true,
      delta: [muted('Type = Deliverable')],
      alert: false,
      route: wbs({ type: ['deliverable'] })
    },
    {
      id: 'workPackages',
      label: 'Work packages',
      value: '2',
      figure: true,
      delta: [],
      alert: false,
```

`model.tools.ts`:

```ts
import type { Scope } from '../../core/api/client'
import { formatInteger } from '../../core/format'
import { interpolate } from '../../core/i18n/dictionary'
import type { Locale } from '../../core/i18n/locale'
import { type Query, ROUTES, type Route } from '../../core/routes'
import type { OverviewStrings } from './strings'

// The part shared by model.ts and model.lists.ts: the context of the screen and a few small functions.

export type Context = {
  locale: Locale
  strings: OverviewStrings
  workspaceId: string
  projectId: string
  scope: Scope
}
export type Tone = 'muted' | 'bad' | 'critical' | 'serious'
type Plural = { readonly one: string; readonly other: string }

export const num = (c: Context, value: number) => formatInteger(c.locale, value)

// A sentence with a count: English changes its wording when the number is 1, the translation layer has no plural function (spec 5.5).
export const counted = (c: Context, count: number, forms: Plural) =>
  interpolate(count === 1 ? forms.one : forms.other, { count: num(c, count) })

// A part of a line of text with a tone. The type of the tone keeps exactly the value passed in, so the sub-line of a tile only has
// 'muted' and 'bad', matching the prop delta of Tile.
export const part = <T extends Tone>(text: string, tone: T) => ({ text, tone })

export const ids = (c: Context) => ({ workspaceId: c.workspaceId, projectId: c.projectId })

// Link to the WBS of the project, the filter taken as is from the server's snapshot (spec 4.3).
export const wbs = (c: Context, drill: Query): Route => ({
  pathname: ROUTES.wbs,
  params: { ...drill, ...ids(c) }
})
```

`model.lists.ts`:

```ts
import type { Overview } from '../../core/api/overview'
import { formatDate } from '../../core/format'
import { interpolate } from '../../core/i18n/dictionary'
import { ROUTES, type Route } from '../../core/routes'
import { type Context, counted, ids, num, part, type Tone, wbs } from './model.tools'

// The part of screen 24 drawn as horizontal bars (Category, person in charge) and the three attention lists.

type Item = Omit<Overview['attention']['upcoming']['items'][number], 'targetDate'>

// Initials from a name: the first letter of the first two words, in capitals ("Denny K." becomes "DK").
export const initialsOf = (name: string) =>
  name
    .split(/\s/)
    .filter((word) => word !== '')
    .slice(0, 2)
    .map((word) => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase())
    .join('')

export function barsOf(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  const top = Math.max(0, ...data.workload.map((row) => row.open))
  const categories = data.progressByCategory.map((row) => ({
    name: row.name,
    value: interpolate(c.strings.categories.value, {
      done: num(c, row.done),
      total: num(c, row.total)
    }),
    segments: [
      { tone: 'good' as const, weight: row.done },
      { tone: 'neutral' as const, weight: row.total - row.done }
    ].filter((segment) => segment.weight > 0),
    route: wbs(c, row.drill)
  }))
  const workload = data.workload.map((row) => ({
    initials: initialsOf(row.name),
    name: row.name,
    value: num(c, row.open),
    // The longest bar is the person with the most open work; when everyone has 0 items there is no bar.
    share: top === 0 ? 0 : row.open / top,
    route: wbs(c, row.drill)
  }))
  return { categories, workload }
}

const rowsOf = <T extends Item, K extends Tone>(
  items: T[],
  c: Context,
  trailing: (item: T) => { text: string; tone: K }
) =>
  items.map((item) => ({
    id: item.id,
    code: item.code,
    labels: item.labels.map((label) => ({ label, text: c.strings.labels[label] })),
    name: item.name,
    trailing: trailing(item),
    route: { pathname: ROUTES.wbsItem, params: { ...ids(c), itemId: item.id } }
  }))

export function listsOf(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  const l = c.strings.lists
  const { upcoming, overdue, risks } = data.attention
  const more = (list: { total: number; items: unknown[] }, template: string, route: Route) =>
    list.total > list.items.length
      ? { text: interpolate(template, { count: num(c, list.total - list.items.length) }), route }
      : null
  const late = { m: data.metrics.milestones.overdue, g: data.metrics.approvalGates.overdue }
  const note = interpolate(l.upcoming.overdueNote, {
    milestones: counted(c, late.m, l.upcoming.milestones),
    gates: counted(c, late.g, l.upcoming.gates)
  })
  return {
    upcoming: {
      title: l.upcoming.title,
      action: { label: l.upcoming.viewInWbs, route: wbs(c, {}) },
      rows: rowsOf(upcoming.items, c, (item) =>
        part(formatDate(c.locale, item.targetDate), 'muted')
      ),
      empty:
        upcoming.total === 0
          ? [l.upcoming.empty, ...(late.m > 0 || late.g > 0 ? [note] : [])].join(' ')
          : null,
      more: more(upcoming, l.upcoming.more, wbs(c, {}))
    },
    overdue: {
      title: l.overdue.title,
      count: num(c, overdue.total),
      rows: rowsOf(overdue.items, c, (item) =>
        part(interpolate(l.overdue.days, { days: num(c, item.daysOverdue) }), 'critical')
      ),
      empty: overdue.total === 0 ? l.overdue.empty : null,
      more: more(overdue, l.overdue.more, { pathname: ROUTES.focus, params: ids(c) })
    },
    risks: {
      title: l.risks.title,
      count: num(c, risks.total),
      rows: rowsOf(risks.items, c, (item) =>
        part(l.risks.levels[item.riskLevel], item.riskLevel === 'critical' ? 'critical' : 'serious')
      ),
      empty: risks.total === 0 ? l.risks.empty : null,
      more: more(risks, l.risks.more, wbs(c, data.metrics.highRisk.drill))
    }
  }
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 10): `rowsOf` gains a type parameter `K extends Tone` and

`model.ts`:

```ts
import type { ApiError } from '../../core/api/client'
import type { Overview } from '../../core/api/overview'
import { formatDateTime, formatPercent } from '../../core/format'
import { interpolate } from '../../core/i18n/dictionary'
import { type Query, ROUTES, type Route } from '../../core/routes'
import { barsOf, listsOf } from './model.lists'
import { type Context, counted, ids, num, part, wbs } from './model.tools'
import type { OverviewStrings } from './strings'

// Screen 24 (spec 3.1, 4.2): pure functions that turn API data into what the screen draws. All text translated, all numbers
// formatted, all links built. The screen does not count or sum rows itself (spec 3.3): every number is a
// snapshot of the server, the drill-down filter is taken as is from the server (spec 4.3). Lists and horizontal bars are in
// model.lists.ts, the shared part in model.tools.ts.

type Freshness = Overview['metrics']['workItems']['freshness']

// Eight tiles in the order of the wireframe (lines 25 to 32).
const TILES = [
  'workItems',
  'deliverables',
  'workPackages',
  'milestones',
  'approvalGates',
  'blocked',
  'delayed',
  'highRisk'
] as const
// Freshness getting worse: the "As of" line states the worst freshness among the snapshots.
const FRESHNESS: Freshness[] = ['fresh', 'partial', 'stale', 'unknown']
// Health levels to compare declared with calculated; unknown cannot be compared.
const RANK = { green: 0, amber: 1, red: 2, unknown: -1 }

// The sub-line of each tile; the Delayed tile apart because it may have no baseline yet.
function deltaOf(data: Overview, c: Context, id: Exclude<(typeof TILES)[number], 'delayed'>) {
  const { metrics } = data
  const d = c.strings.deltas
  const when = (count: number, template: string) =>
    count > 0 ? [part(interpolate(template, { count: num(c, count) }), 'muted')] : []
  if (id === 'workItems') {
    const excluded = metrics.workItems.categoryRowsExcluded
    return excluded > 0 ? [part(counted(c, excluded, d.categoryRows), 'muted')] : []
  }
  if (id === 'deliverables') return [part(d.deliverableType, 'muted')]
  if (id === 'milestones' || id === 'approvalGates') return when(metrics[id].overdue, d.overdue)
  if (id === 'highRisk') return when(metrics.highRisk.critical, d.critical)
  return []
}

function tilesOf(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  return TILES.map((id) => {
    const base = { id, label: c.strings.tiles[id], route: wbs(c, data.metrics[id].drill) }
    const delayed = data.metrics.delayed
    if (id !== 'delayed') {
      const value = data.metrics[id].value
      // BRD OVW-01: Blocked, Delayed, High risk stand out when greater than 0.
      const alert = (id === 'blocked' || id === 'highRisk') && value > 0
      return { ...base, value: num(c, value), figure: true, delta: deltaOf(data, c, id), alert }
    }
    if (delayed.state === 'notBaselined') {
      return {
        ...base,
        value: c.strings.deltas.notBaselined,
        figure: false,
        delta: [],
        alert: false
      }
    }
    const change = delayed.sinceBaseline
    const sign = change > 0 ? `+${num(c, change)}` : num(c, change)
    const since = interpolate(c.strings.deltas.sinceBaseline, {
      version: num(c, delayed.baselineVersion)
    })
    const delta = [part(sign, change > 0 ? 'bad' : 'muted'), part(since, 'muted')]
    return { ...base, value: num(c, delayed.value), figure: true, delta, alert: delayed.value > 0 }
  })
}

// The "As of" line: the earliest time, the worst freshness, the definition versions of all snapshots.
function freshnessOf(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  const snapshots = Object.values(data.metrics)
  const tone = FRESHNESS[Math.max(...snapshots.map((m) => FRESHNESS.indexOf(m.freshness)))]!
  // A UTC time ending in Z may carry fractional seconds (z.iso.datetime() allows it), so sort()[0] may
  // pick a later time within the same second. The text shown does not change: the time prints only to the minute.
  const asOf = snapshots.map((m) => m.asOf).sort()[0]!
  const versions = [...new Set(snapshots.map((m) => m.definitionVersion))].sort((a, b) => a - b)
  const text = interpolate(c.strings.freshness[tone], {
    time: formatDateTime(c.locale, asOf, data.timeZone),
    version: versions.map((v) => num(c, v)).join(', v')
  })
  return { tone, text }
}

function healthOf(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  const h = c.strings.health
  const declared = data.project.declaredHealth
  const { level, reasons } = data.computedHealth
  const lines = reasons.map((reason) => {
    if (reason.kind === 'criticalRisksWithoutMitigation') return counted(c, reason.count, h.risk)
    const items = counted(c, reason.count, h.overdueItems)
    if (reason.milestones === 0) return interpolate(h.deliveryOnly, { items })
    return interpolate(h.delivery, {
      items,
      milestones: counted(c, reason.milestones, h.milestones)
    })
  })
  return {
    title: h.title,
    declared: { label: h.declared, level: declared, text: h.levels[declared] },
    computed: { label: h.computed, level, text: h.levels[level] },
    // Warning strip when declared health is better than calculated health (OVW-05).
    warning: RANK[declared] < RANK[level] ? [h.better, ...lines].join(' ') : null
  }
}

function statusOf(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  const s = c.strings.status
  const rows = data.statusBreakdown.map((row) => {
    const name = s.names[row.status]
    const count = num(c, row.count)
    return { status: row.status, name, count, legend: interpolate(s.legend, { name, count }) }
  })
  const segments = data.statusBreakdown
    .filter((row) => row.count > 0)
    .map((row) => ({ status: row.status, weight: row.count, route: wbs(c, row.drill) }))
  return {
    title: s.title,
    tableView: s.tableView,
    columns: s.columns,
    rows,
    segments
  }
}

// Error states of the screen (spec 4.5, R-B15): 403 no permission, 401 session expired, wrong shape states
// the wrong field; not found has its own sentence; server, network, timeout share one "could not
// load" state with a retry button.
export function problemOf(error: ApiError, strings: OverviewStrings) {
  const st = strings.states
  const back = {
    kind: 'link' as const,
    label: st.back,
    route: { pathname: ROUTES.myFocus, params: {} }
  }
  const retry = { kind: 'retry' as const, label: st.retry }
  const notBuilt = (label: string) => ({ kind: 'notBuilt' as const, label, note: strings.notBuilt })
  if (error.kind === 'forbidden') {
    return {
      kind: 'noAccess' as const,
      ...st.noAccess,
      actions: [notBuilt(st.noAccess.request), back]
    }
  }
  if (error.kind === 'notFound')
    return { kind: 'notFound' as const, ...st.notFound, actions: [back] }
  if (error.kind === 'unauthenticated') {
    return {
      kind: 'sessionExpired' as const,
      ...st.sessionExpired,
      actions: [notBuilt(st.sessionExpired.signIn)]
    }
  }
  if (error.kind === 'invalid') {
    // An empty path is an error of the whole reply (the body is not JSON, or the root has the wrong type): there is no field name
    // to state, so state the phrase of the dictionary. The error sentence (message) is the machine's English, it does not show on the screen
    // (spec 5.5: all displayed text goes through the dictionary).
    const fields = error.issues.map((issue) => issue.path || st.invalid.whole).join(', ')
    return {
      kind: 'invalid' as const,
      title: st.invalid.title,
      body: interpolate(st.invalid.body, { fields }),
      actions: [retry]
    }
  }
  return { kind: 'unavailable' as const, ...st.unavailable, actions: [retry] }
}

export function buildOverview(data: Overview, c: Context) {
  const s = c.strings
  const progress = data.metrics.progress
  const own = (query: Query): Route => ({
    pathname: ROUTES.overview,
    params: { ...query, ...ids(c) }
  })
  return {
    title: s.title,
    freshness: freshnessOf(data, c),
    scopeNote: counted(c, data.metrics.workItems.value, s.scopeNote),
    scope: {
      label: s.scope.label,
      active: c.scope,
      options: [
        { scope: 'project' as const, label: s.scope.project, route: own({}) },
        { scope: 'mine' as const, label: s.scope.mine, route: own({ scope: 'mine' }) }
      ]
    },
    exportLabel: { label: s.export, note: s.notBuilt },
    tiles: tilesOf(data, c),
    progress: {
      title: s.progress.title,
      percent: formatPercent(c.locale, progress.value),
      // Whole-number percentage for the progress bar, rounded down like the text percent (FE-20).
      value: Math.floor(progress.value),
      caption: interpolate(progress.total === 1 ? s.progress.done.one : s.progress.done.other, {
        done: num(c, progress.done),
        total: num(c, progress.total)
      }),
      note: s.progress.note
    },
    status: statusOf(data, c),
    health: healthOf(data, c),
    ...barsOf(data, c),
    titles: { categories: s.categories, workload: s.workload },
    ...listsOf(data, c)
  }
}
```

```tsx
import { createContext, type ReactNode, use, useState } from 'react'

import type { Locale } from '../core/i18n/locale'
import { readLocale, writeLocale } from '../platform/storage'

type LocaleState = { locale: Locale; setLocale: (locale: Locale) => void }

const LocaleContext = createContext<LocaleState | null>(null)

// The app's language (spec 5.3): reads the saved choice once at startup; changing it saves and the text changes at once.
export function LocaleProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [locale, setState] = useState(readLocale)
  const setLocale = (next: Locale) => {
    writeLocale(next)
    setState(next)
  }
  return <LocaleContext value={{ locale, setLocale }}>{children}</LocaleContext>
}

export function useLocale(): LocaleState {
  const state = use(LocaleContext)
  if (state === null) throw new Error('useLocale needs a LocaleProvider above it')
  return state
}
```

```ts
import { renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node'

import type { ApiResult } from '../core/api/client'
import type { Shell } from '../core/api/shell'
import { creativeStudio, digitalProducts } from '../mocks/fixtures/shell'
import { handlersFor } from '../mocks/handlers'
import { useShell } from './useShell'

// Handlers are registered inside each test (beforeEach), not when the file loads: Stryker assigns coverage to
// the right test, and does not treat a mutant of handlers.ts as a static mutant.
const server = setupServer()
beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }))
beforeEach(() => server.use(...handlersFor('default')))
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers())
afterAll(() => server.close())

// Records the value of each render: renderHook with await flushes the mock server's answer inside act,
// so the loading render can only be seen through this record.
const mount = (id: string) => {
  const seen: (ApiResult<Shell> | null)[] = []
  const hook = renderHook(
    ({ workspace }: { workspace: string }) => {
      const value = useShell(workspace)
      seen.push(value)
      return value
    },
    { initialProps: { workspace: id } }
  )
  return { seen, hook }
}

test('the first render is null (loading), then the data of the workspace in the path', async () => {
  const { seen, hook } = mount('creative-studio')
  const { result } = await hook
  expect(seen[0]).toBeNull()
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: creativeStudio }))
})

test('switching workspace: the first render after the switch is null, no old data shown', async () => {
  const { seen, hook } = mount('creative-studio')
  const { result, rerender } = await hook
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: creativeStudio }))
  seen.length = 0
  await rerender({ workspace: 'digital-products' })
  expect(seen[0]).toBeNull()
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: digitalProducts }))
})

test('unknown workspace: notFound error from the client', async () => {
  const { result } = await mount('no-such-workspace').hook
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: false, error: { kind: 'notFound' } }))
})
```

Expected when you run `pnpm exec jest --ci --selectProjects iOS Android --testPathPattern 'shell/useShell'`: exit
1, `Cannot find module './useShell'`. Then `src/shell/useShell.ts` (setState only inside `.then`, not
called synchronously in the effect: the config's rule `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` is an error):

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

import { type ApiResult, getShell } from '../core/api/client'
import type { Shell } from '../core/api/shell'
import { apiConfig } from '../platform/config'

// The shell's data for the workspace in the path (R-B2); null while loading. The answer carries the id
// of the workspace asked about, so when the workspace changes, the old answer is not shown for the new workspace.
export function useShell(workspaceId: string): ApiResult<Shell> | null {
  const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<{ workspaceId: string; result: ApiResult<Shell> } | null>(
    null
  )
  useEffect(() => {
    getShell(apiConfig, workspaceId).then((result) => setAnswer({ workspaceId, result }))
  }, [workspaceId])
  return answer?.workspaceId === workspaceId ? answer.result : null
}
```

The `Main` frame and the `Workspaces` menu are found with `getByLabelText` and then the prop `role` is asserted, not with
`getByRole`, for the same reason as the note after the test table of Task 6 Step 3 (the `*ByRole` of RNTL only matches
accessible elements, and `accessible` on a container frame would hide the items inside from
VoiceOver). The name of the link is matched with a regular expression, because RNTL keeps even the `aria-hidden` glyph in
the name: the name of the My focus item is `◎ My focus 9`, not `My focus 9`.

`Shell({ children })`: takes `workspaceId` (`HOME.workspaceId` if missing) and `projectId` with
`useGlobalSearchParams<{ workspaceId?: string; projectId?: string }>()`, the open destination with

`src/shell/locale.tsx`:

```tsx
import { createContext, type ReactNode, use, useState } from 'react'

import type { Locale } from '../core/i18n/locale'
import { readLocale, writeLocale } from '../platform/storage'

type LocaleState = { locale: Locale; setLocale: (locale: Locale) => void }

const LocaleContext = createContext<LocaleState | null>(null)

// The app language (spec 5.3): reads the saved choice once on open; a change saves it and the text changes at once.
export function LocaleProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [locale, setState] = useState(readLocale)
  const setLocale = (next: Locale) => {
    writeLocale(next)
    setState(next)
  }
  return <LocaleContext value={{ locale, setLocale }}>{children}</LocaleContext>
}

export function useLocale(): LocaleState {
  const state = use(LocaleContext)
  if (state === null) throw new Error('useLocale needs a LocaleProvider above it')
  return state
}
```

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import { Pressable, Text } from 'react-native'

import { readLocale, writeLocale } from '../platform/storage'
import { LocaleProvider, useLocale } from './locale'

jest.mock('../platform/storage', () => ({ readLocale: jest.fn(), writeLocale: jest.fn() }))

function Probe() {
  const { locale, setLocale } = useLocale()
  return (
    <Pressable role="button" onPress={() => setLocale(locale === 'en' ? 'vi' : 'en')}>
      <Text>{`locale=${locale}`}</Text>
    </Pressable>
  )
}

afterEach(() => jest.clearAllMocks())

test('opens with the saved choice; a change saves it again and the text changes at once', async () => {
  jest.mocked(readLocale).mockReturnValue('vi')
  await render(
    <LocaleProvider>
      <Probe />
    </LocaleProvider>
  )
  expect(screen.getByText('locale=vi')).toBeOnTheScreen()
  await fireEvent.press(screen.getByRole('button'))
  expect(screen.getByText('locale=en')).toBeOnTheScreen()
  expect(writeLocale).toHaveBeenCalledWith('en')
  expect(readLocale).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
})

test('using useLocale outside LocaleProvider is a programmer error', async () => {
  jest.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => undefined)
  await expect(render(<Probe />)).rejects.toThrow('useLocale needs a LocaleProvider above it')
})
```

`src/shell/useShell.ts`:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

import { type ApiResult, getShell } from '../core/api/client'
import type { Shell } from '../core/api/shell'
import { apiConfig } from '../platform/config'

// The shell data for the workspace in the path (R-B2); null while loading. The answer carries the id of the
// workspace asked for, so when the workspace changes, the old answer is not shown for the new workspace. The answer
// of a request that has been replaced (the workspace changed before it came back) is dropped, otherwise it arrives late and overwrites the data
// of the current workspace and the shell is left with only the logo.
export function useShell(workspaceId: string): ApiResult<Shell> | null {
  const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<{ workspaceId: string; result: ApiResult<Shell> } | null>(
    null
  )
  useEffect(() => {
    let current = true
    getShell(apiConfig, workspaceId).then((result) => {
      if (current) setAnswer({ workspaceId, result })
    })
    return () => {
      current = false
    }
  }, [workspaceId])
  return answer?.workspaceId === workspaceId ? answer.result : null
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 11): the effect keeps a `current` flag and drops the answer
of a request that has been replaced. In the first version, the late answer of the old workspace overwrote the data of the
current workspace; then `answer.workspaceId` differed from `workspaceId`, so the shell got stuck in the loading state, with only
the logo. The review measured this bug with the hook itself in a trial copy.

`src/shell/useShell.test.native.ts`:

```ts
import { act, renderHook, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw'
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node'

import type { ApiResult } from '../core/api/client'
import type { Shell } from '../core/api/shell'
import { creativeStudio, digitalProducts } from '../mocks/fixtures/shell'
import { handlersFor } from '../mocks/handlers'
import { useShell } from './useShell'

// Handlers are registered in each test (beforeEach), not when the file loads: Stryker assigns coverage to
// the right test and does not treat the mutants of handlers.ts as static mutants.
const server = setupServer()
beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }))
beforeEach(() => server.use(...handlersFor('default')))
afterEach(() => {
  server.resetHandlers()
  server.events.removeAllListeners()
})
afterAll(() => server.close())

// Records the value of every render: renderHook with await flushes the answer of the mock server inside act,
// so the loading render can only be seen through this record.
const mount = (id: string) => {
  const seen: (ApiResult<Shell> | null)[] = []
  const hook = renderHook(
    ({ workspace }: { workspace: string }) => {
      const value = useShell(workspace)
      seen.push(value)
      return value
    },
    { initialProps: { workspace: id } }
  )
  return { seen, hook }
}

test('the first render is null (loading), then the data of the workspace in the path', async () => {
  const { seen, hook } = mount('creative-studio')
  const { result } = await hook
  expect(seen[0]).toBeNull()
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: creativeStudio }))
})

test('workspace change: the first render after the change is null, old data is not shown', async () => {
  const { seen, hook } = mount('creative-studio')
  const { result, rerender } = await hook
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: creativeStudio }))
  seen.length = 0
  await rerender({ workspace: 'digital-products' })
  expect(seen[0]).toBeNull()
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: digitalProducts }))
})

test('unknown workspace: the notFound error of the client', async () => {
  const { result } = await mount('no-such-workspace').hook
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: false, error: { kind: 'notFound' } }))
})

test('a late answer of the old workspace does not overwrite the data of the current workspace', async () => {
  // The handler of the old workspace holds the answer until we release it; the new workspace answers at once.
  let release!: () => void
  const held = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    release = resolve
  })
  server.use(
    http.get('https://api.metis.test/workspaces/creative-studio/shell', async () => {
      await held
      return HttpResponse.json(creativeStudio)
    })
  )
  const delivered = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    server.events.on('response:mocked', ({ request }) => {
      if (request.url.endsWith('/creative-studio/shell')) resolve()
    })
  })
  const { seen, hook } = mount('creative-studio')
  const { result, rerender } = await hook
  await rerender({ workspace: 'digital-products' })
  await waitFor(() => expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: digitalProducts }))

  // Release the old answer, wait for it to reach the client (a short real time for the chain of fetch, body read, then).
  await act(async () => {
    release()
    await delivered
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100))
  })

  expect(result.current).toEqual({ ok: true, data: digitalProducts })
  expect(seen.at(-1)).toEqual({ ok: true, data: digitalProducts })
})
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 11): it adds a fourth test, a late answer of the
old workspace does not overwrite the data of the current workspace (the mock server holds the answer of
`creative-studio` until the test releases it, the new workspace answers at once), and `afterEach` removes the
`server.events` listeners that this test attaches. The new test was red in all 3 trial runs on the old hook. The hook now
has four tests, so Step 2 produces `Tests: 8 passed, 8 total` (two projects), not six.

`src/shell/model.ts`:

```ts
import type { Overview } from '../core/api/overview'
import type { Shell } from '../core/api/shell'
import { formatDate, formatInteger, formatTime } from '../core/format'
import { interpolate } from '../core/i18n/dictionary'
import type { Locale } from '../core/i18n/locale'
import { type Destination, isDestination, ROUTES, type Route } from '../core/routes'
import type { ShellStrings } from './strings'

// App shell (spec 4.1): pure functions that turn the shell data and the project header into what the components
// draw. All text comes from ShellStrings, all numbers go through formatInteger, all links are already built.

type NavEntry = Shell['nav']['home'][number]
// Codes of the sidebar items that have a path (Investment, Scenarios, SteerCo, AI copilot do not).
type LinkCode = Extract<NavEntry['code'], Destination>

// A link has a route and no tag; text with a tag (planned, notBuilt) has a tag and no route.
type NavItem = {
  code: NavEntry['code']
  label: string
  badge: { count: string; alert: boolean } | null
  active: boolean
  testID: string
} & (
  | { kind: 'link'; route: Route; tag: null }
  | { kind: 'planned' | 'notBuilt'; route: null; tag: string }
)

// The sidebar always has three groups in the order Home, Portfolio, Workspace; the project tree sits between groups two and three.
type NavGroup = { label: string; items: NavItem[] }

type SidebarContext = {
  locale: Locale
  strings: ShellStrings
  projectId: string | null
  active: Destination | null
}

type HeaderContext = {
  locale: Locale
  strings: ShellStrings
  timeZone: string
  workspaceId: string
  projectId: string
}

// Breadcrumb path (wireframe 24 line 16): workspace, portfolio, program, project. A project not in
// the workspace tree (or no project open yet) gives only the workspace name.
export function crumbsOf(shell: Shell, projectId: string | null): string[] {
  for (const portfolio of shell.tree) {
    for (const program of portfolio.programs) {
      const project = program.projects.find((candidate) => candidate.id === projectId)
      if (project) return [shell.workspace.name, portfolio.name, program.name, project.name]
    }
  }
  return [shell.workspace.name]
}

// A destination has a path pattern that matches the whole pathname; [name] matches exactly one non-empty segment, with no
// slash. Built inside the function, not at the top of the file, so that Stryker does not count it as a static mutant.
export function activeOf(pathname: string): Destination | null {
  const destinations = Object.keys(ROUTES) as Destination[]
  return (
    destinations.find((destination) =>
      new RegExp(`^${ROUTES[destination].replace(/\[\w+\]/g, '[^/]+')}$`).test(pathname)
    ) ?? null
  )
}

// The link of a sidebar item: My focus and Approvals belong to no workspace.
const linkOf = (code: LinkCode, workspaceId: string): Route =>
  code === 'myFocus' || code === 'approvals'
    ? { pathname: ROUTES[code], params: {} }
    : { pathname: ROUTES[code], params: { workspaceId } }

// Three kinds of item (spec 4.3): a link; text with a Planned tag when the data says planned (rule 2); text with a
// Not built yet tag when there is no destination and the data does not say planned either (rule 3).
function navItemOf(entry: NavEntry, shell: Shell, c: SidebarContext): NavItem {
  const { code, badge, planned } = entry
  const base = {
    code,
    label: isDestination(code) ? c.strings.destinations[code] : c.strings.later[code],
    badge: badge && { count: formatInteger(c.locale, badge.count), alert: badge.alert },
    active: code === c.active,
    testID: `nav-${code}`
  }
  if (planned !== null) {
    return { ...base, kind: 'planned', route: null, tag: c.strings.planned[planned] }
  }
  if (!isDestination(code)) {
    return { ...base, kind: 'notBuilt', route: null, tag: c.strings.notBuilt }
  }
  return { ...base, kind: 'link', route: linkOf(code, shell.workspace.id), tag: null }
}

// Project tree: portfolio and program are not links; a project links to its overview screen.
function treeOf(shell: Shell, c: SidebarContext) {
  return {
    label: c.strings.groups.projects,
    portfolios: shell.tree.map((portfolio) => ({
      name: portfolio.name,
      programs: portfolio.programs.map((program) => ({
        name: program.name,
        count: formatInteger(c.locale, program.projects.length),
        projects: program.projects.map((project) => ({
          name: project.name,
          route: {
            pathname: ROUTES.overview,
            params: { workspaceId: shell.workspace.id, projectId: project.id }
          },
          active: project.id === c.projectId,
          testID: `tree-${project.id}`
        }))
      }))
    }))
  }
}

export function sidebarOf(shell: Shell, c: SidebarContext) {
  const group = (label: string, entries: NavEntry[]): NavGroup => ({
    label,
    items: entries.map((entry) => navItemOf(entry, shell, c))
  })
  return {
    tenant: shell.tenant.name,
    workspace: shell.workspace.name,
    // Choosing a workspace opens its screen 15 (D-B21). The button draws the tenant name then the workspace name, so the accessible name
    // starts with exactly those two names (WCAG 2.5.3, Label in Name).
    switcher: {
      label: interpolate(c.strings.sidebar.switcher, {
        tenant: shell.tenant.name,
        workspace: shell.workspace.name
      }),
      menuLabel: c.strings.sidebar.workspaces,
      items: shell.workspaces.map((workspace) => ({
        label: workspace.name,
        route: { pathname: ROUTES.dashboard, params: { workspaceId: workspace.id } },
        current: workspace.id === shell.workspace.id,
        testID: `workspace-${workspace.id}`
      }))
    },
    search: { label: c.strings.sidebar.search, route: { pathname: ROUTES.search, params: {} } },
    groups: [
      group(c.strings.groups.home, shell.nav.home),
      group(c.strings.groups.portfolio, shell.nav.portfolio),
      group(c.strings.groups.workspace, shell.nav.workspace)
    ] satisfies [NavGroup, NavGroup, NavGroup],
    tree: treeOf(shell, c)
  }
}

// The six tabs of the project in the order of the wireframe (shell.js:117).
const TABS = ['overview', 'charter', 'wbs', 'plan', 'governance', 'focus'] as const

// Project header (spec 3.5): the data is in the contract of the overview screen, so screen 24 calls this function.
// The header is drawn only on the overview screen, so the open tab is always Overview.
export function projectHeaderOf(project: Overview['project'], c: HeaderContext) {
  const h = c.strings.header
  const ids = { workspaceId: c.workspaceId, projectId: c.projectId }
  const { baseline, stage } = project
  return {
    title: project.name,
    client: project.client,
    pm: interpolate(h.pm, { name: project.pm }),
    stage: interpolate(h.stage, {
      name: stage.name,
      index: formatInteger(c.locale, stage.index),
      count: formatInteger(c.locale, stage.count)
    }),
    health: { level: project.declaredHealth, text: h.health[project.declaredHealth] },
    framework: interpolate(h.framework, project.framework),
    baseline:
      baseline === null
        ? h.noBaseline
        : interpolate(h.baseline, {
            version: formatInteger(c.locale, baseline.version),
            date: formatDate(c.locale, baseline.date)
          }),
    share: { label: h.share, note: c.strings.notBuilt },
    changeRequest: {
      label: c.strings.destinations.changeRequest,
      route: { pathname: ROUTES.changeRequest, params: ids }
    },
    tabs: TABS.map((key) => ({
      key,
      label: c.strings.destinations[key],
      route: { pathname: ROUTES[key], params: ids },
      active: key === 'overview',
      testID: `tab-${key}`
    })),
    tabsLabel: h.tabs,
    saved: interpolate(h.saved, { time: formatTime(c.locale, project.savedAt, c.timeZone) }),
    dot: h.dot
  }
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 11): the label of the workspace switcher is built from the tenant name
and the workspace name (the key `sidebar.switcher` takes `{tenant}` and `{workspace}`), instead of a single `{name}`.
The button draws the tenant name then the workspace name, so the accessible name must start with exactly the text that is seen: WCAG 2.2
SC 2.5.3 Label in Name, level A [Source: MDN, Understanding WCAG, section Operable, 2.5.3]. The first version "Choose a
workspace. Current: Creative Studio" does not contain the text "Acme Holdings Creative Studio" on the button.

```ts
  })

  test('[name] matches exactly one segment: non-empty, no slash, the pattern matches the whole path', () => {
    expect(activeOf('/w/creative-studio/projects/p/wbs')).toBe('wbs')
    expect(activeOf('/w/creative-studio/projects/new')).toBe('newProject')
    expect(activeOf('/w//registry')).toBeNull()
    expect(activeOf('/w/a/b/registry')).toBeNull()
    expect(activeOf('/w/creative-studio/registry/more')).toBeNull()
    expect(activeOf('/x/w/creative-studio/registry')).toBeNull()
    expect(activeOf('/')).toBeNull()
  })
})
```

```ts
  test('Workspace group: three links to screens of the workspace', () => {

    expect(investment).toMatchObject({
```

`src/shell/Sidebar.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link, usePathname } from 'expo-router'
import { Fragment, type ReactNode, useState } from 'react'
import { Pressable, ScrollView, View } from 'react-native'

import { CountBadge } from '../design-system/CountBadge'
import { Glyph, type GlyphName } from '../design-system/Glyph'
import { Logo } from '../design-system/Logo'
import { Menu } from '../design-system/Menu'
import { Tag } from '../design-system/Tag'
import { Text } from '../design-system/Text'
import type { sidebarOf } from './model'
import { rowFrame, styles } from './Sidebar.styles'

type Model = ReturnType<typeof sidebarOf>
type Group = Model['groups'][number]
type NavItem = Group['items'][number]

// The body of a row: the glyph column, the label, then the trailing part of the row. The open row switches the glyph and the label to the accent
// color.
function RowBody(props: {
  glyph: GlyphName
  label: string
  variant: 'nav' | 'navTree'
  active: boolean
  trailing: ReactNode
}) {
  const { glyph, label, variant, active, trailing } = props
  return (
    <>
      <View style={styles.glyph}>
        <Glyph name={glyph} size="caption" tone={active ? 'accent' : 'muted'} />
      </View>
      <View style={styles.label}>
        <Text variant={variant} tone={active ? 'accent' : 'text'}>
          {label}
        </Text>
      </View>
      {trailing}
    </>
  )
}

// The trailing part of an item's row: an unbuilt item (Planned or Not built yet) always shows its tag, even
// when the data carries a count (spec 4.3 rules 2 and 3); a link shows the count if there is one.
function Trailing({ item }: { item: NavItem }) {
  if (item.kind !== 'link') {
    return (
      <View style={styles.trailing}>
        <Tag variant="label">{item.tag}</Tag>
      </View>
    )
  }
  if (item.badge) {
    return (
      <View style={styles.trailing}>
        <CountBadge count={item.badge.count} tone={item.badge.alert ? 'alert' : 'neutral'} />
      </View>
    )
  }
  return null
}

// An item with a destination is a link; an item of a later version and an item with no known destination are text, not clickable, with no style of a
// disabled button (spec 4.3 rules 2 and 3).
function NavRow({ item }: { item: NavItem }) {
  const body = (
    <RowBody
      glyph={item.code}
      label={item.label}
      variant="nav"
      active={item.active}
      trailing={<Trailing item={item} />}
    />
  )
  if (item.kind !== 'link') {
    return (
      <View testID={item.testID} style={styles.row}>
        {body}
      </View>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Link href={item.route} asChild>
      <Pressable
        role="link"
        aria-current={item.active ? 'page' : undefined}
        testID={item.testID}
        style={rowFrame(item.active)}
      >
        {body}
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  )
}

function GroupLabel({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <View style={styles.groupLabel}>
      <Text variant="eyebrow" tone="muted">
        {children}
      </Text>
    </View>
  )
}

// The rows are direct children of the content area (Fragment, not View), so that the gap of the content
// area separates them.
function NavGroup({ group }: { group: Group }) {
  return (
    <>
      <GroupLabel>{group.label}</GroupLabel>
      {group.items.map((item) => (
        <NavRow key={item.code} item={item} />
      ))}
    </>
  )
}

// Workspace switcher: the button opens a floating menu right below it; choosing an item opens the screen of that workspace (D-B21).
function Switcher(props: { tenant: string; workspace: string; switcher: Model['switcher'] }) {
  const { tenant, workspace, switcher } = props
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const items = switcher.items.map((item) => ({
    label: item.label,
    href: item.route,
    current: item.current,
    testID: item.testID
  }))
  return (
    <View style={styles.switcherWrap}>
      <Pressable
        role="button"
        aria-label={switcher.label}
        aria-expanded={open}
        testID="workspace-switcher"
        onPress={() => setOpen(!open)}
        style={styles.switcher}
      >
        <View>
          <Text variant="tenant" tone="muted">
            {tenant}
          </Text>
          <Text variant="sidebar" weight="600">
            {workspace}
          </Text>
        </View>
        <Glyph name="caret" size="caption" tone="muted" />
      </Pressable>
      {open ? <Menu label={switcher.menuLabel} items={items} /> : null}
    </View>
  )
}

// Project tree: portfolio and program are not links; a project is a link to its overview screen.
// Each level is nested in a View with left padding.
function Tree({ tree }: { tree: Model['tree'] }) {
  return (
    <>
      <GroupLabel>{tree.label}</GroupLabel>
      {tree.portfolios.map((portfolio, index) => (
        <Fragment key={index}>
          <View style={styles.row}>
            <RowBody
              glyph="portfolio"
              label={portfolio.name}
              variant="navTree"
              active={false}
              trailing={null}
            />
          </View>
          <View style={styles.nested}>
            {portfolio.programs.map((program, position) => (
              <Fragment key={position}>
                <View style={styles.row}>
                  <RowBody
                    glyph="program"
                    label={program.name}
                    variant="navTree"
                    active={false}
                    trailing={
                      <View style={styles.trailing}>
                        <CountBadge count={program.count} tone="neutral" />
                      </View>
                    }
                  />
                </View>
                <View style={styles.nested}>
                  {program.projects.map((project) => (
                    <Link key={project.testID} href={project.route} asChild>
                      <Pressable
                        role="link"
                        aria-current={project.active ? 'page' : undefined}
                        testID={project.testID}
                        style={rowFrame(project.active)}
                      >
                        <RowBody
                          glyph="project"
                          label={project.name}
                          variant="navTree"
                          active={project.active}
                          trailing={null}
                        />
                      </Pressable>
                    </Link>
                  ))}
                </View>
              </Fragment>
            ))}
          </View>
        </Fragment>
      ))}
    </>
  )
}

// The order of the wireframe (shell.js:54-79): workspace switcher, search box, Home group, Portfolio group, project tree,
// spacer, Workspace group. The workspace switcher is rebuilt per path (key), so whichever page we
// go to, the menu closes, even when re-choosing the open workspace (the shell keeps its data unchanged) and
// when returning to the old page (the menu does not reopen by itself).
function Body({ model }: { model: Model }) {
  const [home, portfolio, workspace] = model.groups
  const pathname = usePathname()
  return (
    <>
      <Switcher
        key={pathname}
        tenant={model.tenant}
        workspace={model.workspace}
        switcher={model.switcher}
      />
      <Link href={model.search.route} asChild>
        <Pressable role="link" testID="sidebar-search" style={styles.search}>
          <Text variant="sidebar" tone="muted">
            {model.search.label}
          </Text>
        </Pressable>
      </Link>
      <NavGroup group={home} />
      <NavGroup group={portfolio} />
      <Tree tree={model.tree} />
      <View style={styles.spacer} />
      <NavGroup group={workspace} />
    </>
  )
}

type SidebarProps = {
  // null: loading, draws only the logo.
  model: Model | null
  brand: string
  label: string
  // On an error it draws the error sentence under the logo, not the rest.
  error: string | null
}

export function Sidebar({ model, brand, label, error }: SidebarProps) {
  return (
    <View role="navigation" aria-label={label} testID="sidebar" style={styles.frame}>
      <ScrollView contentContainerStyle={styles.content}>
        <View style={styles.logo}>
          <Logo label={brand} />
        </View>
        {error !== null ? (
          <Text variant="small" tone="muted">
            {error}
          </Text>
        ) : null}
        {error === null && model !== null ? <Body model={model} /> : null}
      </ScrollView>
    </View>
  )
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 11): two places. One: `Trailing` checks `kind !== 'link'`
first, so an unbuilt item always shows the Planned or Not built yet tag, even when the data carries a count; in
the first version the count covered the tag, against spec 4.3 rules 2 and 3. Two: the workspace switcher gets `key={pathname}`,
so whichever page we go to, the menu closes, even when re-choosing the open workspace and when returning to the old
page. The way the coordinator proposed (remember the path when the menu opens, then compare it with the current path) reopens the menu
when going back to exactly the page that opened it (measured), while `key` rebuilds the whole switcher so it has no such bug. There remains
one case where the menu does not close by itself: re-choosing the open workspace while on its own home page, because the path
does not change.

`src/shell/Sidebar.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet, type ViewStyle } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from '../design-system/tokens'

// Sidebar (wireframe.css:21-36). The rows and group labels are direct children of the content area, so
// the space4 gap of the content area separates each row like the `gap: 4px` of wf-sidebar; rows nested in the
// tree sit in a View with left padding, so they have no such gap (like .nav-tree of the wireframe).
export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  frame: {
    width: tokens.sidebarW,
    backgroundColor: tokens.rail,
    borderRightWidth: 1,
    borderRightColor: tokens.line
  },
  // flexGrow 1: when the screen is taller than the content, the spacer pushes the Workspace group to the bottom.
  content: {
    flexGrow: 1,
    paddingVertical: tokens.gap,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space10,
    gap: tokens.space4
  },
  logo: {
    marginTop: tokens.space2,
    marginHorizontal: tokens.space8,
    marginBottom: tokens.space12
  },
  // The wrapper of the workspace switcher: the floating menu is positioned absolutely relative to this wrapper. zIndex 1 because react-native-web gives
  // every View position relative and zIndex 0: each View is a stacking context, so the zIndex of the menu only has
  // meaning inside this wrapper, and the rows that come after (search box, group labels) draw over the whole wrapper, the menu and the menu items
  // are covered, and presses miss. A wrapper with a higher zIndex than its siblings puts the menu above them.
  switcherWrap: { position: 'relative', zIndex: 1 },
  switcher: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    justifyContent: 'space-between',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space8,
    backgroundColor: tokens.surface,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: tokens.line,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius,
    paddingVertical: tokens.space7,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space9,
    marginBottom: tokens.space8
  },
  search: {
    backgroundColor: tokens.surface,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: tokens.line,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius,
    paddingVertical: tokens.space6,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space9,
    marginBottom: tokens.space6
  },
  groupLabel: {
    paddingTop: tokens.space12,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space8,
    paddingBottom: tokens.space6
  },
  row: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space8,
    paddingVertical: tokens.space6,
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.space8,
    borderRadius: tokens.radius
  },
  active: { backgroundColor: tokens.accentSoft },
  glyph: { width: tokens.glyphW, alignItems: 'center' },
  // A long name wraps to the next line instead of overflowing the row.
  label: { flexShrink: 1 },
  trailing: { marginLeft: 'auto' },
  nested: { paddingLeft: tokens.gap },
  spacer: { flex: 1 }
})

// A Pressable inside a Link asChild must have a style that is an object, not an array (the Slot of expo-router
// merges the style of the Link into it), so the parts are flattened into one object.
export const rowFrame = (active: boolean) =>
  StyleSheet.flatten<ViewStyle>([styles.row, active && styles.active])
```

This version differs from the first draft (final fix wave): `switcherWrap` adds `zIndex: 1`. react-native-web gives every
`View` `position: relative` and `zIndex: 0` [Source:
`node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/View/index.js:132,134`, version 0.21.3], so each `View` is
its own stacking context and the `zIndex: 1` of `Menu` only has meaning inside its wrapper; the rows that come
after (search box, group labels) draw over the whole wrapper. Measured on Chromium and WebKit: the menu appears but the element
on top, at the middle of a menu item, is the sidebar, so pressing a workspace does nothing and the focused item is covered
(WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11). After the fix, both menu items are on top and pressing goes to
`/w/digital-products/dashboard`.

```tsx
import { sidebarOf } from './model'

import { STRINGS } from './strings'

// The symbols of Glyph are hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden), so the text lookup must reach them.

const modelOf = (active: Parameters<typeof sidebarOf>[1]['active'] = 'overview') =>
```

```tsx
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByTestId('workspace-switcher'))

    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Workspaces')).toBeNull()
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { expanded: false })).toHaveProp(
      'testID',
      'workspace-switcher'
    )
  })

  test('re-choosing the open workspace: the screen goes to the home page of the workspace and the menu closes by itself', async () => {
    const rendered = mountInLayout()
    await rendered

    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByTestId('workspace-switcher'))
    expect(screen.getByLabelText('Workspaces')).toBeOnTheScreen()
    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByTestId('workspace-creative-studio'))

    expect(rendered.getPathname()).toBe('/w/creative-studio/dashboard')
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Workspaces')).toBeNull()
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { expanded: false })).toHaveProp(
      'testID',
      'workspace-switcher'
    )
  })

  test('going to another page closes the menu and returning to the old page does not reopen it by itself', async () => {
    const rendered = mountInLayout()
    await rendered

    await fireEvent.press(screen.getByTestId('workspace-switcher'))
    await act(async () => router.navigate('/w/creative-studio/registry'))
    expect(rendered.getPathname()).toBe('/w/creative-studio/registry')
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Workspaces')).toBeNull()
    await act(async () => router.navigate('/'))

    expect(rendered.getPathname()).toBe('/')
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Workspaces')).toBeNull()
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { expanded: false })).toHaveProp(
      'testID',
      'workspace-switcher'
    )
  })
})
```

`src/shell/TopBar.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Link } from 'expo-router'
import { Fragment } from 'react'
import { Pressable, View } from 'react-native'

import { interpolate } from '../core/i18n/dictionary'
import { LOCALES, type Locale, NATIVE_NAMES, resolveLocale } from '../core/i18n/locale'
import { ROUTES } from '../core/routes'
import { Avatar } from '../design-system/Avatar'
import { Button } from '../design-system/Button'
import { CountBadge } from '../design-system/CountBadge'
import { Glyph } from '../design-system/Glyph'
import { Select } from '../design-system/Select'
import { Tag } from '../design-system/Tag'
import { Text } from '../design-system/Text'
import type { ShellStrings } from './strings'
import { styles } from './TopBar.styles'

type TopBarProps = {
  // Names from the workspace to the project; empty when the shell data is not there yet.
  crumbs: string[]
  strings: ShellStrings
  user: { name: string; initials: string } | null
  // The formatted number of unread notifications; with null the bell has no number.
  notifications: string | null
  workspaceId: string
  locale: Locale
  onLocale: (locale: Locale) => void
}

// Top bar (spec 4.1, wireframes/assets/shell.js:114-116): breadcrumb path, search box, New button, help,
// notifications, user, language select (D-B17).
export function TopBar(props: TopBarProps) {
  const { crumbs, strings, user, notifications, workspaceId, locale, onLocale } = props
  const t = strings.topbar
  return (
    <View role="banner" testID="topbar" style={styles.bar}>
      <View role="navigation" aria-label={t.breadcrumb} testID="breadcrumb" style={styles.crumbs}>
        <Text variant="crumb" tone="muted" lines={1}>
          {crumbs.map((name, index) => (
            <Fragment key={index}>
              {index > 0 ? t.separator : null}
              {index === crumbs.length - 1 ? (
                <Text variant="crumb" weight="600" tone="text">
                  {name}
                </Text>
              ) : (
                name
              )}
            </Fragment>
          ))}
        </Text>
      </View>
      <Link href={{ pathname: ROUTES.search, params: {} }} asChild>
        <Pressable role="link" testID="topbar-search" style={styles.search}>
          <Text variant="crumb" tone="muted">
            {t.search}
          </Text>
        </Pressable>
      </Link>
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        label={t.create}
        href={{ pathname: ROUTES.newProject, params: { workspaceId } }}
        testID="topbar-new"
      />
      <View testID="topbar-help" style={styles.help}>
        <Text variant="small" tone="muted">
          {t.help}
        </Text>
        <Tag variant="label">{strings.planned.V2}</Tag>
      </View>
      <Link href={{ pathname: ROUTES.notifications, params: {} }} asChild>
        <Pressable
          role="link"
          aria-label={
            notifications === null
              ? strings.destinations.notifications
              : interpolate(t.notifications, { count: notifications })
          }
          testID="topbar-notifications"
          style={styles.bell}
        >
          <Glyph name="bell" size="body" tone="muted" />
          {notifications === null ? null : <CountBadge tone="bell" count={notifications} />}
        </Pressable>
      </Link>
      {user === null ? null : <Avatar size="lg" initials={user.initials} name={user.name} />}
      <Select
        label={t.language}
        value={locale}
        options={LOCALES.map((value) => ({ value, label: NATIVE_NAMES[value] }))}
        onChange={(value) => onLocale(resolveLocale(value))}
        testID="language"
      />
    </View>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { fireEvent, screen, within } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import { renderRouter } from 'expo-router/testing-library'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'

import { tokens } from '../design-system/tokens'
import { TopBar } from './TopBar'
import { STRINGS } from './strings'

const MERIDIAN = [
  'Creative Studio',
  'Client Delivery',
  'Northwind Furniture Co.',
  'Meridian CGI Campaign'
]
const NADIA = { name: 'Nadia R.', initials: 'NR' }

type Props = Partial<ComponentProps<typeof TopBar>>
const mount = (props: Props = {}) =>
  renderRouter({
    index: () => (
      <TopBar
        crumbs={MERIDIAN}
        strings={STRINGS.en}
        user={NADIA}
        notifications="3"
        workspaceId="creative-studio"
        locale="en"
        onLocale={jest.fn()}
        {...props}
      />
    ),
    search: () => null,
    'me/notifications': () => null,
    'w/[workspaceId]/projects/new': () => null
  })

// renderRouter turns on the fake timers of Jest and never turns them off; under Stryker the automatic cleanup of RNTL hangs
// for the full 5 seconds (see Button.test.native.tsx). The afterEach of the nested block runs before the afterEach of the
// outer block, so the real timers are restored before that cleanup.
describe('TopBar', () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    jest.useRealTimers()
  })

  test('top bar: banner region with height topbarH, horizontal padding pagePad, bottom border line, the parts laid out in a row', async () => {
    await mount()

    const bar = screen.getByTestId('topbar')
    expect(bar).toHaveProp('role', 'banner')
    expect(bar).toHaveStyle({
      flexDirection: 'row',
      alignItems: 'center',
      gap: tokens.space12,
      height: tokens.topbarH,
      paddingHorizontal: tokens.pagePad,
      borderBottomWidth: 1,
      borderBottomColor: tokens.line
    })
  })

  test('breadcrumb: four names joined by a separator, the last name bold in the text color, not a link', async () => {
    await mount()

    const crumbs = screen.getByLabelText('Breadcrumb')
    expect(crumbs).toHaveProp('role', 'navigation')
    expect(crumbs).toHaveProp('testID', 'breadcrumb')
    expect(crumbs).toHaveStyle({ flexShrink: 1 })
    expect(crumbs).toHaveTextContent(
      'Creative Studio / Client Delivery / Northwind Furniture Co. / Meridian CGI Campaign'
    )
    expect(screen.getByText('Meridian CGI Campaign')).toHaveStyle({
      fontWeight: '600',
      color: tokens.text,
      fontSize: tokens.fsCrumbs
    })
    expect(within(crumbs).queryByRole('link')).toBeNull()
    const outer = screen.getByText('Meridian CGI Campaign').parent
    expect(outer).toHaveStyle({ color: tokens.muted, fontSize: tokens.fsCrumbs })
    expect(outer).toHaveProp('numberOfLines', 1)
    // Only the last name is a bold nested Text; the earlier names are plain text of the outer Text.
    const parts = outer?.children ?? []
    expect(parts.slice(0, -1).every((part) => typeof part === 'string')).toBe(true)
    expect(typeof parts.at(-1)).toBe('object')
  })

  test('one name makes that name the last one: bold; no name leaves the breadcrumb empty', async () => {
    await mount({ crumbs: ['Creative Studio'] })

    expect(screen.getByText('Creative Studio')).toHaveStyle({ fontWeight: '600' })
    expect(screen.getByTestId('breadcrumb')).toHaveTextContent('Creative Studio')
  })

  test('no shell data yet: the breadcrumb is empty, no error', async () => {
    await mount({ crumbs: [] })

    expect(screen.getByTestId('breadcrumb')).toHaveTextContent('')
    expect(within(screen.getByTestId('breadcrumb')).queryByText(/./)).toBeNull()
  })

  test('the search box is a link to the search screen, width searchW, pushing the rest to the right', async () => {
    const router = mount()
    await router

    const search = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Search projects, WBS items, people (/)' })
    expect(search).toHaveProp('testID', 'topbar-search')
    expect(search).toHaveStyle({
      marginLeft: 'auto',
      width: tokens.searchW,
      borderWidth: 1,
      borderColor: tokens.line,
      borderRadius: tokens.radius,
      paddingVertical: tokens.space6,
      paddingHorizontal: tokens.space10
    })
    expect(within(search).getByText('Search projects, WBS items, people (/)')).toHaveStyle({
      color: tokens.muted,
      fontSize: tokens.fsCrumbs
    })
    await fireEvent.press(search)
    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe('/search')
  })

  test('the + New button is a secondary button, opens the new project screen of the workspace', async () => {
    const router = mount({ workspaceId: 'digital-products' })
    await router

    const create = screen.getByRole('link', { name: '+ New' })
    expect(create).toHaveProp('testID', 'topbar-new')
    expect(create).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: tokens.surface, borderColor: tokens.lineStrong })
    await fireEvent.press(create)
    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe('/w/digital-products/projects/new')
  })

  test('Help is text with a Planned V2 label, not a link', async () => {
    await mount()

    const help = screen.getByTestId('topbar-help')
    expect(help).toHaveStyle({ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: tokens.space5 })
    expect(within(help).getByText('Help')).toHaveStyle({
      color: tokens.muted,
      fontSize: tokens.fsSmall
    })
    expect(within(help).getByText('Planned V2')).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(help.props.role).toBeUndefined()
    expect(screen.queryByRole('link', { name: /Help/ })).toBeNull()
  })

  test('notifications 3: a link with a full-sentence name, bell of size iconBtn, red number in the corner, pressing opens the notifications screen', async () => {
    const router = mount()
    await router

    const bell = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Notifications, 3 unread' })
    expect(bell).toHaveProp('testID', 'topbar-notifications')
    expect(bell).toHaveStyle({
      width: tokens.iconBtn,
      height: tokens.iconBtn,
      borderWidth: 1,
      borderColor: tokens.line,
      borderRadius: tokens.radius,
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center'
    })
    expect(within(bell).getByText('\u{1F514}', { includeHiddenElements: true })).toHaveStyle({
      fontSize: tokens.fsBody
    })
    expect(within(bell).getByText('3')).toHaveStyle({ color: tokens.white })
    expect(bell.children).toHaveLength(2)
    await fireEvent.press(bell)
    expect(router.getPathname()).toBe('/me/notifications')
  })

  test('the user initials are an image with a name, not pressable', async () => {
    await mount()

    const avatar = screen.getByRole('img', { name: 'Nadia R.' })
    expect(within(avatar).getByText('NR')).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(avatar).toHaveStyle({ width: tokens.avatarLg, height: tokens.avatarLg })
    expect(screen.queryByRole('link', { name: /Nadia/ })).toBeNull()
  })

  test('no user and no notification count: no avatar, no number on the bell', async () => {
    await mount({ user: null, notifications: null })

    expect(screen.queryByRole('img', { name: 'Nadia R.' })).toBeNull()
    expect(screen.queryByText('NR')).toBeNull()
    expect(screen.queryByText('3')).toBeNull()
    const bell = screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Notifications' })
    expect(bell).toHaveProp('testID', 'topbar-notifications')
    expect(bell.children).toHaveLength(1)
  })

  test('the language select at the end of the bar: has a name, two languages, the current language is selected', async () => {
    await mount({ locale: 'vi' })

    const select = screen.getByLabelText('Language')
    expect(select).toHaveProp('testID', 'language')
    // The iOS and Android pickers receive an `items` list with labels (an Android item carries no value).
    const items = (select.props as { items: { label: string }[] }).items
    expect(items.map((item) => item.label)).toEqual(['English', 'Tieng Viet'])
    expect((select.props.selectedIndex ?? select.props.selected) as number).toBe(1)
  })

  test('choosing Tieng Viet calls onLocale with vi; an unknown value falls back to English', async () => {
    const onLocale = jest.fn()
    await mount({ onLocale })

    await fireEvent(screen.getByTestId('language'), 'valueChange', 'vi', 1)
    expect(onLocale).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('vi')
    await fireEvent(screen.getByTestId('language'), 'valueChange', 'xx', 1)

    expect(onLocale).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)
    expect(onLocale).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('en')
  })

  test('text comes from the dictionary of the shell that is passed in: Vietnamese', async () => {
    const vi = STRINGS.vi.topbar
    await mount({ strings: STRINGS.vi, locale: 'vi' })

    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: vi.search })).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: vi.create })).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(screen.getByText(vi.help)).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(screen.getByText(STRINGS.vi.planned.V2)).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'Notifications, 3 unread' })).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(screen.getByLabelText(vi.breadcrumb)).toBeOnTheScreen()
    expect(screen.getByLabelText(vi.language)).toBeOnTheScreen()
  })
})
```
