```tsx
import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'

import type { Route } from '../../../core/routes'
import { Button } from '../../../design-system/Button'
import { Card } from '../../../design-system/Card'
import { Chip } from '../../../design-system/Chip'
import { ListNote } from '../../../design-system/ListNote'
import { ListRow } from '../../../design-system/ListRow'
import { Text } from '../../../design-system/Text'
import type { buildOverview } from '../model'

type Model = ReturnType<typeof buildOverview>
// The part of a row shared by all three lists; the end of a row (date, number of days, level) is drawn by each card.
type Row = {
  id: string
  code: string
  labels: ComponentProps<typeof ListRow>['labels']
  name: string
  route: Route
}

// The body of a list card (html:87-102): the rows, then the sentence saying why it is empty or the "+ N more" row, and
// the last row of the card has no bottom border. The empty sentence exists only when there is no row, so those two never
// show together.
function ListBody<T extends Row>({
  rows,
  prefix,
  trailing,
  empty,
  more,
  moreID
}: {
  rows: T[]
  prefix: string
  trailing: (row: T) => ReactNode
  empty: string | null
  more: { text: string; route: Route } | null
  moreID: string
}) {
  return (
    <>
      {rows.map((row, index) => (
        <ListRow
          key={row.id}
          code={row.code}
          labels={row.labels}
          name={row.name}
          trailing={trailing(row)}
          href={row.route}
          last={more === null && index === rows.length - 1}
          testID={`${prefix}-${row.id}`}
        />
      ))}
      {empty === null ? null : <ListNote text={empty} last />}
      {more === null ? null : <ListNote text={more.text} href={more.route} last testID={moreID} />}
    </>
  )
}

// The three attention cards (html:84-104): upcoming items, overdue items, high and critical risks. Each row is a
// link to the item (BR-32).
export function ListCards({
  upcoming,
  overdue,
  risks
}: {
  upcoming: Model['upcoming']
  overdue: Model['overdue']
  risks: Model['risks']
}) {
  return (
    <>
      <Card
        title={upcoming.title}
        flush
        aside={
          <Button
            variant="ghost"
            label={upcoming.action.label}
            href={upcoming.action.route}
            testID="upcoming-view-in-wbs"
          />
        }
      >
        <ListBody
          rows={upcoming.rows}
          prefix="upcoming-row"
          trailing={(row) => (
            <Text variant="small" tone="muted">
              {row.trailing.text}
            </Text>
          )}
          empty={upcoming.empty}
          more={upcoming.more}
          moreID="upcoming-more"
        />
      </Card>
      <Card title={overdue.title} flush aside={<Chip tone="critical">{overdue.count}</Chip>}>
        <ListBody
          rows={overdue.rows}
          prefix="overdue-row"
          trailing={(row) => (
            <Text variant="small" tone="criticalText">
              {row.trailing.text}
            </Text>
          )}
          empty={overdue.empty}
          more={overdue.more}
          moreID="overdue-more"
        />
      </Card>
      <Card title={risks.title} flush aside={<Chip tone="serious">{risks.count}</Chip>}>
        <ListBody
          rows={risks.rows}
          prefix="risk-row"
          trailing={(row) => <Chip tone={row.trailing.tone}>{row.trailing.text}</Chip>}
          empty={risks.empty}
          more={risks.more}
          moreID="risks-more"
        />
      </Card>
    </>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { render, screen, within } from '@testing-library/react-native'
import type { TestInstance } from 'test-renderer'

import type { Overview } from '../../../core/api/overview'
import { tokens } from '../../../design-system/tokens'
import { meridian } from '../../../mocks/fixtures/meridian'
import { showroom } from '../../../mocks/fixtures/showroom'
import { buildOverview } from '../model'
import { STRINGS } from '../strings'
import { ListCards } from './ListCards'

const PROJECT = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign'

// Build the model inside each test, not at the top of the file (code that runs while the file loads is a Stryker static mutant).
const mount = async (data: Overview = meridian) => {
  const model = buildOverview(data, {
    locale: 'en',
    strings: STRINGS.en,
    workspaceId: 'creative-studio',
    projectId: 'meridian-cgi-campaign',
    scope: 'project'
  })
  await render(<ListCards upcoming={model.upcoming} overdue={model.overdue} risks={model.risks} />)
}

// Meridian plus more upcoming items and risks than the number of rows shown: mock data for the two "+ N more" rows that
// Meridian does not have (upcoming-more, risks-more).
const crowded = (): Overview => ({
  ...meridian,
  attention: {
    ...meridian.attention,
    upcoming: { total: 5, items: showroom.attention.upcoming.items },
    risks: { ...meridian.attention.risks, total: 7 }
  }
})

// The names of the WBS labels of a row: each label is a symbol with a name.
const marksOf = (row: TestInstance) =>
  within(row)
    .queryAllByRole('img')
    .map((mark) => mark.props['aria-label'])

// The four overdue rows of Meridian (html:91-94): row id, code, name, number of days, WBS label names.
const OVERDUE: [string, string, string, string, string[]][] = [
  ['item-1.1.1', '1.1.1', 'Phase 1 Render Delivery', '60d', ['Milestone']],
  ['item-3.1', '3.1', 'Visual Quality Approval', '59d', ['Approval gate']],
  ['item-1.1', '1.1', '51 Render Images', '43d', []],
  ['item-1.1.2', '1.1.2', 'Phase 2 Render Delivery', '43d', ['Milestone']]
]

// The four risk rows (html:99-102): row id, code, name, level, text color and background color of the level chip, WBS labels.
const RISKS: [string, string, string, string, string, string, string[]][] = [
  [
    'item-6.1',
    '6.1',
    'Client Feedback Risk',
    'Critical',
    tokens.criticalText,
    tokens.criticalBg,
    []
  ],
  ['item-1.2', '1.2', '3D Film (2 to 3 minutes)', 'High', tokens.seriousText, tokens.seriousBg, []],
  [
    'item-3.2',
    '3.2',
    'Client Approval Gate',
    'High',
    tokens.seriousText,
    tokens.seriousBg,
    ['Approval gate']
  ],
  [
    'item-4.1',
    '4.1',
    'Timeline Risk',
    'High',
    tokens.seriousText,
    tokens.seriousBg,
    ['Risk related']
  ]
]

test('three list cards, each card has a level 3 heading', async () => {
  await mount()

  const headings = screen.getAllByRole('heading')
  expect(headings.map((heading) => heading.props['aria-level'])).toEqual([3, 3, 3])
  expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Upcoming milestones & gates' })).toBeOnTheScreen()
  expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Overdue' })).toBeOnTheScreen()
  expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'High & critical risk items' })).toBeOnTheScreen()
})

test('each list card is a flush card: the card body has no padding, each row has its own horizontal padding', async () => {
  await mount()

  const bodies = [
    screen.getByText('None due from today. 3 milestones and 2 gates are overdue (see Overdue).')
      .parent?.parent?.parent,
    screen.getByTestId('overdue-row-item-1.1.1').parent,
    screen.getByTestId('risk-row-item-6.1').parent
  ]
  for (const body of bodies) {
    expect(body).not.toHaveStyle({ padding: tokens.gap })
    expect(body?.parent).toHaveStyle({ borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.line })
  }
  expect(screen.getByTestId('overdue-row-item-1.1.1')).toHaveStyle({
    paddingHorizontal: tokens.gap
  })
})

test('Meridian has no upcoming items: the View in WBS button, the sentence saying why it is empty in the last row, no rows', async () => {
  await mount()

  const action = screen.getByTestId('upcoming-view-in-wbs')
  expect(action).toHaveProp('role', 'link')
  expect(action).toHaveProp('href', `${PROJECT}/wbs`)
  expect(within(action).getByText('View in WBS')).toHaveStyle({ color: tokens.muted })
  const empty = screen.getByText(
    'None due from today. 3 milestones and 2 gates are overdue (see Overdue).'
  )
  expect(empty).toHaveStyle({ fontSize: tokens.fsSmall, color: tokens.muted })
  // The sentence is text, not a link, and is the last row of the card.
  expect(empty.parent?.parent).toHaveStyle({ borderBottomWidth: 0 })
  expect(empty.parent?.parent?.props.role).toBeUndefined()
  expect(screen.queryByTestId('upcoming-more')).toBeNull()
  expect(screen.queryByTestId(/^upcoming-row-/)).toBeNull()
})

test('Overdue card: count chip in the critical color, four rows then the row that opens Focus as the last row', async () => {
  await mount()

  const count = screen.getByText('9')
  expect(count).toHaveStyle({ color: tokens.criticalText })
  expect(count.parent).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: tokens.criticalBg })

  const more = screen.getByTestId('overdue-more')
  expect(rows[0]?.parent?.children).toEqual([...rows, more])
  // Only the last row of the card has no bottom border: here that is the "more" row, so the four rows above still have a border.
  rows.forEach((row) => expect(row).toHaveStyle({ borderBottomWidth: 1 }))

test('risk card: count chip in the serious color, four rows with no "more" row, last row without a bottom border', async () => {

test('Showroom: two upcoming items with a gray date, last row without a bottom border; empty overdue and risks have a sentence saying why', async () => {
  await mount(showroom)

  const first = screen.getByTestId('upcoming-row-item-1.1')
  const second = screen.getByTestId('upcoming-row-item-2.1')
  expect(first.parent?.children).toEqual([first, second])

    fontSize: tokens.fsSmall,

  })

    borderBottomWidth: 0

  expect(screen.getByText('No high or critical risks.').parent?.parent).toHaveStyle({

  expect(screen.queryByTestId(/^risk-row-/)).toBeNull()
```

`src/screens/24-project-overview/states/StateView.tsx`:

```tsx
import { View } from 'react-native'

import { Button } from '../../../design-system/Button'
import { Dialog } from '../../../design-system/Dialog'
import { Spinner } from '../../../design-system/Spinner'
import { StatePanel } from '../../../design-system/StatePanel'
import { Tag } from '../../../design-system/Tag'
import { Text } from '../../../design-system/Text'
import type { problemOf } from '../model'
import { styles } from './StateView.styles'

type Problem = ReturnType<typeof problemOf>

// The three kinds of action of the model: a link back to My focus, retry, and an action with no target yet (text with the label
// "Not built yet", cannot be pressed, D-B15).
function ActionView({
  action,
  onRetry
}: {
  action: Problem['actions'][number]
  onRetry: () => void
}) {
  if (action.kind === 'link') {
    return (
      <Button variant="secondary" label={action.label} href={action.route} testID="state-back" />
    )
  }
  if (action.kind === 'retry') {
    return (
      <Button variant="secondary" label={action.label} onPress={onRetry} testID="state-retry" />
    )
  }
  return (
    <View style={styles.notBuilt}>
      <Text variant="control">{action.label}</Text>
      <Tag variant="label">{action.note}</Tag>
    </View>
  )
}

// The states of the screen (spec 4.5, D-B15). problem is null while loading; otherwise it is the result of
// problemOf. An expired session is a dialog, every other error is a state panel.
export function StateView({
  problem,
  loading,
  onRetry
}: {
  problem: Problem | null
  loading: string
  onRetry: () => void
}) {
  if (problem === null) {
    return (
      <View testID="state-loading" style={styles.loading}>
        <Spinner label={loading} />
        <Text variant="small" tone="muted">
          {loading}
        </Text>
      </View>
    )
  }
  const testID = `state-${problem.kind}`
  const actions = problem.actions.map((action) => (
    <ActionView key={action.kind} action={action} onRetry={onRetry} />
  ))
  if (problem.kind === 'sessionExpired') {
    return (
      <View style={styles.stage}>
        <Dialog title={problem.title} testID={testID}>
          <Text variant="small">{problem.body}</Text>
          <View style={styles.actions}>{actions}</View>
        </Dialog>
      </View>
    )
  }
  // glyph is an optional prop that does not accept undefined (exactOptionalPropertyTypes), so there are two separate branches.
  return problem.kind === 'noAccess' ? (
    <StatePanel
      glyph="lock"
      title={problem.title}
      body={problem.body}
      actions={actions}
      testID={testID}
    />
  ) : (
    <StatePanel title={problem.title} body={problem.body} actions={actions} testID={testID} />
  )
}
```

`src/screens/24-project-overview/states/StateView.styles.ts`:

```ts
import { StyleSheet } from 'react-native'

import { tokens } from '../../../design-system/tokens'

export const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  // Loading state (D-B15): a centered column, pagePad padding like the other pages of the shell.
  loading: { alignItems: 'center', gap: tokens.space8, padding: tokens.pagePad },
  // Action not built yet (D-B15): text with a label, cannot be pressed; the same pattern as Share in the project header.
  notBuilt: { flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: tokens.space5 },
  // Action row inside the dialog: buttons wrap when space runs out (StatePanel has its own row).
  actions: { flexDirection: 'row', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: tokens.space8 },
  // The overlay of Dialog covers the frame that holds it, and this frame has nothing in the flow; the token set has no
  // height for it, so the height follows the page width (ratio 2 to 1), not the window size.
  stage: { aspectRatio: 2 }
})
```

```tsx
import { fireEvent, render, screen, within } from '@testing-library/react-native'

import { tokens } from '../../../design-system/tokens'
import { problemOf } from '../model'
import { STRINGS } from '../strings'
import { StateView } from './StateView'

// The padlock 🔒 (U+1F512), written in \u form. Decorative symbols are hidden from screen readers, so the text search
// has to reach them.
const LOCK = '\u{1F512}'
const HIDDEN = { includeHiddenElements: true }
const LOADING = 'Loading the project overview.'

const FORBIDDEN: ApiError = { kind: 'forbidden' }
const NOT_FOUND: ApiError = { kind: 'notFound' }
const SERVER: ApiError = { kind: 'server', status: 500 }
const EXPIRED: ApiError = { kind: 'unauthenticated' }
const INVALID: ApiError = {
  kind: 'invalid',
  issues: [{ path: 'metrics.blocked', message: 'Required' }]
}

// Build inside each test, not at the top of the file (code that runs while the file loads is a Stryker static mutant).
const view = (error: ApiError, onRetry: () => void = jest.fn()) => (
  <StateView problem={problemOf(error, STRINGS.en)} loading={LOADING} onRetry={onRetry} />
)

test('loading: a centered column, the spinner with a label then a small gray sentence, no state panel', async () => {
  await render(<StateView problem={null} loading={LOADING} onRetry={jest.fn()} />)

  const loading = screen.getByTestId('state-loading')
  expect(loading).toHaveStyle({
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: tokens.space8,
    padding: tokens.pagePad
  })
  const [spinner, sentence] = loading.children
  expect(spinner).toBe(within(loading).getByLabelText(LOADING))
  expect(sentence).toBe(within(loading).getByText(LOADING))
  expect(sentence).toHaveStyle({ fontSize: tokens.fsSmall, color: tokens.muted })
  expect(loading.children).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(screen.queryByTestId('state-noAccess')).toBeNull()
})

test('403: the no-access panel, the lock symbol, the explanatory sentence, Request access not built yet then the button back to My focus', async () => {
  await render(view(FORBIDDEN))

  const panel = screen.getByTestId('state-noAccess')
  expect(
    within(panel).getByRole('heading', { name: "You don't have access to this project" })
  ).toHaveProp('aria-level', 1)
  expect(within(panel).getByText(LOCK, HIDDEN)).toHaveStyle({ color: tokens.muted })
  expect(
    within(panel).getByText(

    )

  expect(request.parent).toHaveStyle({

  expect(within(request.parent!).getByText('Not built yet')).toHaveStyle({

  })
  expect(screen.queryByRole('button')).toBeNull()
  expect(screen.getAllByRole('link')).toHaveLength(1)
  // Actions in the order of the model: Request access then Back to My focus.

  expect(back).toHaveStyle({ backgroundColor: tokens.surface, borderColor: tokens.lineStrong })
  expect(back.parent?.children).toEqual([request.parent, back])
})

describe('links', () => {
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 14): the line that asserts the level of the heading of the no-access
panel changed from `aria-level` 2 to 1, following `StatePanel` (Task 6). This file is not in the
coordinator's fix list: it pins the old level, so `gate:unit` would go red if it were not changed.

Seven places differ from the table in the steps above, which the review accepted. One: there is no `blocks/ListCards.styles.ts`,
because `ListCards` returns only three `Card flush` and the rows come from the design system, so there is nothing to put a style on.
Two: the expired-session dialog is found with `getByLabelText('Your session expired')` and then asserts that `role` is
`'dialog'`, not with `getByRole('dialog', ...)` (the reason is in the note after the test table of Task 6,
Step 3). Three: `Banner` accepts only text, so `testID="health-warning"` sits on a `View` that wraps it. Four:
the 401 dialog sits inside a frame `aspectRatio: 2` (1208 x 604 at 1440 px): `overview` has no height
in the `ScrollView` of the shell (the container of the scrolling content of react-native-web does not stretch by itself
[Source: `node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/ScrollView/index.js:568-573`, `606-640`]) and no token
is a height, so the overlay covers only this frame, the part below is white, and the sidebar and top bar can still be
pressed; the product owner will see this. Five: the scope selector is checked with `toBeSelected()` of RNTL, because
`Pressable` merges `aria-selected` into `accessibilityState` so `toHaveProp('aria-selected', true)` reads
`undefined` (measured in Task 12); `aria-pressed` of the Table view button can be read with `toHaveProp`.
Six: the first render
of OVW-01 is checked with a held response (`hold()`), not with the list of renders, because
`await renderRouter(...)` flushes the response of the mock server inside `act` before the test can see
the loading render. Seven: the tests of the screen are split into three files (`Screen.test.native.tsx`,
`Screen.states.test.native.tsx`, `Screen.links.test.native.tsx`) because of the 300-line cap.

`gate:mutation` of this task took 52 minutes 39 seconds (1252 mutants killed, 4 timed out, 0 survived), because the
tests of the screen render almost the whole design system, so they also cover its mutants.

Fix round 1 after the review changed three places of the first submission, and the tables above follow the fixed version. One:
`useOverview` drops the slow answer of an old request (the `current` flag), with a test. Two: the names of the tests
of the screen carry the requirement id, all eight ids. Three: `filtersOf` of Task 4 splits a comma-joined value, because
`expo-router` writes `{ risk: ['high', 'critical'] }` as `risk=high%2Ccritical` [Source:
`node_modules/expo-router/build/link/href.js:80-84`], so pressing the High risk tile writes one comma-joined value
while a hand-typed path has a repeated key; after the fix both forms give the same `risk: high, critical` on the
page not built yet, and the test of Task 14 also splits by comma when comparing filters. Mutation testing on the two
changed files alone (`useOverview.ts`, `routes.ts`): 41 killed, 0 survived, 4 minutes 21 seconds.

```tsx
import { Slot } from 'expo-router'
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

import { useAppFonts } from '../platform/fonts'
import { startMocks } from '../platform/mocks'
import { LocaleProvider } from '../shell/locale'
import { Shell } from '../shell/Shell'

// The mock server starts when this file is loaded, before the first render (spec 3.4); only when
// EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS=1. Every page sits inside the real shell (spec 4.3 rule 1).
const mocks = startMocks()

export default function RootLayout() {
  const fontsReady = useAppFonts()
  const [mocksReady, setMocksReady] = useState(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    mocks.then(() => setMocksReady(true))
  }, [])
  if (!fontsReady || !mocksReady) return null
  return (
    <LocaleProvider>
      <Shell>
        <Slot />
      </Shell>
    </LocaleProvider>
  )
}
```

'./contract'`. Then `e2e/web/contract.ts`:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'

import { parse } from 'yaml'

// The screen contract (spec 6), read at run time from src/screens/<screen id>/contract.yaml.
type Search = Record<string, string | string[]>
type Effect =
  | { kind: 'route'; to: number; search?: Search; searchFrom?: 'drill' }
  | { kind: 'url'; search: Search }
  | { kind: 'panel' }
  | { kind: 'state'; attribute: string; from: string; to: string }
export type Element = {
  id: string
  role: string
  nameKey?: string
  nameFrom?: 'data'
  effect: Effect
}
export type Contract = {
  id: string
  route: string
  shell: string
  requirements: string[]
  title: { key: string }
  elements: Element[]
  states: string[]
}

export const contractOf = (screen: string): Contract =>
  parse(readFileSync(resolve(__dirname, `../../src/screens/${screen}/contract.yaml`), 'utf8'))

// A control with this testId on the page is in the contract: an exact match, or a match with an id that ends with *.
export const declared = (contract: Contract, testId: string): Element | undefined =>
  contract.elements.find((element) =>
    element.id.endsWith('*') ? testId.startsWith(element.id.slice(0, -1)) : element.id === testId
  )
```

`e2e/web/open.ts`:

```ts
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test'

type Options = { locale?: 'en' | 'vi'; width?: number }

// Open an app path with a preset language and width, then wait for the fonts to load. The script that sets
// the language runs before every script of the page (including the script that sets lang in public/index.html) and runs again
// on every load, so it sets only when the key is not there yet: overwriting would make a reload after choosing Vietnamese go back
// to English. There is a try because the test "block localStorage" makes localStorage throw an error on read.
export async function openPage(
  page: Page,
  path: string,
  { locale = 'en', width = 1440 }: Options = {}
): Promise<void> {
  await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 900 })
  await page.addInitScript((value) => {
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('metis.locale') === null) localStorage.setItem('metis.locale', value)
    } catch {
      // The browser blocks localStorage: the page opens in English.
    }
  }, locale)
  await page.goto(path)
  await page.evaluate(async () => {
    await document.fonts.ready
  })
}
```

`e2e/web/shape.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, type Page, test } from '@playwright/test'

import { openPage } from './open'
import { box, px, rgb, style } from './support'

const OVERVIEW = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'
const CONFIGS = [
  { width: 1280, locale: 'en' },
  { width: 1280, locale: 'vi' },
  { width: 1440, locale: 'en' },
  { width: 1440, locale: 'vi' }
] as const

// Boxes have fractional parts: tolerance 0,5 px (spec 7, shape).
const near = (actual: number, expected: number) => expect(actual).toBeCloseTo(expected, 0)

// Sidebar, top bar, project header and page body: position, size and margin match the tokens.
async function frames(page: Page, width: number) {
  const sidebar = page.getByTestId('sidebar')
  const side = await box(sidebar)
  near(side.x, 0)
  near(side.width, px('sidebar-w'))
  expect(await style(sidebar, 'background-color')).toBe(rgb('rail'))
  const top = await box(page.getByTestId('topbar'))
  near(top.x, px('sidebar-w'))
  near(top.y, 0)
  near(top.height, px('topbar-h'))
  near(top.width, width - px('sidebar-w'))
  const header = page.getByTestId('project-header')
  const head = await box(header)
  near(head.x, px('sidebar-w'))
  near(head.y, px('topbar-h'))
  expect(await style(header, 'padding-left')).toBe(`${px('page-pad')}px`)
  const body = page.getByTestId('overview-body')
  for (const edge of ['top', 'left', 'right']) {
    expect(await style(body, `padding-${edge}`)).toBe(`${px('page-pad')}px`)
  }
}

// Eight metric tiles: on the same row, sharing the remaining width evenly, separated by gap.
async function tiles(page: Page, width: number) {
  const rects = await Promise.all((await page.locator('[data-testid^="tile-"]').all()).map(box))
  expect(rects).toHaveLength(8)
  const tileWidth = (width - px('sidebar-w') - 2 * px('page-pad') - 7 * px('gap')) / 8
  rects.forEach((rect, index) => {
    near(rect.y, rects[0]?.y ?? NaN)
    near(rect.width, tileWidth)
    const before = rects[index - 1]
    if (before) near(rect.x, before.x + before.width + px('gap'))
  })
}

// Large text size and the height of list rows.
async function sizes(page: Page) {
  const figure = page.getByTestId('tile-workItems').getByText('12', { exact: true })
  expect(await style(figure, 'font-size')).toBe(`${px('fs-figure')}px`)
  // The level 1 heading is the project name at size fs-project-title (26 per the wireframe), not fs-display (R-B9).
  const title = page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })
  expect(await style(title, 'font-size')).toBe(`${px('fs-project-title')}px`)
  const rows = page.locator('[data-testid^="overdue-row-"], [data-testid^="risk-row-"]')
  const heights = await rows.evaluateAll((els) =>
    els.map((el) => el.getBoundingClientRect().height)
  )
  expect(heights.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
  expect(heights.filter((height) => height < px('row-list'))).toEqual([])
}

// Boxes whose content is wider than the box itself (horizontal scrolling inside the shell).
const overflowing = (page: Page, selectors: string[]) =>
  page.evaluate(
    (list) =>
      [...document.querySelectorAll(list.join(','))]
        .filter((el) => el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth)
        .map((el) => el.getAttribute('data-testid')),
    selectors
  )

// Text that is clipped or overflows: text that wraps keeps scrollWidth equal to clientWidth; numberOfLines makes scrollWidth
// exceed (ellipsis) or scrollHeight exceed (a line cut off). One-line text whose line height equals the font size has
// scrollHeight exceeding by 1 px because of line rounding (measured in Task 12: the dot ● and 12 elements of the header), so
// the tolerance is 1 px; a really clipped line exceeds by more.
const clipped = (page: Page, selectors: string[]) =>
  page.evaluate((list) => {
    const bad: string[] = []
    for (const root of document.querySelectorAll(list.join(','))) {
      for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('[dir="auto"]')) {
        const { scrollWidth: sw, clientWidth: cw, scrollHeight: sh, clientHeight: ch } = el
        if (sw > cw || sh > ch + 1) {
          const name = root.getAttribute('data-testid')
          bad.push(`${name}: "${el.textContent?.trim()}" scroll ${sw}x${sh}, client ${cw}x${ch}`)
        }
      }
    }
    return bad
  }, selectors)

const FRAMES = ['[data-testid="sidebar"]', '[data-testid="project-header"]']
const TEXT_ROOTS = [...FRAMES, '[data-testid="overview-heading"]', '[data-testid^="tile-"]']

for (const { width, locale } of CONFIGS) {
  test(`shape measured against tokens at ${width} px, language ${locale}`, async ({ page }) => {
    await openPage(page, OVERVIEW, { locale, width })
    await expect(page.getByTestId('overview-body')).toBeVisible()
    // The fonts of this render (including the Vietnamese face) finish loading before the text is measured.
    await page.evaluate(async () => {
      await document.fonts.ready
    })
    await frames(page, width)
    await tiles(page, width)
    await sizes(page)
    expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth)).toBe(width)
    expect(await overflowing(page, [...FRAMES, '[data-testid^="tile-"]'])).toEqual([])
    expect(await clipped(page, TEXT_ROOTS)).toEqual([])
  })
}
```

`e2e/web/states.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, type Page, test } from '@playwright/test'

import { openPage } from './open'
import { blockingAxe, pageErrors } from './support'

const O = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'
const SHOWROOM = '/w/creative-studio/projects/northwind-showroom-vr/overview'
const NO_ACCESS = '/w/creative-studio/projects/spring-catalogue-renders/overview'
const NO_SUCH = '/w/creative-studio/projects/no-such-project/overview'

// The error reply of the mock server makes both Chromium and WebKit write exactly one console line (measured while writing the plan).
const failed = (status: number, name: string) =>
  `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of ${status} (${name})`

type Row = {
  state: string
  path: string
  seen: (page: Page) => Promise<void>
  // Console errors exactly as in the last column of the table: empty when the state causes no network error.
  console: string[]
}

const ROWS: Row[] = [
  {
    state: 'default',
    path: O,
    seen: async (page) => {
      await expect(page.getByTestId('overview-body')).toBeVisible()
      await expect(page.getByTestId('tile-workItems')).toContainText('12')
    },
    console: []
  },
  {
    state: 'notBaselined and stale',
    path: SHOWROOM,
    seen: async (page) => {
      await expect(page.getByTestId('tile-delayed')).toContainText('Not baselined')
      await expect(page.getByTestId('freshness')).toContainText('Stale')
    },
    console: []
  },
  {
    state: 'loading',
    path: `${O}?mock=loading`,
    seen: (page) => expect(page.getByTestId('state-loading')).toBeVisible(),
    console: []
  },
  {
    state: 'noAccess',
    path: NO_ACCESS,
    seen: (page) => expect(page.getByTestId('state-noAccess')).toBeVisible(),
    console: [failed(403, 'Forbidden')]
  },
  {
    state: 'notFound',
    path: NO_SUCH,
    seen: (page) => expect(page.getByTestId('state-notFound')).toBeVisible(),
    console: [failed(404, 'Not Found')]
```

```ts
import { expect, type Page, test } from '@playwright/test'

import { SCREENS } from '../../src/core/routes'
import { meridian } from '../../src/mocks/fixtures/meridian'
import { activeOf } from '../../src/shell/model'
import { type Contract, contractOf, declared, type Element } from './contract'
import { openPage } from './open'
import { pageErrors } from './support'

const contract: Contract = contractOf('24-project-overview')
const O = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'
// The project the mock user has no access to (the state table of states.spec.ts).
const NO_ACCESS = 'spring-catalogue-renders'
const FORBIDDEN = 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 403 (Forbidden)'
const INTERACTIVE =
  'a[href], button, select, [role="button"], [role="link"], [role="tab"], [tabindex="0"]'

type Effect = Element['effect']
type Filters = Record<string, string[]>

function effectOf(id: string): Effect {
  const element = declared(contract, id)
  if (!element) throw new Error(`${id} is not declared in the contract`)
  return element.effect
}

function routeOf(id: string) {
  const effect = effectOf(id)
  if (effect.kind !== 'route') throw new Error(`${id} is not a route effect`)
  return effect
}

function stateOf(id: string) {
  const effect = effectOf(id)
  if (effect.kind !== 'state') throw new Error(`${id} is not a state effect`)
  return effect
}

const sorted = (search: Record<string, string | string[]>): Filters =>
  Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(search).map(([name, value]) => [name, [value].flat().toSorted()])
  )

// The filters of an address: the decoded query parameters. expo-router writes an array as one value joined
// by commas (risk=high%2Ccritical), while a hand-typed path may repeat the key; both read out the same.
function queryOf(url: URL): Filters {
  const filters: Filters = {}
  for (const [name, value] of url.searchParams) (filters[name] ??= []).push(...value.split(','))
  return sorted(filters)
}

// The data row from which the drill-down filter (searchFrom: drill) of a link is taken, in Meridian.
function drillOf(id: string): Filters {
  const [group = '', key = ''] = id.split('-')
  const rows: Record<string, () => { drill: Filters } | undefined> = {
    status: () => meridian.statusBreakdown.find((candidate) => candidate.status === key),
    category: () => meridian.progressByCategory[Number(key)],
    workload: () => meridian.workload[Number(key)]
  }
  const row = rows[group]?.()
  if (!row) throw new Error(`no data row for ${id}`)
  return row.drill
}

// The filters that the contract promises for a link; null when the contract promises nothing about filters.
function promised(id: string): Filters | null {
  const { search, searchFrom } = routeOf(id)
  if (search) return sorted(search)
  return searchFrom === 'drill' ? sorted(drillOf(id)) : null
}

// The ids of every control in `overview` except `project-header`; a control without a data-testid
// is described by its tag and text, so it never matches an id of the contract.
const controlsOf = (page: Page) =>
  page.getByTestId('overview').evaluate((root, selector) => {
    const header = root.querySelector('[data-testid="project-header"]')
    return [...root.querySelectorAll(selector)]
      .filter((el) => !header?.contains(el))
      .map((el) => el.getAttribute('data-testid') ?? `<${el.localName}> ${el.textContent?.trim()}`)
  }, INTERACTIVE)

const ready = (page: Page, path: string, testId: string) =>
  openPage(page, path).then(() => expect(page.getByTestId(testId)).toBeVisible())

// The ids that must be on the Meridian page: tiles, status segments with a number greater than 0, Category rows, people rows,
// card buttons, overdue rows and risk rows (item ids come from the mock data).
const LINKS = [
  ...[
    'workItems',
    'deliverables',
    'workPackages',
    'milestones',
    'approvalGates',
    'blocked',
    'delayed',
    'highRisk'
  ].map((name) => `tile-${name}`),
  ...['done', 'inProgress', 'waiting', 'notStarted'].map((status) => `status-${status}`),
  ...[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((index) => `category-${index}`),
  ...[0, 1, 2, 3].map((index) => `workload-${index}`),
  'upcoming-view-in-wbs',
  ...meridian.attention.overdue.items.map((item) => `overdue-row-${item.id}`),
  'overdue-more',
  ...meridian.attention.risks.items.map((item) => `risk-row-${item.id}`)
]

test('route: every link of the contract is on the Meridian page, with the right destination and filters', async ({
  page
}) => {
  await ready(page, O, 'overview-body')
  const found = await page
    .getByTestId('overview')
    .evaluate((root) =>
      [...root.querySelectorAll('a[href][data-testid]')]
        .filter((el) => !el.closest('[data-testid="project-header"]'))
        .map((el) => ({ id: el.getAttribute('data-testid') ?? '', href: el.getAttribute('href') }))
    )
  const links = found.filter(({ id }) => declared(contract, id)?.effect.kind === 'route')
  expect(links.map(({ id }) => id).toSorted()).toEqual(LINKS.toSorted())
  for (const { id, href } of links) {
    const url = new URL(href ?? '', page.url())
    const destination = activeOf(url.pathname)
    expect([id, destination && SCREENS[destination]]).toEqual([id, routeOf(id).to])
    const filters = promised(id)
    if (filters) expect([id, queryOf(url)]).toEqual([id, filters])
  }
  // Open one link for each destination screen number: the "not built" page prints the screen number.
  const screens = [...new Set(links.map(({ id }) => routeOf(id).to))].toSorted((a, b) => a - b)
  expect(screens).toEqual([26, 28, 34])
  for (const screen of screens) {
    await ready(page, O, 'overview-body')
    await page.getByTestId(links.find(({ id }) => routeOf(id).to === screen)?.id ?? '').click()
    await expect(page.getByText(`Screen ${screen}`, { exact: true })).toBeVisible()
  }
})

test('url: scope-mine then scope-project write and remove the scope parameter', async ({ page }) => {
  await ready(page, O, 'overview-body')
  const search = (id: string) => {
    const effect = effectOf(id)
    if (effect.kind !== 'url') throw new Error(`${id} is not a url effect`)
    return sorted(effect.search)
  }
  const mine = page.getByTestId('scope-mine')
  await mine.click()
  await expect(mine).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')
  await expect.poll(() => queryOf(new URL(page.url()))).toEqual(search('scope-mine'))
  await expect(page.getByTestId('tile-workItems')).toContainText('12')
  await page.getByTestId('scope-project').click()
  await expect(page.getByTestId('scope-project')).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')
  await expect.poll(() => queryOf(new URL(page.url()))).toEqual(search('scope-project'))
})

test('state: status-table-view changes aria-pressed and shows the table', async ({ page }) => {
  await ready(page, O, 'overview-body')
  const { attribute, from, to } = stateOf('status-table-view')
  const button = page.getByTestId('status-table-view')
  await expect(button).toHaveAttribute(attribute, from)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('status-table')).toHaveCount(0)
  await button.click()
  await expect(button).toHaveAttribute(attribute, to)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('status-table')).toBeVisible()
})

test('state: state-retry makes the root report busy and then the page returns to state-unavailable', async ({ page }) => {
  await ready(page, `${O}?mock=serverError`, 'state-unavailable')
  const { attribute, to } = stateOf('state-retry')
  // The aria-busy value changes within a few milliseconds (the mock server replies at once), so record it with
  // a MutationObserver before the click instead of reading it afterwards.
  const seen = await page.getByTestId('overview').evaluateHandle((root, name) => {
    const values = [root.getAttribute(name)]
    new MutationObserver(() => values.push(root.getAttribute(name))).observe(root, {
      attributes: true,
      attributeFilter: [name]
    })
    return values
  }, attribute)
  await page.getByTestId('state-retry').click()
  await expect.poll(() => seen.jsonValue()).toContain(to)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('state-unavailable')).toBeVisible()
  await expect(page.getByTestId('overview')).toHaveAttribute(attribute, 'false')
})

test('reverse check: every control in the content area is in the contract', async ({ page }) => {
  const pages = [
    [O, 'overview-body'],
    [`${O}?mock=serverError`, 'state-unavailable'],
    [`/w/creative-studio/projects/${NO_ACCESS}/overview`, 'state-noAccess']
  ] as const
  const undeclared: string[] = []
  for (const [path, testId] of pages) {
    await ready(page, path, testId)
    const ids = await controlsOf(page)
    expect(ids.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
    undeclared.push(...ids.filter((id) => !declared(contract, id)).map((id) => `${path}: ${id}`))
  }
  expect(undeclared).toEqual([])
})

test('every link of the shell opens a page that has a heading', async ({ page }) => {
  test.slow()
  const errors = pageErrors(page)
  await ready(page, O, 'overview-body')
  const hrefs = await page.evaluate(() => [
    ...new Set(
      ['sidebar', 'topbar', 'project-header'].flatMap((id) =>
        [...document.querySelectorAll(`[data-testid="${id}"] a[href]`)].map(
          (a) => a.getAttribute('href') ?? ''
        )
      )
    )
  ])
  // Measured: 25 links (sidebar 15, top bar 3, header 7), 23 different addresses.
  expect(hrefs.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)
  for (const href of hrefs) {
    await page.goto(href)
    // Every page has exactly one level 1 heading (the page name), including the state panel of the project without access.
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }), href).toHaveCount(1)
  }
  // Only the project without access causes one network error line (403 from the mock server); otherwise the page is free of errors.
  expect(errors).toEqual([FORBIDDEN])
})

test('keyboard (D-B27): Tab reaches every control and every focus has a focus ring', async ({
  page,
  browserName
}) => {
  test.slow()
  await ready(page, O, 'overview-body')
  const wanted = await controlsOf(page)
  expect(wanted.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
  // Safari's Option+Tab (Alt+Tab in Playwright) goes through every control; plain Tab in WebKit skips
  // links and buttons without a tabindex (measured while writing the plan). In this app react-native-web sets
  // tabindex="0" on every control so both keys go through all 63 stops (measured on 08/10/2026);
  // use Alt+Tab so the test does not depend on that tabindex.
  const key = browserName === 'webkit' ? 'Alt+Tab' : 'Tab'
  const stops: { id: string | null; style: string; width: number }[] = []
  for (let press = 0; press < 150; press++) {
    await page.keyboard.press(key)
    stops.push(
      await page.evaluate(() => {
        const el = document.activeElement ?? document.body
        const { outlineStyle, outlineWidth } = getComputedStyle(el)
        // Focus leaving the page for the body is not a control: the focus ring is not measured.
        const id = el === document.body ? null : (el.getAttribute('data-testid') ?? el.localName)
        return { id, style: outlineStyle, width: Number.parseFloat(outlineWidth) }
      })
    )
  }
  expect(wanted.filter((id) => !stops.some((stop) => stop.id === id))).toEqual([])
  // Each control is hit by Tab over many rounds (150 presses), so each error is listed only once.
  const bare = stops
    .filter((stop) => stop.id && (stop.style === 'none' || !(stop.width > 0)))
    .map((stop) => `${stop.id}: outline ${stop.style} ${stop.width}px`)
  expect([...new Set(bare)]).toEqual([])
})
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 14) in two places. One: the row "every link of the shell opens
a page that has a heading" drops the exception branch for the page without access; every destination has exactly one level 1 heading
(`toHaveCount(1)`), including the state panel of the project without access, thanks to `StatePanel` changing to
`heading={1}` (Task 6); the `import` line of `STRINGS` is dropped because it is no longer used. Two: the two reads of the
address after clicking `scope-mine` and `scope-project` go through `expect.poll`, so that the test does not depend
on whether the address has been updated right after the click. Dropping the exception branch while `StatePanel` is still level 2
makes this row red on both browsers on the page without access (`Expected: 1`, `Received: 0`); changing
`StatePanel` makes it green.

`e2e/web/language.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, type Page, test } from '@playwright/test'

import { meridian } from '../../src/mocks/fixtures/meridian'
import { creativeStudio } from '../../src/mocks/fixtures/shell'
import {
  SAME_IN_VI as SCREEN_SAME_IN_VI,
  STRINGS as SCREEN_STRINGS
} from '../../src/screens/24-project-overview/strings'
import { SAME_IN_VI as SHELL_SAME_IN_VI, STRINGS as SHELL_STRINGS } from '../../src/shell/strings'
import { openPage } from './open'
import { blockingAxe, pageErrors } from './support'

const O = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'

type Tree = { readonly [key: string]: string | Tree }
const SLOT = /\{\w+\}/g

// Every leaf string of a dictionary, with a dotted key as in SAME_IN_VI.
const leaves = (tree: Tree, prefix = ''): [string, string][] =>
  Object.entries(tree).flatMap(([key, value]): [string, string][] =>
    typeof value === 'string' ? [[prefix + key, value]] : leaves(value, `${prefix}${key}.`)
  )

// Every string in a data object (user content such as Category names shown as they are).
const stringsIn = (value: unknown): string[] =>
  typeof value === 'string'
    ? [value]
    : value && typeof value === 'object'
      ? Object.values(value).flatMap(stringsIn)
      : []

const USER_CONTENT = new Set([...stringsIn(meridian), ...stringsIn(creativeStudio)])
const escape = (text: string) => text.replaceAll(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, String.raw`\$&`)
const letters = (text: string) => text.replaceAll(SLOT, '').match(/\p{L}/gu)?.length ?? 0

// The English strings of a dictionary that the Vietnamese version must change: drop the keys that keep the text, strings under 3
// letters, strings equal to user content; turned into an expression anchored at both ends, each {name} being .+.
const leftovers = (source: Tree, same: readonly string[]) =>
  leaves(source)
    .filter(([key, text]) => !same.includes(key) && letters(text) >= 3 && !USER_CONTENT.has(text))
    .map(([, text]) => new RegExp(`^${text.split(SLOT).map(escape).join('.+')}$`))

const ENGLISH = [
  ...leftovers(SHELL_STRINGS.en, SHELL_SAME_IN_VI),
  ...leftovers(SCREEN_STRINGS.en, SCREEN_SAME_IN_VI)
]

// Text on the page: the trimmed textContent of each [dir="auto"] element. react-native-web renders
// each root Text as a div dir="auto" and a nested Text as a span, so nested text reads as one string.
const textsOf = (page: Page) =>
  page.evaluate(() =>
    [...document.querySelectorAll('[dir="auto"]')]
      .map((el) => el.textContent?.trim() ?? '')
      .filter((text) => text !== '')
  )

const english = async (page: Page) =>
  (await textsOf(page)).filter((text) => ENGLISH.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text)))

// Text shown on the page (of the shell or of the screen): the first element that has exactly that text.
const shows = (page: Page, text: string) =>
  expect(page.getByText(text, { exact: true }).first()).toBeVisible()
const html = (page: Page) => expect(page.locator('html'))

test('choose Vietnamese: lang vi, no English text of the dictionary left, axe clean', async ({
  page
}) => {
  await openPage(page, O)
  await shows(page, 'Overview')
  // Positive control: on the English page, the list of leftover strings must catch English text.
  expect(await english(page)).toContain('Overview')
  await page.getByLabel('Language').selectOption('vi')
  await html(page).toHaveAttribute('lang', 'vi')
  await shows(page, 'Tong quan')
  expect(await english(page)).toEqual([])
  expect(await blockingAxe(page)).toEqual([])
})

test('the choice stays after a reload; choosing English again switches back', async ({ page }) => {
  await openPage(page, O)
  await page.getByLabel('Language').selectOption('vi')
  await shows(page, 'Tong quan')
  await page.reload()
  await html(page).toHaveAttribute('lang', 'vi')
  await shows(page, 'Tong quan')
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Ngon ngu')).toHaveValue('vi')
  await page.getByLabel('Ngon ngu').selectOption('en')
  await shows(page, 'Overview')
  await html(page).toHaveAttribute('lang', 'en')
})

test('the browser blocks localStorage: opens in English, choosing Vietnamese still changes the text within the session', async ({
  page
}) => {
  const errors = pageErrors(page)
  // Block exactly the key of the app (getItem and setItem throw SecurityError as a browser that blocks storage does), do not
  // block the whole window.localStorage: the mock server of the e2e build (MSW) reads localStorage right when the
  // module loads, so if the whole object throws it dies before the app runs (measured: pageerror
  // "localStorage is blocked", nothing drawn). The release build has no MSW. The app's handling path is the
  // same: both calls sit inside the try of readLocale, writeLocale and the script of index.html.
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const { getItem, setItem } = Storage.prototype
    const denied = (key: string) => {
      if (key === 'metis.locale') throw new DOMException('storage is blocked', 'SecurityError')
    }
    Storage.prototype.getItem = function (key) {
      denied(key)
      return getItem.call(this, key)
    }
    Storage.prototype.setItem = function (key, value) {
      denied(key)
      setItem.call(this, key, value)
    }
  })
  await openPage(page, O)
  await shows(page, 'Overview')
  await html(page).toHaveAttribute('lang', 'en')
  await page.getByLabel('Language').selectOption('vi')
  await shows(page, 'Tong quan')
  await html(page).toHaveAttribute('lang', 'vi')
  expect(errors).toEqual([])
})
```

`e2e/web/brand.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'

import { expect, type Page, test } from '@playwright/test'

import { openPage } from './open'
import { box, px, style, token } from './support'

const O = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'

// The font faces that finished loading: family (quotes removed) and the unicode-range of the @font-face. WebKit writes the hex digits
// of unicode-range in lower case (U+1ea0-1ef9), Chromium in upper case, so convert to upper case.
const loadedFaces = (page: Page) =>
  page.evaluate(() =>
    Array.from(document.fonts)
      .filter((face) => face.status === 'loaded')
      .map((face) => ({
        family: face.family.replaceAll('"', ''),
        range: face.unicodeRange.toUpperCase()
      }))
  )

// The loaded vietnamese face of a font family: the unicode-range of the @font-face has U+1EA0-1EF9.
const vietnameseOf = async (page: Page, family: string) =>
  (await loadedFaces(page)).filter(
    (face) => face.family === family && face.range.includes('U+1EA0-1EF9')
  )

// The first font family of a font-family list, quotes removed.
const firstFamily = (list: string) => (list.split(',')[0] ?? '').trim().replaceAll(/["']/g, '')

test('three fonts loaded, Vietnamese loads the extra vietnamese face, font-family matches the token', async ({
  page
}) => {
  await openPage(page, O)
  await expect(page.getByTestId('overview-body')).toBeVisible()
  const families = async () => (await loadedFaces(page)).map((face) => face.family)
  await expect.poll(families).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['Inter', 'Newsreader', 'Manrope']))
  const heading = page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })
  expect(firstFamily(await style(heading, 'font-family'))).toBe(firstFamily(token('font-display')))
  // The freshness line has a ● mark (system font) in front of the text; measure the text, not the mark.
  const fresh = page.getByTestId('freshness').getByText(/metrics v\d/)
  expect(firstFamily(await style(fresh, 'font-family'))).toBe(firstFamily(token('font-ui')))
  const create = page.getByTestId('topbar-new').locator('[dir="auto"]').first()
  expect(firstFamily(await style(create, 'font-family'))).toBe(firstFamily(token('font-control')))
  // The vietnamese face of Inter is already loaded on the English page (measured), so by itself it does not
  // tell the two languages apart. The vietnamese face of Manrope (the text of buttons, tabs, sidebar items) loads only when
  // the page has Vietnamese text: absent before choosing Vietnamese, present after choosing it.
  expect(await vietnameseOf(page, 'Manrope')).toEqual([])
  await page.getByLabel('Language').selectOption('vi')
  await expect.poll(() => vietnameseOf(page, 'Inter')).toHaveLength(1)
  await expect.poll(() => vietnameseOf(page, 'Manrope')).toHaveLength(1)
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Tong quan', level: 2 })).toBeVisible()
})

test('logo drawn from the original SVG, favicon can be loaded', async ({ page }) => {
  await openPage(page, O)
  const logo = page.getByTestId('logo')
  const rect = await box(logo)
  expect(rect.height).toBeCloseTo(px('logo-h'), 2)
  // Width follows the viewBox ratio 248,65 x 87 of the original file (measured while writing the plan).
  expect(rect.width).toBeCloseTo(68.578125, 2)
  const source = readFileSync(
    resolve(__dirname, '../../../../brand/logo/metis-wordmark.svg'),
    'utf8'
  )
  const original = [...source.matchAll(/<path d="([^"]+)"/g)].map((match) => match[1])
  const drawn = await logo
    .locator('path')
    .evaluateAll((els) => els.map((el) => el.getAttribute('d')))
  expect(drawn).toHaveLength(6)
  expect(drawn).toEqual(original)
  await expect(page.locator('link[rel="icon"]')).toHaveAttribute('href', '/favicon.ico')
  const favicon = await page.request.get('/favicon.ico')
  expect(favicon.status()).toBe(200)
  expect(favicon.headers()['content-type']).toBe('image/x-icon')
})
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 14): the language check of the fonts now tells the two
languages apart. The first version only waited for the `vietnamese` face of Inter after choosing Vietnamese, but that face is already loaded
on the English page (measured on both browsers), so the test was green even when nothing was chosen. The new version adds
the function `vietnameseOf` and checks the `vietnamese` face of Manrope (the text of buttons, tabs, sidebar items), a face that only
loads when the page has Vietnamese text: absent before choosing, present after choosing. Dropping the line `selectOption('vi')`
or moving the "absent" line to after the choice makes the test red on both browsers.

Four places differ from the tables in the steps above, which the review accepted. One: the rule that text is not clipped allows a deviation of
1 px in height (`scrollHeight` not greater than `clientHeight + 1`): one-line text whose line height equals
the font size exceeds by 1 px because of line rounding (measured in Task 12: the ● mark of freshness and 12 elements of the header), while
a really clipped line exceeds by more; the width is still compared strictly (`scrollWidth` not greater than
`clientWidth`). Two: the multi-value filter is compared after splitting at commas (`queryOf` splits each
value), because `expo-router` writes `risk=high%2Ccritical` and not a repeated key (Task 12, fix round 1).
Three: the row "the browser blocks localStorage" throws `SecurityError` from `Storage.prototype` only for the key
`metis.locale`, not from `window.localStorage`: the MSW mock server of the e2e build reads `localStorage`
right when the module loads, so if the whole object throws it dies before the app runs. The app's handling path is the
same (every call sits inside the `try` of `readLocale`, `writeLocale` and the script of
`index.html`), and dropping the `try` of `readLocale` makes the test red. Four: plain `Tab` in WebKit also goes
through all 63 stops in this app (react-native-web sets `tabindex="0"` on every control, measured on
08/10/2026); the test still uses `Alt+Tab` for WebKit as the plan says so as not to depend on that
`tabindex`.

Fix round 1 after the review changed three places of the first submission, and the tables above already follow the fixed version. One:
the error page has a level 1 heading (`StatePanel` becomes `heading={1}`, Task 6), so the row "every link of the
shell opens a page that has a heading" drops the exception and demands exactly one `h1` on all 23 destinations. Two: the font test tells
the two languages apart by the `vietnamese` face of Manrope. Three: the reads of the address after clicking the scope go
through `expect.poll`. The review also accepted two replacements for the table: the shell links row (that exception was
dropped in One) and the localStorage blocking row (kept, as in Three above). The `gate:web` gate measured 41,16 and 43,08 seconds
on two runs, under the 90 seconds of R-B10, so it stays in `pnpm verify` and the browser install step of CI
stands before it; that step could not run until the first push to GitHub.

- [ ] **Step 1: Scene lifecycle plugin for iOS 27, package id**

`plugins/with-ios-scene-lifecycle.js` (the version from the native trial of 05/10, comments translated into Vietnamese, formatted by Prettier; the iOS 27 SDK
does not open an app that does not use the scene lifecycle, and the native template of SDK 57 lacks it):

```js
// The iOS 27 SDK does not open an app that does not use the UIKit scene lifecycle: measured on 05/10/2026 in the native
// trial (spec line 71 records the trials of that day). expo 57 ships ExpoAppSceneDelegate but the native
// template of SDK 57 does not use it. This plugin does exactly what the SDK 58 template does: the package
// expo-template-bare-minimum@58.0.12 (ios/HelloWorld/AppDelegate.swift, SceneDelegate.swift and
// Info.plist, read on 08/10/2026). Remove it when moving to SDK 58.
const { IOSConfig, withAppDelegate, withInfoPlist } = require('expo/config-plugins')

const SCENE_DELEGATE = `internal import Expo

@objc(SceneDelegate)
class SceneDelegate: ExpoAppSceneDelegate {}
`

function mustReplace(source, pattern, replacement, what) {
  const result = source.replace(pattern, replacement)
  if (result === source) {
    throw new Error(`with-ios-scene-lifecycle: ${what} not found in AppDelegate.swift`)
  }
  return result
}

module.exports = function withIosSceneLifecycle(config) {
  config = withAppDelegate(config, (c) => {
    let source = c.modResults.contents
    if (source.includes('ExpoReactNativeFactoryProvider')) return c
    source = mustReplace(
      source,
      'class AppDelegate: ExpoAppDelegate {',
      'class AppDelegate: ExpoAppDelegate, ExpoReactNativeFactoryProvider {',
      'class declaration'
    )
    // SceneDelegate creates the window and starts React Native.
    source = mustReplace(
      source,
      /#if os\(iOS\) \|\| os\(tvOS\)\n\s*window = UIWindow\(frame: UIScreen\.main\.bounds\)[\s\S]*?#endif\n/,
      '',
      'window and startReactNative block'
    )
    c.modResults.contents = source
    return c
  })
  config = withInfoPlist(config, (c) => {
    c.modResults.UIApplicationSceneManifest = {
      UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes: false,
      UISceneConfigurations: {
        UIWindowSceneSessionRoleApplication: [
          {
            UISceneConfigurationName: 'Default Configuration',
            UISceneDelegateClassName: '$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).SceneDelegate'
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    return c
  })
  return IOSConfig.XcodeProjectFile.withBuildSourceFile(config, {
    filePath: 'SceneDelegate.swift',
    contents: SCENE_DELEGATE,
    overwrite: true
  })
}
```

This version differs from the first draft (fix round 1 of Task 15): the comment at the top of the file has the date of the measurement and the source. The iOS
27 SDK does not open an app that does not use the scene lifecycle (measured on 05/10/2026 in the native trial); the plugin does exactly
what the SDK 58 template does, checked against the package `expo-template-bare-minimum@58.0.12`
(`AppDelegate.swift`, `SceneDelegate.swift`, `Info.plist`, read on 08/10/2026). The plugin runs at
`expo prebuild`, outside the `src` area that Jest and Stryker cover (the `roots` of Jest is `src`,
`gate:tooling` scans only `eslint-rules` and `scripts`), so it has no test of its own; the evidence is that the real
iOS build runs. It is only temporary, until moving to SDK 58.

- [ ] **Step 2: Two pictures at 1440 px**

`reports/review/shots.mjs` (captures the whole scrolling area: the window is stretched to the height of `page`, because the shell keeps
the sidebar and the top bar still, D-B22):

```js
// Once, from apps/metis, after pnpm build:web:e2e: capture screen 24 of Meridian in two languages at
// 1440 px (the whole page) into reports/review/. Not added to the repo.
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'

import { chromium } from '@playwright/test'

const PORT = 5394
const OVERVIEW = '/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview'
const browser = await chromium.launch()
const server = spawn('node', ['scripts/serve-web.mjs', 'dist-e2e', String(PORT)], {
  stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'inherit']
})
try {
  // Wait for the line "serve-web: ..." from this very server; if the port is busy it exits and the script stops here.
  await new Promise((ready, fail) => {
    server.stdout.once('data', ready)
    server.once('exit', (code) => fail(new Error(`serve-web exited with code ${code}`)))
  })
  mkdirSync('reports/review', { recursive: true })
  for (const locale of ['en', 'vi']) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
    await page.addInitScript((value) => localStorage.setItem('metis.locale', value), locale)
    await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}${OVERVIEW}`)
    await page.getByTestId('overview').waitFor()
    await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready)
    // The page scrolls inside the "page" area of the shell, not the whole document: stretch the window to fit the content.
    const height = await page
      .getByTestId('page')
      .evaluate((el) => el.getBoundingClientRect().top + el.scrollHeight)
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height: Math.ceil(height) })
    const file = `reports/review/24-overview-${locale}-1440.png`
    await page.screenshot({ path: file, fullPage: true })
    console.log(`${file} lang=${await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang)}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} finally {
  await browser.close()
  server.kill()
}
```

```bash
pnpm build:web:e2e < /dev/null
node reports/review/shots.mjs
file reports/review/24-overview-en-1440.png reports/review/24-overview-vi-1440.png
lsof -t -iTCP:5394 -sTCP:LISTEN
```

Expected: the two lines `reports/review/24-overview-en-1440.png lang=en` and `reports/review/24-overview-vi-1440.png
lang=vi`; `file` prints `PNG image data, 1440 x` for both; `lsof` prints nothing (the static server of the script has
stopped). If port 5394 is busy the script stops with `serve-web exited with code 1` and leaves no process
behind (measured while writing the plan).

## As-built notes for spec 3.5

For the product owner to copy into the spec when reviewing; the plan does not edit the spec.

- The second call: `GET {apiBase}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/shell` returns
  `{ user: { name, initials }, tenant: { name }, workspace: { id, name }, workspaces: { id, name }[],
  nav: { home, portfolio, workspace }, tree, notifications }`; each item of `nav` is
  `{ code, badge: { count, alert } | null, planned: 'V2' | 'V3' | null }`, `code` belongs to the 15 codes of
  `NAV_CODES`; `tree` is portfolio, program, project (`{ id, name }`) (`src/core/api/shell.ts`).
- The overview screen additionally sends `?scope=mine` when "My items" is chosen; for the whole project it does not send `scope`
  (`src/core/api/client.ts`).
- Errors become names that the screen knows how to draw: 401 `unauthenticated` (session expired), 403 `forbidden`, 404 `notFound`,
  another code outside 2xx `server` with the code, a body that is not JSON or has the wrong shape `invalid` with the path of
  the field (for example `metrics.blocked`), a network error `network`, beyond `timeoutMs` (10 000 ms, `src/platform/config.ts`)
  `timeout`; an empty id, `.`, `..` is `notFound` without calling the network.

## The real run (06 to 08/10/2026)

The plan ran straight on `main` (FE-19), without stopping between the plan and the execution to wait for the product owner to review
(FE-21), one agent doing each task and another agent reviewing. Ten of the sixteen tasks had exactly one fix round after the
review (Task 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15); Task 1, 4, 5, 8, 13 were clean the first time; Task 16 only
wrote into the folder `reports/` that git ignores, so it had no review of its own. After Task 16 there was one review
of the whole branch (opus): 0 serious defects, one important cross-task defect (the workspace select menu was drawn under the
rows of the sidebar, clicking a workspace did nothing), then a final fix batch with one narrow re-review, and
one more full `pnpm verify` on the delivery tree itself. No `git add`, `git commit` or `git push` command
was run; the list of changed files is handed to the product owner.

Every whole-file code block of this plan was compared with the final code by `cmp`: 201 blocks identical byte for byte (189
of the 194 blocks with a path-style heading that the extractor `extract-plan.py` recognizes, plus 12 blocks with other headings:
the plugin, `app.json`, `stryker.config.json` and the Maestro flow of Task 15, `_layout.tsx` and the route of Task 13,
the contract reader of Task 14, `locale.tsx` of Task 11 and three pieces of `eslint.config.js`; the Maestro
flow alone was compared with the file of lane (e), because the folder `reports/` is not in the snapshot). The remaining ten blocks are an
intermediate step that a later task replaces entirely: the skeleton `NotBuilt.tsx` and `NotBuilt.test.native.tsx` with
`_layout.tsx` of Task 8 (Task 11 and 13 replace them), the two blocks `knip.jsonc` and `stryker.config.json` of Task 2
(Task 15 replaces them; the extractor wrongly assigned the second block to `public/index.html`), the trial file `src/shell/model.ts` of
Task 10 Step 3 (deleted at once), and the draft of the hook with the hook test in Task 11 Step 2 and Task 12 Step 1
(the block that was run is in the section "Real code after the review" at the end of each task).

Two Macs. The first machine (06/10) wrote the plan, scanned before running (16 findings, all fixed in the
plan) and ran Task 1 to 4 on the main tree. The second machine (07 to 08/10; 11 cores, 18 GB) ran Task 5 to
16. On that machine `node_modules` in the iCloud folder could not be used (593 conflicting copies; the command to delete it was held
back by iCloud for more than ten minutes), so the rest ran in a copy outside iCloud, `~/metis-run/lanes/main`, and
the reviewed code was merged back into the main tree with `merge.mjs` after Task 10, 11, 13 and 15. The main tree holds the reviewed
code of Task 1 to 15; the final fix batch still has to be merged into it at delivery, together with one `pnpm install
--frozen-lockfile` (the main tree has no `node_modules` yet).

A lane is an APFS copy of the repo for one task to run on its own; a snapshot (`snaps/`) is a read-only copy
of the code tree at one moment, used for the review and for copying the real code into the plan. The lanes that ran:

Machine limits. The product owner reported (07/10, 22:53) that Activity Monitor showed eight or more Node processes and the
memory nearly overloaded with only four agents. Measured: those Node processes are the testing tools, not agents (the agents
sit in one Claude Code process, 354 MB): each Stryker run opens 10 child processes of 280 to 530 MB
(about 3,8 GB), Jest by default also opens 10; the largest is the `fileproviderd` of iCloud, 3,9 GB, while the command to
delete `node_modules` was still held; swap used 11,5 of 12 GB. Two measures. One: every Node process of the run
sees only 4 cores (a preload file `~/metis-run/bin/cap-cpus.cjs` through `NODE_OPTIONS`: Jest is left with 3 child
processes, Stryker 4); raised to 6 at 02:37 when three lanes had been merged, lowered back to 4 at 05:15 when five child processes
of Stryker held nearly 2 GB each (1841 to 2116 MB). Two: `heavy.sh`, a machine-wide lock for the heavy test
suites (`pnpm verify`, `gate:unit`, `gate:mutation`, web export, native build), one at a time.
Price: each mutation testing run is about twice as slow, and the lanes queue for the lock for a few minutes. One mutation
testing run on the merged tree was stopped at 500 of 1269 mutants (0 surviving, 4 timed out); the final result comes from the full
run of Task 16.

What the real run added compared with the original plan, each one measured by a review: filtering `.DS_Store` in
the two tests of Task 2 and the OFL license next to the web fonts; a static server that survives a mistyped address and a stricter
release detector (Task 3); the error kind `stale` of `auditDictionaries` (Task 9; plan A); `rowsOf`
keeps the own tone of each list and drops two `as Route` casts (Task 10); the `current` flag in `useShell` and
`useOverview`; `filtersOf` splits comma-joined values; `StatePanel` level 1; the accessible name of the workspace
select button starts with the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3), `key={pathname}` and `zIndex: 1` for its menu,
`role="main"` on the page area of the shell, the phrase `whole` in the dictionary; the trial flow adds `project-header`
with a control flow, and `/ios`, `/android` anchored in the Stryker configuration.

Environment to know: `~/Documents` is synced by iCloud including `.git` and `node_modules`, so do not work
on two machines at the same time, and heavy copies (lanes) stay outside `~/Documents`; Finder or iCloud scatters
`.DS_Store`, which turned two tool tests red (filtered in Task 2); Jest sometimes lost a child process to
`SIGSEGV` of Node 24.15.0 (seen in Task 11, Task 12 and Task 15), never together with a red test, and
running again gives green; `pnpm` prints `Packages: -78` every time it rearranges `node_modules`, the lockfile still matches.

with its reason and the price if wrong:

   24 for review (FE-21). If wrong: the product owner wants to read plan B first; it is already on disk.

   design. If wrong: a few more rounds are spent.

   plan: Task 4 imports each type separately so that Knip does not go red (F1); the boundary zone of the model allows `./strings` (F2);
   Task 11 and then 12 run on the main tree (F3); two type errors of Task 12 (F4); `Meter` takes the integer of the
   model so that 0,29 does not become 28 (F5); Task 1 deletes the trial file before the reverse test (F6); Task 16 quotes verbatim
   the decisions (F7); state colors only through `status.ts` (F8); Task 14 measures both the header and the sidebar
   in Vietnamese (F9); the small omissions F10 to F16. If wrong: a step of the plan deviates from the code, it is exposed
